abstract: Ras proteins regulate signaling pathways initiated by tyrosine kinase receptors, and activating Ras mutations are drivers in cancer and RASophaties. The development of therapies against these diseases requires a profound understanding of how Ras mutations modify pathway output and interact with other pathway components. Here we generated G12V activating mutations in the Drosophila Ras1 locus and used Ras1 G12V and human KRASB G12V to analyze in vivo the consequences of endogenous Ras G12V expression and its interplay with other components of the EGFR/MAPK pathway. We find that Ras G12V acts as an amplifier of EGFR stimulation. Consistently, Ras G12V proteins respond to EGFR and can compensate for EGFR loss to generate basal levels of ERK activity. However, full pathway activation by Ras G12V is strictly dependent on EGFR function. Altogether, our results suggest that EGFR not only activates wild type Ras, but also Ras G12V , and support the notion that Ras G12V mutants are non-constitutively active.

abstract: Chagas disease (CD), caused by the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma cruzi , affects an estimated 10.5 million people worldwide and remains a leading cause of infectious cardiomyopathy in Latin America. Although infection is lifelong without treatment, only 20–30% of chronically infected individuals progress from an asymptomatic stage to clinically significant cardiac disease, and current antiparasitic therapies are limited by toxicity and variable efficacy. Reliable biomarkers capable of predicting disease progression would improve clinical risk stratification and support therapeutic development. Here, we performed a metabolomics study to identify serum biomarkers predictive of progression from asymptomatic infection to cardiac CD. Untargeted liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry profiling using complementary chromatographic platforms and univariate statistics, machine learning feature selection, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis were performed to identify candidate biomarkers. These biomarkers were validated by targeted analysis. We identified eight individual metabolite biomarkers and 45 combinatorial panels predictive of progression status, including 10 panels that met sensitivity and specificity criteria defined in the target product profile for CD treatment-response biomarkers. These findings demonstrate that circulating metabolites measured at baseline can predict future cardiac disease progression and provide a foundation for clinically deployable prognostic tools in chronic Chagas disease.

abstract: OSTα/β is the essential basolateral transporter responsible for returning reabsorbed bile acids to the portal circulation, yet its molecular mechanism remains unclear. Here, we report the cryo-electron microscopy structure of human OSTα/β at 2.7 Å resolution, revealing a 7-TM architecture distinct from all established SLC transporter folds. We further determined the taurocholate (TC)-bound structure at 3.2 Å, showing that the substrate laterally binds to a surface groove on OSTα, but not in the central cavity. The TC molecule is captured by a line of conserved polar residues along the groove, which were further proved by structure-guided mutagenesis combined with transport assays. Molecular dynamics simulations also suggest that it is energetically favored for TC moving along the surface groove. Together, structural analysis, functional assays, and simulations demonstrate that OSTα/β mediates bile acid transmembrane translocation via a facilitated lateral diffusion mechanism with subtle conformational change, which is distinct from known SLCs. These findings establish a mechanistic framework for OSTα/β function in enterohepatic bile acid circulation and provide a foundation for therapeutic modulation of bile acid homeostasis.

abstract: Nonsense mutations in tumour suppressor genes (TSGs) drive cancer initiation and progression but remain “undruggable” due to formidable challenges in rescuing the functional impairment of heterogeneous truncated proteins with a single agent. Here we observe that suppressor transfer RNAs (sup-tRNAs) can overcome diverse nonsense mutations in TP53 , restoring full-length p53 expression and function. Sup-tRNAs enable high-fidelity incorporation of optimal amino acids and can further enhance the transcriptional activity of p53 to suppress tumour cell proliferation. Moreover, we employ a computational model to guide sup-tRNA design by in silico saturation mutagenesis for targeted readthrough of different nonsense-mutant TSGs. Remarkably, sup-tRNAs produced p53 variants with enhanced activity relative to restored wild-type p53, reducing cancer cell colony area by up to 82%. In two xenograft models harbouring nonsense mutant TP53 , we observed up to a 74% reduction in tumour volume after lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-based sup-tRNA treatment, attributed to robust recovery of p53 expression and function. Critically, sup-tRNA monotherapy surpassed nab-paclitaxel chemotherapy in efficacy, and their combination induced near-complete tumour regression (a maximum of 93% reduction in tumour volume) without detectable toxicity in multiple mouse tumour models. Our findings highlight the potential of tRNA-based therapy to provide a promising strategy for rescuing nonsense-mutant TP53 .

abstract: Gametogenesis rejuvenates the cellular lineage and excludes senescence-associated factors from gametes. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae , this involves sequestration of nuclear constituents into the Gametogenesis Uninherited Nuclear Compartment (GUNC), which is excluded from gametes. Here we identify the conserved mitochondrial import receptor Tom70 as a key regulator of GUNC-mediated exclusion. Loss of TOM70 disrupts the sequestration of nuclear pore complexes, but not senescence-associated aggregates and nucleolar components, into the GUNC. Tom70’s role appears independent of its canonical function in mitochondrial import and instead reflects a meiosis-specific requirement for mitochondria-nuclear envelope tethering. During meiosis II, Tom70 concentrates around the GUNC, where it recruits the nuclear envelope tethering protein Cnm1. Loss of CNM1 partially phenocopies tom70 ∆, consistent with parallel tethering interactions. These findings uncover a previously unrecognized organelle contact-dependent pathway that remodels the nuclear envelope to support selective nuclear inheritance. More broadly, they highlight how organelle contacts integrate with nuclear quality control to safeguard gamete integrity.

abstract: Radiation-induced bystander effects (RIBEs) compromise radioprotection and radiotherapy by propagating damage to non-irradiated cells; however, the mediators and underlying circuitry remain incompletely defined. Using localised UV irradiation as the primary experimental system and localised X-ray irradiation as a supportive test in an in vivo Caenorhabditis elegans model, we identify tyramine, a trace amine structurally and functionally related to adrenaline/noradrenaline, as a neuron-derived mediator of RIBEs. Tyramine released from tyraminergic RIM neurons activates TYRA-3, a tyramine-responsive adrenergic-like GPCR related to vertebrate adrenergic receptors. This neuron-to-intestine signal promotes secretion of the insulin-like peptide INS-5, aberrantly engages the DAF-2/insulin signalling pathway (IIS), and triggers endoplasmic reticulum stress, DNA damage responses, and embryonic lethality in non-irradiated tissues. These findings reveal a neuro–intestinal–germline axis that orchestrates RIBEs and uncover an unanticipated role for adrenaline-like signalling. Our work provides a conceptual framework for systematically discovering additional RIBE mediators and identifies pathway components for future evaluation as radioprotective or radiotherapy-modifying targets.

abstract: Functional MRI (fMRI) has traditionally focused on grey matter activations, overlooking the contribution of white matter pathways to brain organisation. Yet evidence suggests that white matter constrains, modulates, and integrates signals across distant regions. Here, we introduce a framework to map the functional specialisation of white matter circuits using fMRI scans collected while participants watched naturalistic videos. By leveraging ecologically valid stimuli, this method captures cognition as it naturally unfolds. Integrating fMRI with brain connections, we derived a functionally grounded parcellation of the connectome, challenging conventional cortical-based cognitive taxonomy. Distinct cognitive profiles emerged for association and commissural fibres, with association pathways preferentially linked to language-related processes and commissural pathways to executive and motor functions, affirming the functionally heterogeneous nature of white matter systems. An artificial intelligence framework applied to independent datasets confirmed the robustness and functional relevance of the identified parcels. This open-access framework also enables the interactive exploration of white matter functional organisation, offering a new lens on the neural bases of cognition.

abstract: Metabolic reprogramming plays a critical role in heart failure (HF), but its regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Zinc finger E-box binding homeobox 1 (ZEB1), a transcription factor initially identified as a regulator of epithelial-mesenchymal transition, has recently been implicated in metabolic regulation. Here, we show that ZEB1 expression is reduced in failing cardiomyocytes. Cardiomyocyte-specific deletion of Zeb1 leads to progressive HF with impaired glycolysis and fatty acid metabolism. Mechanistically, ZEB1 interacts with TEA domain transcription factor 1 (TEAD1) to activate metabolic genes, including pyruvate kinase muscle isozyme 1 (PKM1) and acetyl-CoA acyltransferase 2 (ACAA2), which regulate glycolysis and fatty acid β-oxidation, respectively. Loss of Acaa2 aggravates stress-induced cardiac hypertrophy and mitochondrial dysfunction. Acetate supplementation restores cardiac function in Zeb1 -deficient mice, whereas ZEB1 overexpression improves pressure overload- and doxorubicin-induced HF. These findings identify the ZEB1-TEAD1 axis as a regulator of cardiac metabolic homeostasis and a potential therapeutic target for HF.

abstract: How do neurons code information? Recent work emphasizes the geometry and information content of population codes, using measures that are blind to the native tunings (or ‘axes’) of neural responses. But might these representational axes matter, with some privileged systematically over others? We developed methods to test for alignment of neural tuning across brains and deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs). Across both vision and audition, both brains and DCNNs consistently favoured certain axes for representing the natural world. Moreover, the representational axes of DCNNs trained on natural inputs were aligned to those in perceptual cortices, such that axis-sensitive model–brain similarity metrics better differentiated competing models of biological sensory systems. We further show that coding schemes that privilege certain axes can facilitate task performance, reduce downstream wiring costs and improve generalization. These results motivate a new framework for understanding neural tuning in biological and artificial networks and its computational benefits.

abstract: Cell segmentation is a critical yet under-standardized step in spatial transcriptomics, directly affecting cell identity assignment, spatial organization and downstream biological interpretation. Despite rapid advances in spatial transcriptomics technologies, systematic evaluations of segmentation methods across platforms and biological contexts remain limited. Here we benchmark 11 image-based, transcriptomics-based and multimodal segmentation methods across 15 datasets generated by 5 spatial transcriptomics technologies, spanning 12 human and mouse tissue types. We introduce biologically informed evaluation metrics that quantify segmentation quality, transcript recovery, cell composition, morphology, expression purity and spatial organization. Benchmarking reveals substantial variation in performance across datasets, technologies and evaluation criteria, highlighting trade-offs among segmentation completeness, transcriptomic fidelity and biological interpretability. Cross-technology analyses further demonstrate that segmentation choice critically shapes downstream analyses, including cell-type specificity, transcript contamination and ligand–receptor inference. Together, our unified Nextflow pipeline provides a scalable foundation for standardized evaluation of segmentation and method selection in spatial transcriptomics.

abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are present in biofluids and may be useful biomarkers to non-invasively monitor brain cells, but isolating cell type-specific EVs remains challenging. Here we introduce an approach to immuno-isolate EVs from neurons and glia based on protein surface markers. We first selected transmembrane proteins suitable as cell type-specific EV markers based on gene expression and EV proteomic data. We developed a high-purity EV isolation method and cataloged the proteins present on EVs in human cerebrospinal fluid and plasma. We then computationally identified cell type-specific candidate markers for isolating EVs from neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes and microglia. Using ultrasensitive immunoassays against several predicted neuron-specific proteins, we confirmed one marker, NRXN3, as present on EVs in cerebrospinal fluid and plasma. Finally, we developed efficient EV immuno-isolation methods and applied them to isolate NRXN3 + EVs. Our work provides a general methodology for the isolation of cell type-specific EVs, advancing the goal of using EVs to study brain diseases.

abstract: Psychedelics produce long-lasting antidepressant effects, but their hallucinogenic properties limit clinical use. Using structure-guided design of 5-HT 2A R–β-arrestin-biased agonists, we identified β-arrestin signaling as a critical driver of prolonged antidepressant-like effects in mice. Here we show that the slow-dissociation kinetics of lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD) enable progressive accumulation of 5-HT 2A R engagement during repeated low-dose administration, approaching the receptor occupancy achieved by an acute high dose while avoiding its high peak concentration. This kinetic separation sustains β-arrestin signaling while limiting robust Gα q -mediated Ca 2+ responses. Consistent with this framework, repeated low-dose LSD and repeated low-dose psilocybin pretreatment followed by a high-dose psychedelic challenge produced sustained antidepressant-like behavioral effects in mice. In parallel, these regimens produced no detectable psychedelic-associated behavioral disruption in mice and cynomolgus macaques. Together, these findings uncover the signaling basis of sustained psychedelic efficacy and provide a rational framework for developing nonhallucinogenic psychedelic therapies for psychiatric disorders.

title: A computational framework for modeling fluid and solid stressesin porous tissues with application to the trabeculated embryonic heart.

author_details.name: Buffinton CM
author_details.affiliation: Department of Mechanical Engineering, Bucknell University, Lewisburg, Pennsylvania, United States of America.

author_details.name: Baish JW
author_details.affiliation: Department of Biomedical Engineering, Bucknell University, Lewisburg, Pennsylvania, United States of America.

abstract: This study provides a framework for efficient solutions of computational fluid-solid interaction models of porous tissue, with a focus on blood flow through the developing heart wall in the critical chamber and valve formation stages, when trabeculation fills much of the ventricles. This porous, trabeculated tissue is the site of complex mechanotransduction processes, but accurately estimating solid and fluid stresses within such intricate geometries is difficult. We addressed this with three levels of modeling and verification. Images of E12.5 mouse ventricles were first obtained through confocal microscopy and 3D reconstruction. These guided creation of explicit pore-scale finite element simulations with fluid-solid interaction. Idealized and image-derived unit cells were analyzed to determine hydraulic permeability. Next, a multi-pore representation of the ventricular wall was solved with full fluid and solid equations. A continuum model based on Brinkman equations then replaced the explicit pore structure, and sensitivity to permeability was evaluated in terms of fluid flow in the open channel and porous region. Permeabilities obtained from unit cell simulations followed trends from Kozeny-Carman solid-pore and fiber theory for the rigid case, while simulations for hyperelastic unit-cell material quantified the effects of tissue elasticity. Comparison of continuum and explicit model results showed the Brinkman equation, which incorporates the diffusion of shear stress from flow in the free fluid into the porous media, but not explicitly inertial effects, could significantly improve the accuracy of continuum models compared to Darcy's law. A 3D model of blood flow through the ventricles of the developing mouse heart demonstrated the application of the technique to more realistic geometry, showed locations of peak solid and shear stress, and produced physiologically reasonable flow. Furthermore, we developed methodologies to estimate local wall shear and solid stress from continuum-based calculations. This approach can enable efficient, whole-organ parametric analyses of fluid flow, circumventing the need for computationally expensive explicit pore modeling.

abstract: Gene-expression biomarkers for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) are often transported across retrospective cohorts that differ in treatment, assay platform, and clinical annotation. Using REMARK as the reporting framework, we audited prognostic associations with fixed scoring rules. Four Gene Expression Omnibus cohorts were harmonized for survival analysis. Treatment context was assessed after outcome-blind transcriptional state discovery. A directly mapped five-gene historical benchmark was evaluated with continuous Cox models in four R-CHOP cohorts. A 76-gene program selected in GSE31312 and GSE10846 served as a case study of two-cohort discovery, with GSE87371 as the only full-coverage independent evaluation and GSE32918 as a cross-platform sensitivity analysis. Coverage ablation, technical replicates, matched random programs, meta-analysis, and clinical-increment analyses assessed attenuation. The survival analyses included 470, 232, 87, and 140 patients. State composition was strongly associated with CHOP versus R-CHOP context in GSE10846 (Cramer's V = 0.986). The historical score's unadjusted random-effects hazard ratio (HR) was 1.35 (95% confidence interval 1.04-1.75); the prediction interval crossed the null (0.77-2.37). Common age/sex adjustment yielded HR 1.27 (1.05-1.54), with a prediction interval of 0.94-1.72. The 76-gene program was not independently validated in GSE87371 (unadjusted HR 1.23, 0.87-1.75; IPI/COO-adjusted HR 0.88, 0.56-1.40; age/sex-adjusted HR 1.09, 0.76-1.55). Its effect exceeded most matched random programs, but cross-cohort attenuation was pronounced and estimated clinical increment was negligible. With only 32 validation events, modest effects remain compatible with the data. Public DLBCL transcriptomic associations can be cohort-specific despite fixed scoring rules. Independent full-coverage evaluation and transparent treatment and platform audits should precede claims of general prognostic utility.

abstract: Hypotension is a common complication in pregnant mothers during cesarean section after spinal anesthesia. Identifying the association between abdominal circumference and the likelihood of developing hypotension following a cesarean delivery while under spinal anesthesia can facilitate preventing hypotension. This study aims to assess the relationship between the abdominal circumference of pregnant women and the occurrence of hypotension during cesarean section under spinal anesthesia at public hospitals in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, 2024. A prospective observational study through a simple systematic random sampling technique was conducted on 360 pregnant mothers who underwent elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia from January 7, 2024, to March 30, 2024. Data was collected using a data collection questionnaire and checklist. The data was entered using Epi Info 7.2 and exported into SPSS 26. The Patients were categorized by their median abdominal circumference, < 102 cm (small abdominal circumference (SAC)) and ≥102 cm (large abdominal circumference (LAC)). The chi-square test was used to compare the numerical and percentage representations of the categorical variables. Descriptive analyses, bivariate logistic regression, and multivariate regression were carried out. In multivariate variables, p ≤ 0.05 was used as statistical significance, and an odds ratio was used for the strength of association. Among 360 study subjects, the incidence of post-spinal hypotension was 76.67% with 95%CI [71.9-80.9]. The Large abdominal circumference (LAC) group showed a greater maximal decrease in MAP from baseline compared to the SAC group (LAC 85.6% and SAC 63.3%, p < 0.001). The identified associated factors with the incidence of hypotension were LAC (AOR = 2.98, 95% CI [1.57, 5.65] p = 0.01); BMI > 25 kg/m2 (AOR = 2.3, 95%CI [1.16-4.6], P = 0.018); baby weight> 4 kg (AOR = 11.41 95%CI [2.0-64.86] P = 0.006); sensory block of above T6 level (AOR = 2.22, 95%CI [1.12, 4.42]) p = 0.023) and greater than 500 ml preload given (AOR = 0.42 [95%CI 0.2-0.89] p = 0.023. The study found that there was a high incidence of hypotension during elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia and a significant difference between the SAC and LAC groups. Also, the study found that the independent factors significantly associated with the incidence of hypotension were LAC, higher BMI, higher baby weight, and higher sensory block level, while greater preload volume was protective.

title: Accumulation or adaptation? A longitudinal study of role conflict and turnover intention among Chinese social workers.

author_details.name: Ji J
author_details.affiliation: Yiwu Industrial & Commercial College, Yiwu, China.; Center for Social Work with Chinese Characteristics, YWICC, Yiwu, China.

abstract: The Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) model suggests that job demands and resources influence employees' turnover intention (TI), yet less is known about how these effects unfold over time. Drawing on the competing perspectives of accumulation and adaptation, this study examines whether TI among social workers is shaped by the cumulative effects of past role conflict (RC) or by responses to changing work conditions. Using matched panel data from the 2019 and 2022 waves of the China Social Work Longitudinal Study (CSWLS), the study investigates both lagged and change effects of RC and workplace support (WS). The results show that the association between baseline RC and subsequent TI becomes non-significant after controlling for prior TI. In contrast, changes in RC are positively associated with changes in TI, while changes in WS are negatively associated with changes in TI. Taken together, these findings indicate that baseline RC does not remain independently associated with subsequent TI after prior TI is taken into account, whereas changes in work conditions correspond to changes in TI over time. This study extends the JD-R model by introducing a longitudinal perspective and highlights the importance of considering changes in job demands and resources alongside their prior levels when examining turnover intention over time. Overall, the pattern of findings is more consistent with the adaptation perspective than with a persistent independent association of baseline RC with subsequent TI, contributing to a more dynamic understanding of workforce stability among social workers.

abstract: Bone is a hierarchical and heterogeneous bio-composite material, with cortical and trabecular regions exhibiting distinct mechanical behaviors across scales. Patient-specific Finite Element Analysis (FEA) derived from medical images is increasingly used in both human and veterinary medicine to predict bone mechanical behavior under various loading conditions, assess fracture risk, and evaluate treatment outcomes. However, due to the complexity associated with measuring full elasto-plastic bone properties across multiple scales and bridging microscale properties to macroscale models, simplified material definitions are often adopted in FEA simulations. Such simplifications may produce unrealistic mechanical responses and fail to capture permanent microscopic and macroscopic deformations that occur when stresses exceed the bone yield point, particularly in implant design applications. This study presents an integrated experimental-computational framework for generating continuum material maps as a function of density from tissue-scale characterization of the canine femur. High-depth spherical nanoindentation combined with Genetic Algorithm (GA)-based inverse optimization was conducted to extract mechanically consistent elasto-plastic properties of cortical and trabecular bone from load-displacement responses influenced by post-yield contact uncertainties. Trabecular tissue-scale properties were then assigned to Representative Volume Elements (RVEs) reconstructed from micro-Quantitative Computed Tomography (μQCT) data and homogenized to account for architecture-dependent effective behavior. Finally, optimized cortical and homogenized trabecular properties were correlated with density to establish compartment-specific material mapping relationships for whole-bone FEA simulations. The optimized responses showed good agreement with the experimental indentation measurements, supporting the capability of the proposed framework to generate mechanically informed material definitions for patient-specific bone FEA simulations. Overall, the proposed framework provides a pathway for translating localized experimental measurements into heterogeneous elasto-plastic material inputs for whole-bone FEA without explicitly resolving trabecular microarchitecture.

abstract: Supportive cancer care (SCC) is essential for comprehensive oncology care. It addresses treatment-related adverse effects, reduces long-term sequelae and improves patients' quality of life. Patient-partner (PP) programmes positively impact psychological well-being, patient empowerment and supportive care. Nevertheless, access to SCC remains inconsistent, fragmented and unequally distributed, while PPs are rarely integrated into routine cancer care pathways. Anal cancer is a predominantly localised cancer with high survival rates. Treatment is associated with acute toxicity and often severe long-term sequelae. This interventional public health research study aims to implement and evaluate an innovative enhanced care pathway combining systematic SCC and structured PP support for all individuals diagnosed with anal cancer living in France. The study will assess the intervention's clinical, organisational, and social effects, and will identify the conditions required for its long-term sustainability and transferability. This is a longitudinal mixed-methods case study conducted in two French Comprehensive Cancer Centres. The intervention entails introducing a systematic, coordinated, and repeated SCC offer together with a structured PP support programme for all patients diagnosed with anal cancer and over 12 months following diagnosis. One centre will implement the enhanced care pathway, while the other will initially provide standard care before progressively adopting the intervention during the transferability phase. Quantitative data will include patient-reported outcomes, clinical information and implementation indicators. Qualitative data exploring implementation processes, organisational changes and contextual determinants, will be collected through observations, semi-structured interviews, focus groups and PP activity logs. The study's results will provide essential scientific knowledge on the implementation of programmes providing equitable SCC and PP support access to people living with anal cancer. Specifically, by combining implementation research, participatory approaches and mixed-methods evaluation, the project aims to identify the organisational conditions for the sustainable implementation of such programmes for this population, and their successful transferability to other populations living with cancer and to other healthcare settings.

abstract: This study used mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) D-loop region sequence polymorphisms as molecular markers to investigate the genetic structure and maternal origin of six cattle breeds in the Ili River Valley region of Xinjiang, China. Blood samples were collected from six cattle breeds in the region, including Xinjiang Brown cattle (n = 30), Kazakh cattle (n = 33), Altay White-headed cattle (n = 33), Chinese Simmental cattle (n = 34), Chinese Holstein cattle (n = 31), and Angus cattle (n = 22), for DNA extraction. Complete mtDNA D-loop region sequences were obtained from 183 individuals. Sequence alignment, correction and SNP screening were implemented to characterize sequence variation and base composition. Genetic diversity parameters and pairwise genetic distances were estimated, and a neighbor-joining (NJ) phylogenetic tree was constructed. The complete sequences of the mtDNA D-loop region in the six cattle breed populations were 910-911 bp. The average contents of A, G, T, and C were 32.76%, 13.83%, 28.79%, and 24.62%, respectively, and the overall AT content was higher than GC content. A total of 147 SNPs were detected, accounting for 16.10% of the total sequence length. In total, 107 haplotypes were identified, of which 92 were classified as Bos taurus and 15 as Bos indicus. The k, Hd, and Pi values were 14.24, 0.99, and 0.02, respectively. The constructed NJ phylogenetic tree revealed two major maternal origins-Bos taurus and Bos indicus-among the six cattle breeds. The six cattle breeds in the Ili River Valley region exhibit rich genetic diversity and two maternal origins, predominantly influenced by Bos taurus. These findings provide a theoretical basis for the conservation and rational use of cattle genetic resources in the region.

abstract: Dynamic disturbances significantly impact the stability of end-anchored systems, yet their bearing capacity attenuation and energy response evolution remain poorly understood. This study investigated sandstone end-anchored specimens with anchorage lengths of 300 mm and 600 mm. By conducting comparative static pull-out tests and pull-out tests following sinusoidal cyclic disturbances via a custom-designed apparatus, coupled with Particle Flow Code 2D (PFC2D) numerical simulations, the capacity attenuation, energy dissipation, and internal damage evolution were analyzed. Results reveal a negative correlation between bearing capacity and disturbance frequency. Low-frequency (10 Hz) disturbances cause severe damage, triggering extensive interfacial debonding, whereas 50-200 Hz disturbances induce highly localized damage. The failure process involves elastic, slip, debonding-slip, and complete detachment stages, governed by a tensile-shear mode. This is characterized by axial debonding along the cable-anchoring agent interface and radial or oblique tensile micro-cracking within the anchoring agent. Low-frequency energy propagates efficiently over long distances and continuously accumulates, whereas high-frequency energy dissipates rapidly. Furthermore, extending the anchorage length to 600 mm effectively enhances system rigidity and dynamic resistance. Numerical simulations confirm that lower frequencies accelerate tensile crack development, exacerbating internal damage and capacity degradation.

abstract: This study aimed to develop and comparatively evaluate four YOLO nano-scale one-stage object detectors-YOLOv8n, YOLOv10n, YOLO11n, and YOLO12n-for the automated detection of retained root fragments in dental radiographic images, under identical preprocessing, training, and evaluation protocols. A curated dataset was organized in the YOLO format and evaluated using a nested 5-fold cross-validation strategy to prevent data leakage. An ablation study was additionally conducted to validate the combined bilateral filtering and histogram equalization (BF + HE) preprocessing pipeline. Four YOLO models were fine-tuned from official pretrained weights over 200 epochs. Detection performance was assessed at both the epoch level and the decision-threshold level, reporting the unbiased mean and standard deviation across the independent test folds for precision, sensitivity, F1 score, mean average precision (mAP), and false positives per image (FP/image). In the primary multi-model benchmark, YOLO12n achieved the highest overall detection performance across the held-out test folds, yielding a mean best-epoch F1 score of 0.885 ± 0.007, mAP@0.5 of 0.919 ± 0.021, and mAP@0.5:0.95 of 0.447 ± 0.025 (reaching an optimal-threshold F1 score of 0.888 ± 0.016 with 0.346 ± 0.052 FP/image). YOLO11n followed closely as the second-best performing architecture (F1 = 0.874 ± 0.012, mAP@0.5:0.95 = 0.445 ± 0.019). Furthermore, the preprocessing ablation study confirmed that the hybrid BF + HE pipeline improved detection performance over raw radiographs, elevating YOLO12n's F1 score from 0.856 ± 0.013 to 0.888 ± 0.016 and mAP@0.5:0.95 from 0.438 ± 0.011 to 0.461 ± 0.008. All models demonstrated stable convergence behavior. Modern YOLO architectures, particularly YOLO12n and YOLO11n, demonstrate technical efficacy for automated RRF localization. The observed performance advantages of YOLO12n are associated with its overall architectural refinements, though dedicated modular ablation studies are warranted to isolate the exact contribution of individual attention mechanisms. These findings demonstrate the technical feasibility of lightweight one-stage object detectors for identifying retained root fragments in dental panoramic radiographs, serving as a baseline for future prospective clinical evaluations.

title: Comparative evaluation of machine learning algorithms for Maize Lethal Necrosis Disease detection under class imbalance.

author_details.name: Wanyonyi M
author_details.affiliation: Department of Mathematics and Statistics, University of Embu, Embu, Kenya.; African Institute for Capacity Development (AICAD), Nairobi, Kenya.

abstract: Maize Lethal Necrosis Disease (MLND) remains a major threat to maize production in sub-Saharan Africa, creating a need for accurate, interpretable, and computationally efficient diagnostic tools. This study presents a comprehensive comparative evaluation of nine machine learning algorithms for MLND detection using a structured feature-based dataset comprising 7,892 maize leaf observations obtained from the Kenya Agricultural and Livestock Research Organization (KALRO). The extracted features captured color, texture, lesion, and morphological characteristics associated with MLND symptoms. To address moderate class imbalance, the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and class weighting were incorporated within the model development pipeline, and their contribution was quantified through an ablation study. Model performance was evaluated using repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation, an independent 80/20 test set, and leave-one-county-out cross-validation (LOCO-CV) to assess geographic generalisability. Across repeated cross-validation, the leading models demonstrated consistent predictive performance with narrow 95% confidence intervals. CatBoost achieved the highest mean accuracy (0.753; 95% CI: 0.730-0.773), while Logistic Regression attained the highest mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC = 0.808; 95% CI: 0.787-0.830). The overlapping confidence intervals among the best-performing models indicate broadly comparable predictive performance, highlighting the importance of considering complementary criteria beyond accuracy alone. LOCO-CV demonstrated minimal performance variation across counties, indicating good internal geographic generalisability. Calibration analysis using Expected Calibration Error (ECE) showed that post-hoc probability calibration substantially improved the reliability of predicted probabilities. At the same time, explainable artificial intelligence techniques consistently identified Chlorosis Intensity, Green-Yellow Ratio, and Necrotic Area as the most influential predictors. Considering predictive performance alongside computational efficiency, model size, and inference latency, LightGBM provided the most favorable balance for resource-constrained environments. In contrast, Logistic Regression offered a highly interpretable alternative with minimal computational requirements. Although the achieved performance indicates that approximately one in four samples may be misclassified and further external validation is required before operational deployment, the findings demonstrate that structured feature-based machine learning provides a transparent, computationally efficient, and interpretable framework for MLND detection and establishes a strong foundation for future field-based decision-support systems.

abstract: The forthcoming scoping review will synthesize evidence on arts-based and digital engagement initiatives that support social inclusion, mental health, and cultural expression among older adults, with a particular focus on structurally-disadvantaged populations. Rapid digital transformation in the arts, including virtual and augmented reality, digital storytelling, and generative artificial intelligence, has expanded opportunities for participation and creative expression. However, access remains uneven, and there is limited consolidated evidence on effectiveness, equity considerations, and best practices for implementation across diverse contexts. Guided by Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR reporting standards, the forthcoming review will systematically search peer-reviewed and grey literature across major health, social science, and interdisciplinary databases from inception to October 2026. An integrated knowledge translation approach will be embedded throughout the review, engaging older adults, caregivers, community arts practitioners, and cultural leaders as active partners in refining search strategies, interpreting findings, and shaping dissemination. Data will be extracted and synthesized using both quantitative mapping and qualitative content analysis to identify program models, theoretical frameworks, implementation strategies, outcomes, and equity considerations. Findings will generate a comprehensive evidence map of effective and emerging practices, highlight barriers such as digital exclusion and cultural underrepresentation, and identify ethical and legal considerations in digital arts engagement. The review will inform the development of culturally safe, accessible, and inclusive arts and digital programming, and will provide actionable guidance for researchers, practitioners, policymakers, and community organizations seeking to enhance well-being, social connection, and cultural continuity among older adults.

abstract: This study translated, culturally adapted, and evaluated the First Aid Willingness Questionnaire for Schoolchildren to assess adolescents' self-reported readiness to help and potential barriers to first-aid provision. This cross-sectional psychometric study included 470 high school students in Aksaray, Türkiye. The questionnaire underwent forward-backward translation, review by 12 experts, and pilot testing with 35 students. Exploratory factor analysis derived the structure, which was subsequently evaluated via ordinal confirmatory factor analysis in the same sample. Content and construct validity, internal consistency, and measurement invariance across gender, grade level, and perceived family income were assessed. All item-level content validity ratios exceeded 0.83; the scale-level content validity index was 0.90. Removing two items yielded a 16-item, three-factor structure: First Aid Willingness, Negative Emotions, and Perceived Knowledge. The model showed acceptable fit: scaled χ²(101) = 288.09, p < 0.001; comparative fit index = 0.95; Tucker-Lewis index = 0.94; root mean square error of approximation = 0.06, 90% confidence interval [0.05, 0.07]; standardized root mean square residual = 0.06. Composite reliability ranged from 0.79 to 0.90. Average variance extracted ranged from 0.49 to 0.59, with borderline convergent validity for Negative Emotions. Discriminant validity was supported. Cronbach's alpha ranged from 0.72 to 0.87, and McDonald's omega from 0.74 to 0.87. Configural, threshold, metric, and scalar invariance were supported across all grouping variables. Strict invariance was supported across grade level and perceived family income, but not gender. The results provide preliminary evidence for the Turkish questionnaire's psychometric properties and support subscale interpretation and latent mean comparisons within the study sample. Independent replication and evaluation of temporal stability, responsiveness, and external validity are needed.

title: Data-driven forecasting of Flu, RSV, and COVID-19 related outcomes in the United States and Canada via Hankel dynamic mode decomposition.

author_details.name: Redman WT
author_details.affiliation: Intelligent Systems Center, Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory, Laurel, Maryland, United States of America.; Electrical and Computer Engineering Department, Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore, Maryland, United States of America.

abstract: The (large) season-to-season variability and limited dynamical history make the forecasting of infectious diseases a challenging problem. Here, we examine the extent to which advances in data-driven dynamical modeling can provide accurate predictions by benchmarking the performance of one such method, Hankel dynamic mode decomposition (DMD), on the 2024-2025 influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and COVID-19 seasons in the United States and Canada. Using Hankel-DMD, we generated weekly forecasts that were submitted to the Center for Disease Control and Prevention's (CDC) FluSight Forecast Hub and the University of Guelph's AI4CastingHub. Across both Hubs, we find that Hankel-DMD can provide high quality forecasts at the beginning and end of the season, but forecasts in the middle of the season suffer from significant overestimation of the season peak. This leads to worse than baseline performance on FluSight Forecast Hub, when submissions are evaluated across the entire season. Hankel-DMD is found to be the best among a small number of models that submitted enough forecasts against which to compare for forecasting influenza, RSV, and COVID-19 in Canada. As this was the first active year of AI4CastingHub, this suggests that Hankel-DMD may be especially useful when expertise is lacking for predicting infectious dynamics in new regions. To study how Hankel-DMD can be better equipped to provide accurate forecasts during the season peak, we explored whether DMD with memory, a recently developed approach for applying DMD to non-stationary dynamical systems, provides significant improvements. Retrospective analysis using DMD with memory shows promise in reducing overestimation during season peak, but the extent to which its optimal use can be achieved in a live forecasting setting remains to be seen. Collectively, our results demonstrate that Hankel-DMD has potential as an efficient and interpretable method for the forecasting of infectious diseases, while also highlighting a number of remaining methodological challenges which future work should aim to address.

abstract: Due to their low signal-to-noise ratio and non-stationarity, accurately classifying EEG signals is still one of the main hindrances that limit the real-world applications of a brain-computer interface (BCI). Deep learning (DL) is a potential method for addressing the problem. However, how to create a suitable DL network for motor imagery (MI)-based BCIs poses severe challenges in the case of insufficient training data. In this paper, a DL network based on multiscale convolutional neural network (CNN) and temporal and channel attention mechanisms is proposed for decoding MI tasks. Temporal and spatial features are extracted by four parallel CNN branches, each of which is followed by a Transformer block for learning the global correlations of local time features. The outputs from the four Transformer blocks are concatenated along channel dimension and then input into a channel attention module for channel fusion. The subsequent feature map is classified by a CNN, which replaces the commonly used fully connected layer for reducing computational complexity. The proposed network was evaluated on three publicly available BCI datasets and compared with five state-of-the-art DL networks. The training data sets are augmented using the approach segmentation and reconstruction. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed network achieved an average accuracy of 80.21% on Dataset 1 (4-class tasks), 90.19% on Dataset 2 (2-class tasks), and 97.32% on Dataset 3 (4-class tasks), surpassing the strongest baselines FBCNet on Dataset 1, MSFBCNN on Dataset 2 and MSFBCNN on Dataset 3 by 2.59%, 1.27%, and 1.99% respectively. The network effectively decoded the MI-based EEG signals, providing a potential method for BCI applications.

abstract: Foot posture is a key determinant of limb-biomechanics, gait balance as well as functional mobility. Usage of foot pressure index (FPI) is widespread to but the determinants of FPI without accounting to the left right foot differences. Therefore, identifying limb-specific determinants would enhance screening accuracy and help in more targeted interventions. The objective of the study was to determine and compare limb specific predictors based on the foot pressure index of right and left foot among young adults using machine learning models. A total of 581 (290 females and 291 males) 18-25-year-old young adults were assessed on anthropometric measures, joint hyper mobility and functional mobility. Using SAS-Viya, separate entropy-based decision trees, along with logistic regression models were developed and model performance was evaluated using validation-test accuracy and area under the curve (AUC). Decision tree models outperformed logistic regression for both FPI-Left (FPI-L) and FPI-Right (FPIR). FPIR was primarily predicted by joint hyper mobility, followed by stair ascent time, stability as well as BMI with stronger influence of both structural and load related factors. FPIL was predicted by closed-eye balance along BMI, open eye balance, stair ascent, Beighton score, underscoring the role of sensory motor control. The findings of the study reflect that young adults foot posture is complex, limb specific interactions among anthropometric, functional and sensory factors.

abstract: Leaf day respiratory rate (Rd), a pivotal component of plant carbon metabolism that directly modulates net photosynthetic carbon gain and plant fitness, has long been challenging to accurately quantify due to overlapping CO2 fluxes with photosynthesis and photorespiration (Rp). This study aimed to disentangle Rd from Rp in C3 crops using a high-CO2/low-O2 (>1200 μmol mol-1 CO2 + 2% O2) An/Ca (net photosynthetic rate-ambient CO2 concentration) model. We integrated two datasets: An/Ca curve data of four C3 species (Trifolium pratense, Silphium perfoliatum, Lolium perenne, Triticum aestivum) under ambient O2 (21% O2) from Ye et al. (2025) and newly collected data under low O2 (2% O2) for the same species. A dedicated model (Eqn 1) was developed to extract key parameters [e.g., the maximum net photosynthetic rate (Anmax), CO2 compensation point (Γ) in the presence of Rd, photorespiratory rate at Ca = 0 μmol mol-1 (RC0)] from An/Ca curves, with ANOVA confirming no significant differences between calculated and observed parameter values (p > 0.05). Under 2% O2, Rp was strongly suppressed, making the gross photorespiratory rate (RC = Rp + Rd) a reliable proxy for approximate Rd. Results showed that Rd estimates from the high-CO2/low-O2 approach (0.74-1.12 μmol m-2 s-1) were consistent with literature ranges (0.74-2.89 μmol m-2 s-1) for four C3 crops. Interspecific differences in Rd were observed: L. perenne had the highest Rd, while T. aestivum had the lowest, which correlated with species-specific photosynthetic traits (e.g., carboxylation efficiency). Rd remained stable across O2 levels (21% vs. 2%), indicating independence from short-term photorespiratory flux changes. The RC ≈ Rd assumption is supported by the substantial decrease in Γ (50-67%) and RCO (40-55%) under 2% O2, and by the consistency of Rd estimates with literature ranges, although independent ground-truth measurements remain to be conducted. This study suggests the high-CO2/low-O2 An/Ca model as a new tool for Rd quantification in C3 crops. The findings enhance understanding of non-photosynthetic carbon flux dynamics and provide critical parameters for refining crop carbon cycling models to predict growth and yield under current and future atmospheric conditions.

abstract: Since 2015, oral emergency contraceptives (ECs) have been available in German community pharmacies without prescription as over-the-counter medicines. Given the financial burden, unnecessary hormonal exposure and associated side effects, systematic information gathering is crucial to prevent unnecessary recommendations. This study aimed to determine whether pharmacy staff ask the checklist questions recommended by the German Federal Chamber of Pharmacists (BAK) guideline and provide correct recommendations when oral EC is not indicated (appropriate outcome), and to examine associated factors. A nationwide study using the simulated patient methodology - considered the "gold standard" - was conducted with a stratified random sample of 376 community pharmacies across Germany. Eight trained female mystery callers aged 21-24 simulated a scenario in which a combined oral contraceptive was forgotten once after sexual intercourse. However, the pill could still be taken within the 12-hour window, making oral EC unnecessary according to the BAK guideline. To ensure quality, each call was monitored by a second observer. Of 376 mystery calls conducted, 322 were included in the primary analysis. An appropriate outcome was achieved in 44.4% (143/322), while oral EC was unnecessarily recommended in 49.1% (158/322). The median questioning score was 2.0 of 4.0 points. A multivariable logistic regression model showed that a higher questioning score and mystery caller identity were significantly associated with the appropriate outcome. Qualitative findings indicated both positive counseling practices and notable deficiencies among pharmacy staff. The results show deficits in information gathering and appropriate recommendations. To improve counseling, the consistent use of the BAK checklist during telephone consultations should be explicitly recommended in the relevant guideline. Targeted training for pharmacy staff may help address professional and communication deficits. Surprisingly, some mystery callers were significantly associated with the appropriate outcome, highlighting the need for further research on the influence of vocal characteristics and last names in telephone consultations.

abstract: Banana breeding programs prioritize improving yield with resistance to biotic stresses while maintaining fruit quality. This study focused on identifying genotypes with resistance to five major biotic constraints including Cosmopolites sordidus, Radopholus similis, banana Xanthomonas wilt, Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense - Race 1 and Pseudocercospora fijiensis. A diverse set of diploid and tetraploid genotypes was phenotyped under controlled screenhouse and field conditions to identify potential sources of. A partially replicated (P-rep) design, was used to accommodate unequal plant availability arising from asynchronous multiplication. P-rep design enabled robust phenotypic comparisons and identification of genotypes expressing resistance to multiple biotic stresses. Several diploid genotypes exhibited resistance to multiple constraints, highlighting their potential as parental lines for resistance introgression and broadening the genetic base for banana improvement. Leveraging on the efficiency and precision of the P-rep experimental design, these findings accelerate the phenotyping of genotypes.

abstract: Adolescent pregnancy remains a significant public health concern, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Although various interventions have been implemented to address this issue, many have failed to achieve positive outcomes due to numerous barriers. To explore the barriers to implementing adolescent pregnancy prevention interventions in LMICs. This qualitative exploratory study involved 19 adolescent pregnancy prevention program implementers across 24 LMICs. Data were collected through virtual in-depth individual interviews, organized using Dedoose software, and analyzed thematically. Findings highlighted seven interrelated challenges shaping programme reach, acceptability, and sustainability. Experts reported that adolescents' engagement depended on perceived usefulness and, at times, material or social benefits of attendance, while stigma made participation social risky and encouraged private information-seeking. Prevention efforts were further constrained by gendered allocation and unequal decision-making power, which limited boys' participation and girls' agency. Separately, poverty, household material insecurity, and transactional marriage practices such as bride price contributed to early unions and subsequent childbearing, while programme legitimacy is challenged by taboo, religious opposition, contraception myths, and the normalization of violence. Finally, implementation was hindered by administrative delays, weak institutional backing, school-level resistance, and unstable or poorly enforced policy environments, limiting continuity and scale-up of interventions. Effective teenage pregnancy prevention in LMICs requires more than delivering sexual and reproductive health (SRH) information; programmes must be designed to feel relevant to adolescents while reducing stigma and protecting confidentiality to support genuine engagement. Interventions also need to address gendered power dynamics and gatekeeper control, alongside community-level legitimacy barriers such as taboo, religious opposition, contraception myths, and normalized violence. Sustainable impact will depend on enabling implementation conditions, including reduced bureaucratic delays, stronger institutional and school support, coherent policies, reliable financing beyond donor cycles, and better data to guide targeted action.

abstract: Smartphone mHealth apps (mHealth apps) have played a highly positive role in medical services, which provides a new direction for users' medical services and health management. Although smartphone mHealth apps provide many benefits for users, people know little about the factors that drive elderly users to adopt this new service platform in the context of an aging population. This study aims to learn the factors that affect elderly people's intentions to adopt smartphone mHealth apps, and use the technology acceptance model as a theoretical basis to integrate perceived convenience, perceived quality, perceived risk and perceived trust, in an attempt to construct a research model on the intentions to use smartphone mHealth apps. The elderly users' data were collected by questionnaire survey and analyzed quantitatively by structural equation model. By analyzing the 263 valid data collected, the results showed that users' perceived trust (β = 0.427, p < .001), attitude (β = 0.285, p < .001), and perceived quality (β = 0.278, p < .001) of mobile medical applications positively influenced users' intention to use the applications, while perceived risk (β = -0.173, p < .001) had a negative impact on the intention to use. Perceived trust was also directly positively influenced by perceived quality (β = 0.434, p < .001) and perceived ease of use, and perceived convenience positively influenced perceived usefulness (β = 0.358, p < .001) and attitude (β = 0.299, p < .001). These findings can help us better understand the factors that influence the adoption of smartphone mHealth apps. This study further extends the technology acceptance model and its application domains to help mHealth researchers, designers, marketers, and service providers improve mHealth services and help increase users' intentions to adopt mHealth apps.

abstract: Various 3D point cloud semantic segmentation methods have been proposed, yet they remain challenged by limited use of geometric cues and inaccurate predictions around thin structures, object boundaries, and rare classes in cluttered indoor scenes. To address these limitations, we propose GAMPoint, a transformer-based framework for 3D semantic segmentation. Specifically, Enhanced Relative Positional Encoding (EnhancedRPE) augments relative positional modeling with local surface-variation cues to strengthen geometry-aware feature learning. In addition, Conditional Multimodal Gating (CMG) is introduced as an input-side embedding interface. In GAMPoint, XYZ coordinates provide the basic point-cloud geometry, while CMG incorporates available auxiliary attributes, such as RGB colors and surface normals, before the serialized encoder. For RGB-D reconstructed datasets such as ScanNet, XYZ coordinates already contain depth-derived geometric information; raw depth is not used as an additional per-point channel. GAMPoint incorporates EnhancedRPE and CMG into Point Transformer V3 and is evaluated on S3DIS and ScanNet. Experimental results show competitive performance and modest gains over strong point-transformer baselines. Class-wise and repeated-run analyses further indicate category-dependent improvements and consistent gains across matched repeated runs under the reported settings. Code is available at github.com/airmanss/ GAMPoint.

abstract: Past climate change has repeatedly reshaped Earth's biomes, yet how their expansion and contraction influence biodiversity patterns through time remains unclear. Competing hypotheses propose that either historical biome area has a strong influence on diversity, or that biodiversity responds rapidly to environmental change, such that present-day biome area and energy are sufficient to explain diversity patterns. Progress in testing these ideas has been limited by sparse and inconsistent proxy data and the coarse resolution of existing paleoclimate models. Here, we reconstructed global biome histories for the Cenozoic (66-0 Ma) by downscaling five different paleoclimate simulations. Estimates of change in biome area through time were generally consistent among alternative climate models and with the empirical proxy record. Accounting for variation among models, we found that present-day area and energy were consistently better predictors of vertebrate diversity than historical measures. These findings suggest biodiversity tracks the ecological limits set by shifting biomes, leaving sparse legacy of past dynamics. Our results highlight the importance of integrating multiple paleoclimate reconstructions when assessing the historical drivers of biodiversity.

abstract: The influence of the phyllosphere microbiome on plant health and disease development is well established. However, the roles of host resistance phenotype, seasonal variations, and accumulated temperature in shaping the phyllosphere mycobiome of Norway spruce (Picea abies) remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated (i) the phyllosphere mycobiome assembly of a subset of Heterobasidion partially resistant and susceptible Norway spruce genotypes, (ii) how fungal community composition in these genotypes changes across seasons and with temperature, and (iii) the extent to which the phyllosphere mycobiome shared taxa with the seed-associated fungal communities of the same genotypes. Needle samples were collected from Heterobasidion partially resistant and susceptible Norway spruce seedlings growing in an open field in May, July and September 2022. Fungal communities were characterized using internal transcribed spacer (ITS) amplicon sequencing. Alpha diversity metrics (richness, diversity and evenness) of the phyllosphere fungal community were significantly different between susceptible and partially resistant Norway spruce genotypes. Although the distributions showed substantial overlap between resistance classes, all three alpha-diversity metrics differed significantly between the groups (p < 0.05). Community composition was associated with both host resistance phenotype and temperature-related variables, with average and accumulated temperature explaining a greater proportion of variation than host resistance phenotype. Less than 1% of phyllosphere fungal taxa overlapped with the seed-associated fungal communities. Network analyses further revealed seasonal differences in fungal association patterns between partially resistant and susceptible seedlings.

abstract: Participation equity is essential for ensuring that students gain cognitive and social benefits from collaborative learning, yet there is a lack of quantitative benchmarks for interpreting participation and opportunity distributions in small-group collaboration. This study focuses on two turn-based analytical dimensions of participation equity: participation equality, measured by students' shares of speaking turns, and opportunity equality, measured by students' shares of addressed opportunities. Using the standard deviation of these rates, the study establishes preliminary, context-specific simulation-based reference values for identifying departures from an idealized triadic turn-taking baseline. The empirical dataset included 117 fourth-grade primary school students from two classes in mainland China, who worked in heterogeneous triads on mathematical and reading tasks. Using agent-based modeling and Monte Carlo simulation, the study estimated local turn-taking parameters from empirical data, generated reference distributions under an ideal-equity baseline, and conducted sensitivity analyses to examine model stability. Results support the internal stability of the model and provide turn-count-specific reference values for interpreting participation and opportunity inequality. The findings offer preliminary reference values for interpreting participation and opportunity distributions in collaborative learning and highlight the importance of turn count when evaluating structural patterns of participation and opportunity in triadic classroom dialogue. These reference values describe structural participation patterns rather than collaboration quality and require recalibration and independent validation before application in other educational settings.

abstract: Marburg virus disease (MVD), a deadly zoonotic illness in humans, is caused by the Marburg virus (MARV), a single-stranded RNA virus belonging to the Orthomarburgvirus genus of the Filoviridae family. There are currently no approved vaccines or efficient antiviral therapies for MARV, despite high morbidity and fatality rates of the virus, particularly in Africa. Recognizing its epidemic potential and its inclusion on the WHO list of blueprint priority pathogens, an immunoinformatics approach was used to design novel multi-epitope saRNA vaccine candidates (MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII) targeting the viral GP, NP, VP40, and VP35 via CD8 + , CD4 + , and B cell epitopes. These epitopes were derived from target protein sequences and incorporated into MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII after validation for antigenicity, non-allergenicity, non-toxicity, and conservation. Additionally, the selected epitopes were conjugated to suitable adjuvants via various linkers, thereby enabling the design of a potentially stable vaccine. Additionally, the designed MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII were incorporated into the standard saRNA model, in which ORF-2 encodes the target vaccine peptide. Moreover, biophysical analyses unveiled that the developed vaccines are basic (pI < 7), soluble (GRAVY < 0), and stable (aliphatic index < 80). Subsequently, docking of MB-saVaxI to TLR2 (-938.3) and TLR4 (-902.4), and MB-saVaxII to TLR3 (-1485.4) and TLR7 (-1543.6) demonstrated significant affinity, with detailed hydrogen-bond interactions validated by MM-GBSA and molecular dynamics simulations. Furthermore, MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII were effectively cloned in-silico into Escherichia coli, and immune simulations indicated that the vaccines triggered robust innate and adaptive immunity, with a sustained memory response and TH cell activation, as evidenced by IFN-γ and IL-2 production. Additionally, the mRNA structure of MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII remained stable throughout the expression pathway in the host. However, extensive in-vitro and in-vivo studies are needed to establish the safety and efficacy of this vaccine candidate conclusively.

abstract: British Columbia is one of the most ethnically diverse provinces in Canada, with South Asians emerging as one of the fastest-growing ethnic minority groups, burdened by a high incidence of type 2 diabetes. During the COVID-19 pandemic, many healthcare services shifted to virtual care to minimize infection transmission. Given the limited understanding of how primary care physicians in BC adapted their diabetes care approaches and the consequent impact on patient experience, this qualitative study aims to explore the effects of pandemic-related control measures on primary care diabetes services in BC from the perspectives of general practitioners, focusing particularly on their South Asian patients. We conducted semi-structured interviews with ten primary care physicians serving large South Asian patient populations. Interviews explored the pandemic's effects on care delivery, provider adaptations, and consequences for South Asian patients with diabetes. Sessions were held in person or via Zoom/Teams and transcribed verbatim. Transcripts underwent thematic content analysis to identify recurring themes and insights regarding barriers, adaptations, and recommendations to improve diabetes care. The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted diabetes care, shifting services to virtual care and interrupting routine monitoring. This transition impacted specific aspect of diabetes care that can best be provided in-person (e.g., foot examinations, blood pressure checks and lifestyle counselling). The pandemic compounded existing issues, e.g., cost, concerns with side effects, and medication compliance among South Asian patients. Physicians also observed a general rise in anxiety and depression during the pandemic among their patients. Older South Asian patients faced additional cultural, language, and digital barriers; physicians struggled to obtain timely Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) tests. For many patients, a significant reliance on pharmacists embedded within certain physician's clinics, ensured an uninterrupted access to diabetes medication and supplies. The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted diabetes care, with some groups facing additional cultural, language, and digital barriers. Our findings highlight the need for primary care reforms: improved telemedicine and EMR infrastructure, and policies to support virtual care. Bridging the digital divide and implementing targeted supports are essential to minimize care disruption for vulnerable populations during future pandemics or similar crises and ensure equity.

abstract: There is limited data on prescription behaviour and compliance with interstitial lung disease (ILD) guidelines among pulmonologists. This study aimed to evaluate ILDs treatment prescription behaviour in India. Prescriptions of treatment-naive ILD patients from 13 tertiary care hospitals were reviewed and classified as guideline compliant (GCP) or non-compliant (GNCP) for pharmacological and non-pharmacological components. Change in forced vital capacity (FVC), diffusing capacity (DLCO), and six-minute walk distance (6-MWD) at 6 and 12 months were compared between GCP and GNCP. After screening 720 participants, 425 treatment-naïve ILD patients (56.7% female; mean age 51.7 years) were included. Connective tissue associated-ILD (CTD-ILD) was the most common diagnosis (36.2%), followed by hypersensitivity pneumonitis (17.4%), idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF, 13.9%), interstitial pneumonia with autoimmune features (13.9%), and sarcoidosis (8.2%). GCP rates for ILD specific pharmacotherapy were 83%, 74.7%, and 93.5% for IPF, CTD-ILD, and sarcoidosis, respectively. In IPF, patients with GCP had significantly lower FVC decline at 12 months compared to the GNCP (0.06 L vs. 0.25 L; p = 0.02). There was huge care-gap in non-pharmacological advice with 13.2%, 7.1%, 10.2% and 4.2% of eligible cases were advised vaccination, pulmonary rehabilitation, antigen avoidance, and lung transplantation counselling, respectively. India-ILD care study revealed a huge care gap with significantly under-prescription of non-pharmacological components. These results highlight the urgent need for organized implementation strategies including dissemination of guidelines, and a greater emphasis on a structured management protocol that includes both pharmacological and non-pharmacological treatment to optimize outcomes for ILD in India.

abstract: Preclinical thoracic micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) is constrained by the brief pulmonary enhancement window of intravenously (IV) administered iodinated contrast, which the kidneys clear rapidly. We performed a feasibility study in mice comparing IV tail-vein injection with intratracheal microspray instillation of the clinical agent iohexol. Mice received iohexol (100 µL, 500 mg/mL) by either route. Whole-body projections were acquired to 120 min and thoracic sections to 30 min, each animal scanned before contrast in the same session. Contrast distribution was recorded by compartment and quantified from regions of interest. IV delivery produced vascular and cardiac opacification with progressive bladder accumulation, which was the largest signal in every IV animal by 120 min. Intratracheal delivery produced widespread, comparatively uniform lung-parenchymal opacification at 5, 15 and 30 min with no discrete bladder opacity at any time; coronal thoracic signal was 0.77 at 5 min and 0.72 at 30 min, against 0.09 to 0.19 after IV injection. Acute safety was assessed at 5 and 29 h by serum biochemistry and histopathology against untreated controls. ALT, AST and blood urea nitrogen did not differ among groups. Creatinine was modestly higher than in controls after both routes, with no difference between routes, consistent with renal excretion of absorbed iohexol. Lung, heart, liver, spleen and kidney showed preserved architecture without acute injury. These data identify intratracheal microspray delivery as a practical way to hold iodine in the lung parenchyma across a thoracic micro-CT acquisition and provide the basis for a confirmatory quantitative study.

abstract: The footprints of residential segregation have long been documented, yet the role of urban form as both medium and manifestation of segregation remains under-specified. We investigate whether the configuration of the built fabric may encode residential segregation in its spatial structure, hypothesising that built-form entropy (BFE) regimes are associated with the spatial distribution of income groups and their local clustering in non-linear ways. We examine this by quantifying BFE through a Shannon-based measure computed from building footprints, characterising income-based distributions using the Gini index and Moran's I, and placing both on a common spatial footing through a regular tessellation. Applying this framework to São Paulo, Latin America's largest city, we find non-linear relationships between BFE, income, and segregation: income levels and residential clustering increase toward both extremes of the entropy spectrum, with a stronger rise at the high-entropy end. This asymmetry suggests that high-entropy urban forms are associated with distinct spatial processes of segregation, including elite enclaving and incremental development in lower-income settlements, while low-entropy forms reflect more selective occupation shaped by planning and market filtering. Overall, the findings suggest that built form is more than a neutral backdrop, functioning as both affordance and signal of segregation.

abstract: Lens dislocation (ectopia lentis) is a recognized anterior-segment manifestation of fibrillinopathy. This exploratory phenotype-first study compared macular optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) parameters between participants with and without documented lens dislocation and descriptively reviewed available archived clinical FBN1 reports. This retrospective, availability-based study included 16 participants classified by verified current or historical lens-dislocation status. Participant-level superficial capillary plexus (SCP) vessel density was calculated by averaging valid bilateral measurements or using the single valid eye. Five OCTA endpoints were compared using two-sided Mann-Whitney U tests; Benjamini-Hochberg q values were used as a multiplicity sensitivity analysis. Seven archived clinical FBN1 reports from lens-dislocation-positive (LD+) participants were summarized without variant reclassification. No genotype-OCTA association was assessed. The cohort comprised 7 LD+ and 9 lens-dislocation-negative (LD-) participants; 15 participants (6 LD+ and 9 LD-) contributed quantitative OCTA data. Foveal SCP vessel density was lower in LD+ participants (median [IQR], 19.38% [18.68-20.04] vs 30.20% [29.20-31.85]; p = 0.036), but the finding was not retained after multiplicity sensitivity analysis (q = 0.180). Whole-image, parafoveal, and perifoveal vessel-density comparisons were not significant (p = 0.328, 0.272, and 0.238; q = 0.410 each), and OD-only foveal avascular zone area did not differ (n = 14; p = 0.606; q = 0.606). Six of seven archived reports documented an FBN1 variant; one was negative within its assay scope. The unadjusted foveal signal was not robust to multiplicity analysis, and other OCTA endpoints did not differ significantly. Marked between-group differences in spherical equivalent and axial length, the small sample, and heterogeneous routine-care genetic reports limit interpretation. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish OCTA as a diagnostic or prognostic test or demonstrate an individual-level genotype-OCTA association.

abstract: Stroke is a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with hypertension being its most important modifiable risk factor. Although the association between elevated blood pressure and stroke is well established, the extent to which longitudinal blood pressure patterns influence the timing of stroke remains poorly understood, particularly in low-resource settings. We investigated the association between longitudinal systolic and diastolic blood pressure trajectories and time to stroke among hypertensive patients in Ethiopia. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 494 newly diagnosed hypertensive patients receiving follow-up care at two general hospitals in Benishangul-Gumuz, Ethiopia, between January 1, 2015, and September 1, 2024. Time to stroke was analyzed using a Cox proportional hazards model, while repeated systolic and diastolic blood pressure measurements were modelled using linear mixed-effects models. The longitudinal and survival processes were jointly estimated using a Bayesian multivariate joint modelling framework. Posterior adjusted hazard ratios (AHRs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs) were estimated. The incidence of stroke was 2.19 per 100 person-years (95% CI: 1.60-2.64). Higher current underlying systolic and diastolic blood pressure levels were associated with increased stroke risk, with posterior AHRs of 3.25 (95% CrI: 1.85-5.83) and 2.32 (95% CrI: 1.35-4.27), respectively. Older age (≥65 years; AHR: 6.18; 95% CrI: 2.32-18.05), comorbidity (AHR: 4.00; 95% CrI: 1.72-10.25), and stage II hypertension (AHR: 4.06; 95% CrI: 1.49-16.36) were associated with earlier stroke occurrence. Rural residence was associated with a lower hazard of stroke (AHR: 0.16; 95% CrI: 0.05-0.40). Higher longitudinal systolic and diastolic blood pressure trajectories were associated with earlier stroke occurrence. These findings support regular blood pressure monitoring and targeted prevention strategies among older adults and patients with comorbidities in similar resource-limited settings.

abstract: Conical picks are critical components in key excavation equipment (including shearers, continuous miners, and roadheaders) employed for rock fragmentation in mining and civil engineering. This study proposes the multi-fidelity transfer learning multi-layer perceptron (MF-TLMLP) method to predict cutting performance. Addressing the scarcity of high-fidelity (HF) data, MF-TLMLP integrates low-fidelity (LF) and HF data through a multi-channel fusion and transfer learning approach. Simulations using Latin hypercube sampling (LHS) generated 2500 LF samples and 500 HF samples. Compared to traditional Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and transfer learning models, MF-TLMLP demonstrated superior performance, achieving a higher coefficient of determination (R2) and a lower mean squared error (MSE). Morris screening based on mean absolute elementary effects revealed output-dependent sensitivities, with cutting thickness dominating the force responses and cutting speed dominating the pulse-number responses within the sampled domain. These results demonstrate the potential of MF-TLMLP for predicting HF numerical cutting responses for the investigated rock properties, parameter ranges, and adjacent double-pick configuration.
