abstract: Cytotoxic chemotherapy typically results in the elimination of a fraction of the tumor with surviving cells entering a state of persistence or premature replicative senescence that can lead to recurrence. Here, we show that therapy-induced senescence is associated with robust up-regulation of Fas and/or TRAIL-R2/DR5 death receptors in vitro and in vivo. The latter receptors restricted entry to senescence and exerted selective pressure on senescent cells through promoting assembly of proapoptotic receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)/Fas-associated death domain protein (FADD)/Caspase-8 "FADDosome" complexes, restrained by cFLIPL. Accordingly, deletion of CASP-8 robustly enhanced entry to senescence and prolonged the life span of senescent cells. cIAP-2, which inhibits death receptor-driven cell death, was also up-regulated in senescent cells, and deletion of IAPs suppressed entry to senescence. Consistent with this, small-molecule IAP antagonists exhibited potent senolytic activity through enhancing death receptor-initiated Caspase-8 activation. Thus, death receptor-driven assembly of RIPK1/FADD/Caspase-8 complexes in senescent cells orchestrates addiction to IAPs that can be exploited by IAP antagonists.

abstract: Understanding oceanic transport and material fate has long relied on observations that primarily resolve mesoscale, largely geostrophic flows, leaving the role of submesoscale turbulence comparatively unobserved and poorly understood. Here, using new high-resolution drifter-cluster experiments with closest initial spacings below 1 km, we provide direct Lagrangian observations of how submesoscale turbulence modifies mesoscale eddy coherence and transport pathways. The clustered drifters resolve intense, transient ageostrophic motions that are fundamentally absent from geostrophic descriptions of eddy behavior. Analyzed in an eddy-centered reference frame, the observations reveal pronounced submesoscale-driven radial dispersion that facilitates substantial water-mass exchange between the eddy core and its periphery in both the mixed layer and the subsurface. Quantitative estimates indicate submesoscale horizontal diffusivity of O(10 to 100) m2/s and a nonlocal dispersion regime across submesoscales. These results challenge the traditional view of mesoscale eddies as coherent structures containing a persistent water mass, with broad implications for interpreting and predicting the transport and fate of tracers in the ocean.

abstract: Anatomically modern humans first settled in Europe at least 45,000 years ago, yet limited genomic data from 45 to 20 thousand years (ka) constrain reconstructions of Upper Palaeolithic population dynamics. Before the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM; ∼26.5 to 19 ka), Gravettian groups (∼34 to 25 ka) were widespread across Europe and genetically diverse, including the Fournol and Věstonice lineages. Here, we present genome-wide data from three Gravettian individuals: two from the Franco-Cantabrian region (Chufín, Spain, and Isturitz, France) and one from Italy (Ostuni1b). Our analyses reveal previously undetected gene flow between eastern and western early Gravettian populations in southwestern Europe, challenging models of regional genetic continuity from the Aurignacian to the Solutrean (∼24 to 19 ka). To investigate population history during the LGM, a period for which human skeletal remains are extremely rare, we analyzed sedimentary ancient DNA from Solutrean Layer 122 at El Mirón Cave (Cantabria, Spain; ∼22,000 calibrated years before the present), recovering ∼14,000 human single-nucleotide polymorphisms. These data support persistence of Fournol-related ancestry in southwestern Europe throughout the LGM.

abstract: Active control over optical nonlinearity in solid-state systems is central to unlocking exotic many-body phenomena and photonic devices. While exciton-polaritons in transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) offer a promising platform, their practical utility is impeded by fixed interactions and a trade-off between nonlinearity and oscillator strength. Here, we report electrically tunable dipolar polaritons in a dual-gated bilayer MoS2 microcavity, demonstrating in situ reshaping of the dispersion and modulation of the light-matter coupling strength via the quantum-confined Stark effect. Crucially, this electrical control yields a seven-fold enhancement of the polariton-polariton interaction strength. This enhancement arises from the combined tuning of the effective exciton-exciton interaction and the excitonic Hopfield coefficient. In addition, electrostatic doping provides an independent knob to continuously drive a strong-to-weak coupling crossover. Our findings establish dual-gated TMD homobilayer as a versatile platform for on-chip, dynamically reconfigurable nonlinear light-matter physics.

abstract: In simple microbial populations, the fitness effects of selected mutations are typically assumed to be constant, regardless of mutant frequency. This assumption underpins predictions about evolutionary dynamics, epistasis, and the maintenance of genetic diversity. Here, we systematically test this assumption using beneficial mutations from early generations of the Escherichia coli long-term evolution experiment (LTEE). Using flow cytometry-based competition assays, we find that frequency-dependent fitness effects are the norm rather than the exception, occurring in ∼80% of strain pairs tested. Most competitions exhibit negative frequency dependence, where fitness advantages decline as mutant frequency increases. We demonstrate that the strength of frequency dependence is predictable from invasion fitness measurements, which explain approximately half of the biological variation in frequency-dependent slopes. We also observe violations of fitness transitivity in several strain combinations, indicating that competitive outcomes cannot always be predicted from fitness measured against a single reference strain. High-resolution measurements reveal that frequency dependence changes substantially within the growth cycle, with the net per-cycle effect reflecting the balance of opposing dynamics at different growth phases. Our results demonstrate that, even in a model system designed to minimize ecological complexity, subtle interactions between closely related genotypes create frequency-dependent selection that can fundamentally alter evolutionary trajectories.

abstract: Tactile perception systems based on flexible pressure sensors are indispensable for humanoid robots to perform dexterous manipulation, compliant interaction, and operation in visually challenging environments. Although strategies relying on surface or spatial microstructure engineering have improved sensor performance, the long-standing trade-off among sensitivity, sensing range, and linearity continues to hinder their practical deployment. Inspired by the gradient distribution of mechanoreceptors in human fingertip skin, we report a gradient-interlayer-based flexible iontronic pressure sensor (GriFIPS) in which a single direct-ink-written elastomeric mesh-like interlayer, with a centrifugal increase in aperture size, is placed between the soft electrode and an ionic hydrogel layer. Operating upstream of the functional layer, the mesh enables progressive, stage-wise contact under increasing load and decouples macroscopic contact-area evolution from the microscopic interfacial response. The sensor simultaneously achieves a sensitivity of 175.9 kPa-1, a linear sensing range up to 360 kPa with a coefficient of determination of 0.997, a low detection limit of about 2.1 Pa, and a response time of about 25 ms, while remaining stable over 6000 loading cycles and 2000 cycles of 50% tensile strain. Building on this single-channel device, we further extend the architecture into a 3-axis gradient-interlayer-based flexible iontronic force sensor (3-axis GriFIFS) capable of resolving triaxial forces and surface textures. When integrated onto a dexterous robotic hand and combined with a temporal convolutional network, the sensors support tactile object recognition, fabric texture discrimination, human-robot interaction, and tactile-guided assembly, offering a generalizable route to tactile sensing for embodied intelligence.

abstract: The desert locust (Schistocerca gregaria) performs high-acceleration jumps within milliseconds, relying not only on powerful muscles and spring-loaded hindlegs, but also on precise tarsi-substrate interactions. Although the mechanics of jumping have been extensively studied, the mechanisms enabling rapid attachment and detachment remain poorly understood. Here, we characterize the frictional properties of hindleg tarsi under controlled low-speed contact conditions targeting selected loading features associated with jumping. We hypothesize that locusts coordinate tarsal cuticular structures with internal hemolymph pressure to modulate contact mechanics. Using high-speed videography, a suite of advanced microscopic techniques, biomechanical experiments, and biomimetic prototypes, we provide evidence that hemolymph pressure modulates tarsal stiffness and acts together with structural asymmetry to produce direction-dependent frictional responses. This interplay may contribute to adaptive friction tuning associated with jumping. Our findings advance the understanding of locust locomotor biomechanics and suggest design principles for robotic systems requiring rapid and controllable surface engagement.

abstract: DNA methylation is a fundamental epigenetic modification that regulates gene expression, cellular identity, and disease-associated regulatory programs. However, high-throughput single-cell DNA methylation technologies have been limited by DNA degradation, low CpG recovery, and the poor scalability of bisulfite-based methods. Here, we present scEM-seq, a droplet-based single-cell enzymatic methylome sequencing method that integrates barcode ligation within a single emulsification step, followed by postemulsion cytosine-to-uracil conversion. This design substantially reduces DNA loss and enables robust profiling of tens of thousands of single cells per experiment. scEM-seq generates high-quality single-cell methylomes with moderately improved CpG coverage and balanced read utilization compared with other droplet-based microfluidic methods. Applied to peripheral blood mononuclear cells, scEM-seq accurately resolves major immune lineages, and in prostate cancer tissues, it reveals diverse malignant cell states and patient-specific epigenetic and copy number architectures. scEM-seq enables scalable single-cell dissection of epigenetic heterogeneity across diverse biological and disease contexts, broadening the scope of DNA methylation-based studies into cellular regulation and disease.

abstract: CD8+ T cells, as the most important cytolytic cells in adaptive immunity, can differentiate into distinct subpopulations with specific functions and fates. During this process, CD8+ T cells exhibit substantial plasticity in their differentiation trajectory. Notably, epigenetic regulation has emerged as a pivotal mechanism to govern T cell fate decisions. In this study, we demonstrate that the histone methyltransferase NSD2 critically regulates CD8+ T cell differentiation during acute viral infection. While NSD2 deficiency enhances the early expansion of activated CD8+ T cells, it severely compromises their survival fitness during the contraction phase, leading to a disproportionate collapse of the antigen-specific pool and limiting the establishment of robust long-lived memory. Mechanistically, this defect is driven by the disruption of the H3K36me2-Zbtb20 regulatory axis. Furthermore, we show that in the absence of NSD2, CD8+ T cells in tumor exhibit an increased proportion but dysfunctional resident memory T cell phenotype. Collectively, our findings highlight a critical role for NSD2 in providing more mechanistic insights into how epigenetic mechanisms fine-tune T cell differentiation.

abstract: Liver fibrosis is a severe complication of diverse chronic liver diseases characterized by a dysregulated hepatic microenvironment, and effective clinical therapeutic strategies for this condition remain lacking to date. Chimeric antigen receptor macrophages (CAR-Ms) hold considerable therapeutic potential for liver fibrosis via antigen-specific recognition and efferocytotic activity, yet their clinical translation is largely hindered by the sophisticated ex vivo preparation procedures. Herein, we report an in situ CAR-M engineering strategy that uses a phosphatidylserine (PS)-incorporated, macrophage-targeted lipid nanoparticle (LNP) for the codelivery of CAR messenger RNA (mRNA) and Cas9 mRNA in vivo. Our findings demonstrate that this engineered LNP achieves efficient targeting of liver-resident macrophages. Transfection with fibroblast activation protein α (FAPα)-CAR mRNA equips macrophages with the capacity to specifically target activated hepatic stellate cells (aHSCs), whereas Cas9-mediated follistatin-like protein 1 (FSTL-1) gene editing enhances the efferocytotic function of macrophages in liver tissues. Consequently, functional CAR-Ms are generated in situ, which elicits robust antifibrotic effects, including reduced collagen deposition, restored sinusoidal architecture and enhanced immune-mediated antifibrotic activity. Collectively, our customized LNP-mediated in situ engineering of liver macrophages into CAR-Ms enables precise antifibrotic intervention for liver fibrosis and circumvents the cumbersome ex vivo CAR-M preparation process.

abstract: Interferon-λ (IFN-λ, type III IFN) mediates antiviral immunity at anatomic barriers, including the maternal-fetal interface. To investigate the effects of IFN-λ during congenital Zika virus (ZIKV) infection, we infected mice lacking the IFN-αβ receptor (Ifnar1-/-) or both the IFN-αβ and IFN-λ receptors (Ifnar1-/-Ifnlr1-/-) at embryonic day 9 and found that loss of maternal IFN-λ signaling resulted in greater transplacental transmission, highlighting a protective effect of IFN-λ at the maternal-fetal interface. To investigate the spatial relationship between ZIKV infection and antiviral responses, we used HiPlex RNAscope on the entire gravid uterus and found that IFN-λ was expressed more proximal to the site of ZIKV infection in Ifnar1-/- dams compared to Ifnar1-/-Ifnlr1-/- dams. We performed immunophenotyping of the placenta and uterus by flow cytometry and found a decrease in dendritic cells and natural killer (NK) cells in the uterus of Ifnar1-/-Ifnlr1-/- dams compared to Ifnar1-/- dams, but NK cell depletion did not affect fetal infection. Using conditional knockout mice, we identified maternal dendritic cells as the key IFN-λ-responsive cell type mediating protection against ZIKV congenital infection. Together, our data support a model in which IFN-λ signaling to maternal dendritic cells increases dendritic cell accumulation in the uterus, which facilitates a protective antiviral response that restricts ZIKV congenital infection.

abstract: Categorization is crucial for survival, helping animals forage, navigate, and avoid predators-all tasks involving movement. Yet, dominant theories of category learning treat it as a purely cognitive or perceptual process. Here, we challenge this view by demonstrating that physical movement can enhance category learning-but selectively. Using immersive virtual reality, we found that performing large actions, such as swinging a lightsaber, substantially improved learning of categories requiring integration of multiple cues (e.g., distinguishing aggressive from noncancerous lesions), while having minimal impact on categories involving independent evaluation of features (e.g., sorting by color and shape). This selective enhancement reveals a previously unrecognized motor contribution to categorization and may explain why prior studies missed it, opening avenues for optimizing training in critical categorization tasks.

abstract: The human placenta is essential for pregnancy, yet the dynamic regulation of its DNA methylome during development remains poorly understood. To address this, we generated a single base-resolution DNA methylation atlas of human placental trophoblasts across gestation. We identified a lineage-specific methylation program established immediately after implantation, followed by gestational age-dependent methylation accumulation. This program acted as a developmental barrier that coordinated placental maturation and immune homeostasis. By integrating histone modifications and functional perturbations, we revealed a temporal dynamic between H3K27me3 and DNA methylation that silenced proinflammatory loci and a switch from H3K9me3 to DNA methylation at repeat elements to maintain genome stability. Aberrant methylation in preterm placentas underscored the physiological importance of methylation regulation. Using human trophoblast stem cells, we demonstrated that DNMT1 was critically required for maintaining trophoblast methylome integrity and self-renewal, while the DNMT3 family were equally essential for trophoblast survival. Overall, we established a placenta-specific epigenetic framework for human trophoblast development.

abstract: Placenta defects are one of the major causes of miscarriages, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. We demonstrate that trophoblast-specific depletion of the acetyltransferase Kat5, or introduction of acetylation-defective mutants Kat5-Q377E G380E and Kat5-Y47A, induces severe chromosomal instability (CIN) during trophoblast cells division, leading to embryonic lethality. Moreover, mutation of a key lysine acetyltransferase 5 (KAT5) substrate, H2A.Z, via the introduction of H2az1-K5R K8R K12R K14R (which prevents H2A.Z acetylation), phenocopies the effects of KAT5 loss. Integrated RNA sequencing and CUT&Tag in mouse trophoblast stem cells reveal that KAT5, through H2A.Z acetylation, regulates transcription of key mitotic genes (Aurka, Aurkb, and Cenpa). We extend our finding to human trophoblast stem cells, demonstrating a conserved role for KAT5 in preventing CIN. Clinical analysis of placental villi from recurrent pregnancy loss patients with copy number variations revealed reduced expression of KAT5 and acetylated H2A.Z. This study demonstrates that the conserved KAT5-H2A.Z acetylation pathway safeguards chromosomal stability in trophoblast cells, supporting placenta development and successful pregnancy.

abstract: Biological flyers achieve ecological dominance not through flight alone, but by seamlessly integrating aerial locomotion with forceful physical interactions, including snatching prey, perching on irregular surfaces, and operating across diverse media. Translating this agility into aerial robotics demands reconciling a fundamental conflict: impulsive, high-force actions destabilize the flight platform. Here, we present a bio-inspired unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) equipped with a mechanically intelligent impulsive limb that resolves this tradeoff through physical decoupling. An asymmetric bistable impulse module delivers a 2.3-fold extension within 70 ms, while a soft-linkage architecture reduces the transmission of impulsive interaction forces to the airframe. For the tested seven-segment configuration, intrinsic geometric tolerance corresponds to a passive vertical accommodation range of approximately 70% of the fully deployed arm length, reducing the need for precise altitude regulation within the tested range. We demonstrate the system's multimodal capacity through dynamic in-flight snatching, energy-efficient perching, high-impact solid fracture, and cross-medium capture in viscous fluids, establishing a new paradigm for UAVs executing physically demanding tasks in complex environments.

abstract: Accurate and real-time monitoring of blood electrolyte composition, particularly sodium (Na+) and potassium (K+), is crucial for guiding intraoperative and postoperative decisions, as these ions regulate critical bodily functions such as cardiac rhythm and fluid balance. Current blood analysis relies on ex vivo blood sampling, which introduces substantial time delays and can be susceptible to inaccuracies caused by temperature fluctuations. To address these challenges, we report here a multiplexed and implantable fiber sensor (MIFS) capable of monitoring Na+ and K+ ions in real time directly in the bloodstream. MIFS integrates three parallel liquid metal channels with a multilayer surface-electrode architecture, which synergistically enhances sensitivity, minimizes sensing drift, ensures mechanical flexibility, and offers outstanding biocompatibility for vascular implantation. In vivo testing in rabbit models and validation in human blood samples demonstrate MIFS's superior sensing accuracy, real-time, and stable sensing in agreement with conventional ex vivo measurements. This work paves the way for real-time blood monitoring in clinical practice.

abstract: Chronic lung graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) remains difficult to treat, and broad immunosuppression increases infection risk. Single-cell profiling of bronchoalveolar lavage from bronchiolitis obliterans lesions revealed collapse of an epithelial nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) metabolic axis with pathogenic immune-epithelial remodeling, nominating NAD+ restoration as an entry point. Because free NAD+ is poorly cell-permeable and rapidly consumed, we engineered CaNAD+-PGB-LiP (CNAPL), a high-payload NAD+ nanomedicine enabling direct intracellular replenishment. In murine allo-HSCT GVHD, CNAPL improved clinical scores and survival, reduced vascular and epithelial injury, and curtailed hyperinflammation and effector overactivation across GVHD target organs. Unlike immunosuppression, CNAPL preserved phagocytosis, NK/NKT cell (natural killer/natural killer T cell) cytotoxicity, and T cell memory. In posttransplant influenza or Klebsiella infection, CNAPL maintained pathogen control without rekindling GVHD, decoupling inflammation control from infection susceptibility. This metabolism-centered, host-directed strategy restores immune-tissue homeostasis and provides a practical translational path for durable lung GVHD control with preserved antimicrobial defense.

abstract: Cancer cells must balance detoxification of reactive metabolic by-products while preserving redox homeostasis, but how this trade-off is managed remains unclear. The Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (KEAP1)-nuclear factor-erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) pathway, a key regulator of antioxidant defenses, is frequently hyperactivated in cancer. Formaldehyde, a genotoxic one-carbon by-product, is typically detoxified via glutathione (GSH), which is also essential for suppressing ferroptotic cell death. Here, we show that NRF2 promotes formaldehyde tolerance through up-regulation of the cystine transporter SLC7A11, enabling a protective mechanism that is largely independent of GSH, which remains necessary for ferroptosis resistance. In NRF2-active cells, formaldehyde reacts with cysteine to form a thiazolidine conjugate, and the combination of formaldehyde stress and SLC7A11 inhibition activates the integrated stress response, suppresses global protein synthesis, and markedly compromises cell viability. Together, these findings reveal that NRF2 coordinates ferroptosis resistance and formaldehyde tolerance, exposing a cancer vulnerability through combined inhibition of cystine uptake and GSH synthesis.

abstract: Sleep disruption in obstructive sleep apnea syndrome is characterized by frequent microarousals and reduced sleep depth, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we show that intermittent hypercapnic air (HA) induces time-locked microarousals, fragments sleep, reduces non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep depth, and diminishes rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. HA exposure activates glutamatergic neurons in the nucleus tract solitary (NTSVglut2), and their optogenetic or chemogenetic activation is sufficient to trigger arousal and impair sleep. Projection-specific activation reveals that NTSVglut2 projections to the paraventricular nucleus (PVN), parabrachial nucleus (PB), paraventricular thalamus, and locus coeruleus (LC) promote arousal, whereas projections to the PB and LC additionally reduce NREM sleep depth. Inhibition of NTSVglut2 projection to the PVN significantly postpones HA-induced arousal. NTSVglut2 terminals monosynaptically activate corticotropin-releasing hormone neurons in the PVN (PVNCRH), and inhibition of PVNCRH neurons or knockdown of Slc17a6 (encoding Vglut2), but not Crh, delays hypercapnia-induced arousal. These findings identify neural circuits underlying hypercapnia-induced microarousal and reduced sleep depth.

abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) pose a threat to human health. Although receptor specificity, polymerase adaptation, and airway tropism have been studied extensively, it remains unresolved how they combine to shape tropism in airway epithelia. Here, we show that avian IAVs infect ciliated and secretory cells but preferentially bind to ciliated cells because of higher apical α2,3-linked sialic acid levels. As replication levels are comparable between cell types, this translates into overall preference for ciliated cells. Human IAVs also preferentially bind to ciliated cells despite comparable α2,6-linked sialic acid abundance. Instead, they show higher viral RNA and protein levels in secretory cells, linked to their compatibility with human ANP32 proteins and modestly higher ANP32A/B expression in this cell type, resulting in equal infection levels across cell types. Our findings redefine IAV tropism in the human airway as a stage-resolved process shaped by the interplay between apical glycans, viral binding, polymerase cofactor compatibility, and cell-type-specific replication capacity, moving beyond receptor-centric models.

abstract: The phagosome is an immune organelle that integrates signals from diverse cargos to drive pathogen killing, tissue homeostasis, and antigen presentation. How this compartment coordinates such diverse functions remains incompletely understood. A comprehensive view of phagosomal composition across cell states and perturbations could accelerate insight into its regulation. Here, we establish PhagoID, a modular proximity labeling approach that enables in situ proteomic profiling of the phagosome lumen in living cells. Applying PhagoID to murine and human macrophages, we define conserved and species-specific phagosomal proteomes that include both canonical lysosomal components and unexpected contributors from nuclear, mitochondrial, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) compartments. Integrating these proteomes with 25 genome-scale CRISPR screens of phagosomal phenotypes, we identify a network of lumenal proteins that regulate cargo uptake, acidification, antigen presentation, and microbial control highlighting previously unrecognized phagosomal effectors. We next adapt PhagoID to profile the microbe-containing phagosome and compare the sterile bead-containing phagosome to the Escherichia coli-containing phagosome, demonstrating a modest E. coli signature of phagosome remodeling. Comparative analyses further reveal that loss of LAMP1 enhances recruitment of ER-derived proteins to the phagosome, whereas loss of TFEB minimally perturbs the lumenal proteome despite its role in lysosomal biogenesis. Last, cytokine stimulation remodels the phagosome lumen to enrich for proteins involved in antigen presentation and antimicrobial activity in response to type I and II interferons. These data demonstrate that PhagoID delivers a high-confidence, quantitative, and integrative map of the phagosome lumen, revealing previously unidentified axes of organellar communication and regulatory control in innate immunity.

abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is marked by unchecked expansion of undifferentiated myeloid cells. Although oncogenic fusions such as MLL-AF9 can initiate disease, the early steps of leukemogenesis and the role of cell-intrinsic regulators remain unclear. We previously showed that the Polycomb-associated factor Phf19 is required for hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) maintenance and state control in mice and that its loss (Phf19KO) impairs HSC function. To define Phf19's role in transformation, we expressed MLL-AF9 in Phf19KO hematopoietic cells and performed integrated multiomic analyses. Phf19 deletion promoted acquisition of stemlike features and reduced responsiveness to differentiation-inducing AML therapies. Molecular and functional consequences of Phf19 loss paralleled those observed in the datasets of patients with AML. From these data, we derived a prognostic signature-PHFScore-which reveals previously unrecognized AML survival-correlating genes that robustly stratify patients across distinct cellular origins and leukemogenic stages, underscoring Phf19's key role in AML biology and prognosis.

abstract: The metastatic outcome depends on the state of disseminated cancer cells (DCCs) leading to overt metastasis or undergoing dormancy. Before distant organ colonization, primary tumor microenvironment may shape the decision between proliferation and dormancy. Here, we identify lactic acid (LA), a highly abundant environmental metabolite at the primary site in prostate cancer (PCa), as a key inducer of dormant state. LA-uploading PCa cells undergo a proliferation delay, associated with stemness, therapy tolerance, and invasiveness through the nuclear receptor subfamily 2 group F member 1 (COUP-TF1/NR2F1) activation. These traits rely on LA-driven accumulation of lipid droplets (LDs), which serve as reservoirs of lipid-derived acetyl moieties essential for histone acetylation. Notably, the epigenetic reader BRD4 is essential for COUP-TF1 expression and for establishing and maintaining dormancy. In metastatic sites, where LA levels are low, dormant features are lost, allowing DCCs to support metastatic growth. Last, targeting LA-mediated LD formation or BRD4 activation prevents dormancy entry, reducing PCa cell adaptability and increasing vulnerability to antiproliferative therapies.

abstract: Aberrant activation of the RAS/RAF/mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase (MEK)/extracellular signal-regulated kinase pathway is a frequent cause of cancer. Allosteric MEK inhibitors block this pathway by binding RAF-MEK complexes to prevent activation of MEK by RAF. However, how MEK inhibitor potency varies across the three RAF isoforms remains poorly understood. We profiled seven allosteric MEK inhibitors and observed a notable hierarchy of sensitivity: All most potently inhibited CRAF-driven MEK activation while relatively sparing ARAF-driven activation. We identified point mutations in ARAF and CRAF proximate to the MEK inhibitor binding site that markedly altered inhibitor sensitivity. Using a rational design approach, we developed a more potent inhibitor of ARAF-driven MEK signaling, TWG-07-148. Our cryo-electron microscopy structure shows how this acrylamide-containing analog of MEK inhibitor trametinib covalently targets Cys514, a residue unique to ARAF. Our studies highlight the importance of the activating RAF isoform as a determinant of MEK inhibitor sensitivity and provide proof of concept for the development of MEK inhibitors that more effectively block ARAF-driven MEK signaling via covalent targeting of Cys514.

abstract: Over the past 5 to 7 million years, humans and chimpanzees have diverged in brain size, structure, and cognition despite high conservation of protein-coding genes. However, retroviral infections within host genomes have introduced numerous species-specific regulatory elements. Chimpanzees harbor lineage-specific PTERV1 endogenous retroviruses that are absent in humans, but their role in brain evolution has remained unclear. We performed an epigenomic analysis of PTERV1 insertions in chimpanzee neural organoids and found they are heavily DNA methylated, forming over 150 species-specific heterochromatin domains with the potential to influence gene regulation. We identified a chimpanzee-specific insertion on chromosome 19 that silences the long noncoding RNA LINC00662 through DNA methylation spreading. CRISPR-mediated deletion of this PTERV1 restored LINC00662 expression in chimpanzee induced pluripotent stem cells. We show that LINC00662, a human-specific transcript expressed during brain development, plays a role in neuronal maturation, axon outgrowth, and neural organoid development. These findings reveal a mechanism by which endogenous retroviral insertions contributed to human-chimpanzee brain divergence.

abstract: PrimPol-mediated fork repriming generates single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) gaps during DNA damage tolerance (DDT), which, if not properly repaired, can threaten genomic stability. PrimPol is a highly error-prone polymerase. Thus, PrimPol activity should be tightly regulated to fit into DDT and remain low during unstressed DNA replication. Human sex comb on midleg like-2 (SCML2), a Polycomb protein containing MBT repeats, has been identified as a component of the noncanonical PRC1 complex and a regulator of p53 and CHK1 stability. Here, we show that SCML2A is a suppressor of PrimPol. SCML2A directly binds two domains of PrimPol: Its RBR domain binds the C terminus of PrimPol, and its SAM domain binds the amino-terminal AEP domain, thereby inhibiting ssDNA-binding capacity of the AEP domain. SCML2 depletion leads to increased nascent DNA synthesis and accumulation of PrimPol-mediated ssDNA gaps under replication stress. SCML2 depletion also enhances PrimPol engagement during unstressed DNA replication, leading to subsequent accumulation of ssDNA gaps, which are filled by REV1/POLζ-mediated translesion synthesis (TLS) and RAD51-mediated template switching (TS). SCML2 depletion confers cellular hypersensitivity to RAD51 or REV1/POLζ inhibition, which is associated with increased accumulation of ssDNA gaps. Furthermore, CDK2 phosphorylates SCML2A at Ser267, which suppresses RBR-mediated PrimPol interaction. Cyclin E1 overexpression leads to CDK2-mediated SCML2A Ser267 hyperphosphorylation, which releases the inhibitory effect of SCML2A on PrimPol and subsequently induces ssDNA gap accumulation. Collectively, we identify SCML2A as a negative regulator of PrimPol.

abstract: SMCHD1 is a chromatin architectural protein linked to heterochromatin repression. Loss of function mutations of SMCHD1 cause facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy type 2 (FSHD2) through activation of the DUX4 transcription factor gene. However, it is unknown how SMCHD1 may regulate transcription independently of DUX4. Here, we show that SMCHD1 safeguards enhancer organization within the three-dimensional (3D) genome in human myoblasts. Loss of SMCHD1 leads to widespread gains in chromatin accessibility, aberrant transcription, and selective remodeling of myogenic transcription factor MYOD1 occupancy. Integrative analyses of histone modifications, chromatin accessibility, Hi-C looping, and enhancer-gene modeling reveal that SMCHD1 loss rewires the landscape of clustered enhancers and promotes the emergence of new networks of enhancer elements, termed MYOD1 enhancer nexuses. These structures are marked by increased enhancer connectivity, increased local 3D chromatin interactions, and coordinated activation of genes likely relevant for FSHD pathology. Our findings identify SMCHD1 as a key architectural constraint that suppresses hyperactive enhancer networks, thereby preserving transcriptional homeostasis in myoblasts.

abstract: Scalable interferometers lie at the heart of photonic quantum technologies, but their expansion has been fundamentally limited by optical losses that grow with circuit depth. Here, we introduce and experimentally demonstrate a measurement-induced architecture for multimode squeezed-light interferometers that overcomes this barrier. By shifting complexity from deep optical networks to programmable homodyne measurements, we realize effective transformations within a shallow, low-loss platform. We validate the principle with a six-mode device and extend it to a 400-mode interferometer, marking a leap in scale beyond conventional designs. Crucially, this strategy not only enables scalable squeezed light interferometry but also provides a powerful route to the generation of large-scale entangled states-a key requirement for quantum computing, simulation, and communication. Our results establish measurement-induced circuits as a practical pathway toward noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) applications and future demonstrations of quantum advantage.

abstract: Compared with conventional motors and servos, soft-actuated angular-motion devices are superior in environmental adaptability and human-robot interaction, yet they can only achieve active bidirectional angular motion by integrating antagonistic actuators or restriction modules. The integration of such components introduces deformation antagonism, compromises structural simplicity, and increases control complexity. Herein, we propose a spider-inspired centimeter-scale soft bidirectional robotic joint driven by a pair of synchronously controlled electrohydraulic actuators (EHAs). Specifically, the EHAs generate multiaxial strain, enabling the joint to bidirectionally rotate depending on its physical state, without introducing additional functional components or asynchronous controllers. Furthermore, the joint demonstrates (i) high-speed (forward: 2851° per second, reverse: 1934° per second) and wide-stroke (up to 156.8°) rotational performance, (ii) multimodal motion (e.g., self-unfolding, self-folding, and reciprocating swinging), (iii) continuous response (up to 40 hertz), and (iv) payload-bearing capability. Last, three joint-integrated devices validate its feasibility as a multifunctional, high-dynamic, and single-channel-controlled actuation component in diverse robotic applications. This work establishes a viable design framework for minimalist yet versatile bioinspired robots.

abstract: Start codon selection extensively regulates the cellular proteome and is implicated in cancer and other diseases. The eIF5-mimic proteins (5MPs: 5MP1/BZW2 and 5MP2/BZW2) restrict non-AUG start codon usage and thereby reprogram proteoform expression from mRNAs with alternative start sites, such as the oncogenic c-Myc. Here, using in extracto cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and biochemical assays, we report how 5MP represses translation dependent on the sequence context at start codons. Cryo-EM structures of 48S preinitiation complexes (PICs) reveal 5MP1 bound at the A site of the small ribosomal subunit. 5MPs act as initiation factors that stabilize an open PIC conformation, promoting mRNA scanning and inhibiting initiation at suboptimal start codons. We propose to designate 5MP as eIF1S (eukaryotic initiation factor 1 scanning). These findings reveal the structural basis for proteome modulation by 5MPs and may help correct dysregulated translation in disease.

abstract: DNA methylation dynamics shape hematopoietic differentiation and leukemogenesis, yet how the dioxygenase TET2-frequently mutated in myeloid malignancies-directs lineage-specific regulatory programs remains unclear. Here, we integrated DNA methylation, chromatin accessibility, three-dimensional (3D) genome architecture, transcriptional profiling, and TET2 chromatin occupancy to define TET2-dependent control of human myeloid commitment. We found that TET2-bound regulatory regions gain short- and long-range chromatin interactions and that a distinct subset of distal, enhancer-enriched sites undergoes TET2-driven demethylation and activation. Among these, we identified and functionally validated an AGO2 myeloid-specific intragenic enhancer that is frequently hypermethylated in patients with TET2-mutant acute myeloid leukemia. AGO2 expression stratifies patient survival, and AGO2 depletion abrogates leukemic engraftment in vivo. These findings uncover a TET2-AGO2 regulatory axis that integrates epigenetic remodeling, 3D genome reorganization, and leukemic fitness, and they highlight AGO2 as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target in myeloid leukemia.

abstract: Throughout eukaryotes, the synaptonemal complex (SC) is a supramolecular structure essential for meiotic chromosome dynamics and sexual reproduction. While metazoan SC proteins display substantial sequence divergence, the lack of functional analyses beyond bilaterian models has obscured a mechanistic understanding of SC evolution. Here, we report that the sea anemone Nematostella vectensis exhibits synapsis of homologous chromosomes in a classic zipper-like manner and expresses at least eight orthologs of 10 known vertebrate SC proteins. Unexpectedly, mutagenesis of the core SC components sycp1, syce2, and sycp3 resulted in divergent and sexually dimorphic phenotypes, indicating the functional diversification of these conserved factors. Combined, these findings challenge the assumption that the conservation of protein sequence or ultrastructure implies mechanistic homology.

abstract: El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is the primary source of climate predictability on seasonal and longer timescales over much of the globe, but predicting its phase beyond 9 months has remained challenging. Here, we leverage an underappreciated factor in ENSO forecasting: the substantial variation in forecast skill based on the ENSO phase at the time a forecast is issued. Our analysis of transitions between ENSO phases in a dynamical hindcast dataset demonstrates that this variation markedly exceeds intermodel differences in predictive capability. Forecasts initialized during La Niña conditions perform best, with three models correctly predicting transitions to El Niño 1 year in advance over 70% of the time. We present our findings in a simple framework that allows decision-makers to assess the likelihood of a forecast being correct on the basis of the current ENSO state. Applied effectively, these findings could improve long-lead ENSO forecasting strategies, enhancing global risk management.

abstract: Interleukin-21 receptor engagement initiates a Janus kinase-signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) signalling cascade that activates several STAT proteins that drive the germinal centre (GC) response. However, the relative effects of IL-21 on individual STAT proteins during the differentiation of T follicular helper (Tfh) cells and GC B cells has been difficult to distinguish. Here, we characterize a novel mutation in the interleukin-21 receptor (IL-21R EINS ) that creates a dominant defect in the activation of STAT1. Our findings provide evidence that IL-21-mediated activation of STAT1 has a non-redundant role in the differentiation of Tfh cells following T-dependent immunization. IL-21R EINS Tfh cells were even more impaired than Tfh cells genetically deficient in IL-21R, questioning our current understanding of the role of IL-21 derived from protein knockout mice. The observation that functional compensation fails in the presence of the IL-21R hypomorph provides insight into how underlying compensation can impact our interpretation of a complex biological system.

abstract: Nav1.7 voltage-gated sodium channels are strongly expressed in human primary pain-sensing neurons (nociceptors), and selective Nav1.7 inhibitors have been developed as possible therapeutic agents for treating pain, so far with disappointing clinical results. In contrast, a selective Nav1.8 channel inhibitor (suzetrigine) has had successful clinical trials. Because nociceptors express both Nav1.7 and Nav1.8 channels, it is of interest to compare effects of Nav1.7 and Nav1.8 inhibitors on the excitability of human nociceptors. To compare with previous results with suzetrigine, we characterized the effects of a selective Nav1.7 inhibitor, AM-2099, on action potential generation and repetitive firing of dissociated human dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons, studied at 37°C. Inhibition of Nav1.7 channels by 600 nM AM-2099 generally produced a substantial depolarizing shift of action potential threshold, an increase in rheobase, a decrease in action potential upstroke velocity, decrease in action potential peak, and prolongation of the refractory period. Compared to inhibition of Nav1.8 channels, inhibition of Nav1.7 channels had larger effects on threshold and maximal upstroke velocity, while action potential peak was reduced similarly by both. Nav1.8 inhibition produced much more dramatic reduction of repetitive firing than Nav1.7 inhibition. The results show that although the excitability of human DRG neurons is affected by inhibition of Nav1.7 channels, most notably by an increase in threshold and increase in refractory period, repetitive firing of the neurons in response to strong stimuli is little affected.

title: Morphology and ultrastructure of pharyngeal sense organs of Drosophila larvae.

abstract: This study provides a comprehensive ultrastructural analysis of the pharyngeal sensory system in Drosophila melanogaster larvae, focusing on the four major pharyngeal sense organs: the ventral pharyngeal sensilla (VPS), dorsal pharyngeal sensilla (DPS), dorsal pharyngeal organ (DPO), and posterior pharyngeal sensilla (PPS). Our analysis revealed 15 sensilla across these organs, comprising four mechanosensory, nine chemosensory, and two dual-function sensilla. We identified 35 Type I neurons (6 mechanosensory and 29 chemosensory) and 6 Type II neurons with putative chemosensory functions. Additional sensory structures, including papilla sensilla and chordotonal organs in the cephalopharyngeal region, were characterized. This detailed mapping and classification of pharyngeal sensory structures completes their structural characterization and provides a foundation for future anatomical and functional studies of sensory perception in insects. This work represents a significant step toward a complete analysis of the larval sensory system, providing new opportunities for investigating how an organism processes sensory information to navigate and interact with its environment.

title: The new paradox of women's health research.

author_details.name: Debarnot U
author_details.affiliation: Inter-University Laboratory of Human Movement (LIBM), Université Lyon 1, Lyon, France.

author_details.name: Fouré A
author_details.affiliation: Inter-University Laboratory of Human Movement (LIBM), Université Lyon 1, Lyon, France.

abstract: Women have long been underrepresented in biomedical research, prompting efforts to make research more sex inclusive. These advances are essential, but they can create an unintended tension when rigorous inclusion is interpreted as requiring extensive hormonal or reproductive characterization, even when such detail is unnecessary for the question being asked. We examine this paradox, in which standards intended to strengthen research on women may inadvertently make some studies involving females harder to pursue. We argue that characterization should match the claim a study is designed to support, and that funders, institutions and journals must provide the resources needed to make such rigor feasible. Methodological progress should ultimately broaden, not narrow, the evidence base needed to improve women's health.

title: Task-specific topographic organization of neural activity in the primate lateral prefrontal cortex
abstract: Neurons in the primate lateral prefrontal cortex (LPFC) flexibly adapt their activity to support diverse cognitive demands. Whether this flexibility is accompanied by changes in the spatial organization of neural population activity remains unclear. Here, we characterized the functional topography of LPFC neural activity in awake, behaving macaques performing three distinct cognitive tasks. Using chronically implanted multi-electrode arrays and topographic similarity analysis (TSA), we found that LPFC topographies were reproducible within tasks but less consistent across tasks. We then separated neural activity into task-tuned and trial-to-trial residual components to determine the basis of these effects. Task-tuned topographies mirrored the overall pattern: they were less consistent across than within tasks, whereas residual topographies remained comparatively stable across tasks. Moreover, task-tuned and residual topographies showed opposing patterns of consistencies. Within tasks, task-tuned topographies were more consistent than residual topographies; across tasks, the pattern reversed. This dissociation suggests a reproducible spatial organization of task-related activity that reconfigures across tasks. Nevertheless, task-tuned topographies remained significantly correlated across tasks, revealing a shared component of spatial organization. Across all three tasks, topographies exhibited a common spatial scale comparable to that of patterned afferent inputs to LPFC reported in previous anatomical tracing studies. Together, these findings suggest that LPFC functional organization combines a shared spatial scaffold with selective, task-dependent reconfiguration of task-tuned population activity.
author_corresponding_institution: Western Institute for Neuroscience, University of Western Ontario, London, ON, Canada; Robarts Research Institute, University of Western Ontario, London, ON, Ca

title: Opposing plasticity mechanisms enhance visual inputs that violate their context
abstract: To navigate complex environments, the mammalian visual system prioritizes informative inputs by comparing incoming sensory signals with learned contextual information. While this process is often conceptualized as a difference computation, cortical circuitry poses fundamental challenges: visual contextual feedback is predominantly amplifying, and whether inhibitory circuits support selective subtraction is unknown. Here, we show how layer 2/3 pyramidal neurons in mouse primary visual cortex can implement this comparison through plasticity that acts in opposite directions on responses to direct visual stimulation and contextual signals. To dissociate these components, we presented full images to mice or images where one quadrant was occluded, removing direct visual stimulation while preserving surrounding contextual information, and measured pyramidal cell responses to these stimuli before and after visual familiarization. After familiarization to non-occluded images, responses to direct visual inputs were selectively reduced, whereas contextual responses to occluded images strengthened. This strengthening generalized across natural scenes, allowing contextual inputs to also drive responses to novel occluded images and amplify responses to novel non-occluded images. A computational model reproduced these changes by weakening feedforward inputs and strengthening both feedforward-driven inhibition and contextual feedback in response to repeated pyramidal cell activity. This context-contrasting mechanism produced a conserved structure of responses to occluded and non-occluded images across mice and previously acquired monkey and human data. Together, these results suggest a mechanism for saliency assignment that exploits the compartmental organization of cortical pyramidal neurons: they learn the generalized statistical structure of familiar contexts, allowing selective amplification of improbable inputs or omissions.

title: Neuronal expression of E2F4DN restores adult neurogenesis in homozygous 5xFAD mice via TrkB signaling
abstract: Background: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is increasingly recognized as a disorder that disrupts brain plasticity long before extensive neuronal loss occurs, including early impairment of adult neurogenesis. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying these alterations remain poorly understood. Methods: Neuronal expression of E2F4 carrying the Thr249Ala/Thr251Ala mutation (E2F4DN) was achieved using an AAV.PHP.eB vector in the 5xFAD mouse model of AD. Neurogenic potential was assessed by immunohistochemistry and quantitative PCR (qPCR) targeting neurogenesis-associated markers. For in vitro experiments, neural stem cells (NSCs) isolated from the subventricular zone (SVZ) were exposed to conditioned media from primary cortical neurons expressing E2F4DN, with or without pharmacological inhibitors. NSC proliferation and differentiation were evaluated by immunocytochemistry and qPCR. Results: Neuronal expression of E2F4DN restored the proliferative and differentiation capacity of NSCs in 5xFAD mice both in vivo and in vitro. Pharmacological inhibition of TrkB signaling abolished the pro-neurogenic effects of E2F4DN-conditioned medium, whereas direct activation of TrkB in NSCs recapitulated these effects. Conclusions: These findings identify a mechanism by which neuronal dysfunction in AD compromises neurogenesis through impaired TrkB-mediated signaling. The results uncover a previously underappreciated paracrine communication between neurons and NSCs and highlight neuronal E2F4DN expression and TrkB modulation as promising therapeutic strategies to counteract early neurogenic deficits in AD.

title: Rationality self-organizes beyond subjective reasonings through the coupling of brain and internal organs
abstract: Psychological evidence shows that updating the rhythmic, internal body activity (IBA) based on the decision outcome is important to have a rational decision-making in a gambling task. However, the detailed mechanism how body guides rationality remains largely unclear. This paper provides a comprehensive theory that bridges the rhythmic coupling between the brain and internal organs and the rationality in a gambling decision-making task. Through our study of human binocular rivalry, we show that IBA creates the decision-switching (Sw) and -locking (Loc) phases based on the IBA parameters such as frequency, amplitude, and mean activity. When applied to a gambling task, the Sw-Loc structure creates directionality within the expected-value space of the decision options, wherein only options with expected values aligned with that directionality are stabilized. The stable direction can flip by changing how the IBA is updated in response to a decision outcome (e.g., taking a deeper or shallower breath). Using a theoretical analysis of a Brownian particle in a two-state heat bath, we show that the Sw region induces a large first-passage decision bias based on the random decision switching rate. Then, the Loc region acts as a rectifier, allowing only options with expected values aligned with the stable direction to persist. The rhythmic coupling of a brain and internal organs creates a directed medium that absorbs and separates external information, inducing biased decision-making through randomness.

title: Functional inertia reveals history-dependent organization of large-scale brain dynamics
abstract: The brain does not process the present in isolation. Its responses are shaped by the accumulating weight of prior states, yet existing frameworks treat large-scale brain dynamics as sequences of transient configurations, leaving the constraining influence of history implicit in how models are specified rather than measured directly. Here we define functional inertia as the rate of change of an accumulated latent state and make it measurable through an inertial state-space model. Applied to resting-state fMRI in 160 healthy controls and 151 individuals with schizophrenia, functional inertia organizes brain activity into three recurrent regimes, and patients redistribute their time across them in a way that tracks negative symptom severity. The same measure carries opposite consequences in the two groups, linked to better cognition in controls and to more severe symptoms in patients, because what inertia means depends on the accumulated configuration it operates from. The same contextual logic holds across circuits, where stronger inertia tracks greater symptom negative severity in integrative hubs and lower severity in sensory pathways, resolving the longstanding tension between reports of excessive rigidity and reports of excessive volatility in schizophrenia. These findings position functional inertia as a multilevel constraint on brain reorganization, and the accumulated past as a dimension of brain function that can be measured rather than assumed.

title: The Intermediate CA1 and CA3 Subfields of the Hippocampus Differentially Encode Social Recognition
abstract: Social recognition requires linking information about others to the spatial contexts in which they are encountered, a computation thought to engage the hippocampus. Although this process depends on coordinated activity across the hippocampal network, it remains unclear how specific subfields differentially contribute to social recognition. Of particular interest are the intermediate CA1 (iCA1) and CA3 (iCA3) subfields, which have both been shown to be causally involved in social recognition. Historically, the dense feed-forward projections from CA3 to CA1 led to the view that these subfields form a hierarchical circuit, with CA1 primarily integrating and refining computations from CA3. However, recent causal manipulations of the iCA1 and iCA3 have revealed distinct and separable contributions to approach and avoidance behavior, suggesting functional specialization across the subfields. This functional divergence suggests that iCA1 and iCA3 may differentially encode social recognition information. To test this possibility, we performed one-photon calcium imaging in freely behaving mice to record endogenous activity from the iCA1 and iCA3 during a novel behavioral paradigm that disentangles social identity from spatial position. Notably, we found that iCA3 neurons more robustly discriminated between novel and familiar conspecifics, while iCA1 neurons more strongly encoded spatial position. These results identify the iCA3 as a key locus for social novelty encoding and suggest distinct contributions of the iCA1 and iCA3 to social recognition.

title: Gait transition mechanism from quadrupedal to bipedal locomotion in the Japanese macaque based on inverted pendulum
abstract: The ability of non-human primates to transition from quadrupedal to bipedal locomotion offers critical insights into both the evolution of human bipedalism and the principles of complex motor control. While quadrupedal and bipedal gaits in non-human primates have been studied, the dynamic mechanisms underlying the transition between these gaits remain poorly understood. Japanese macaques trained to walk bipedally have been reported to utilize inverted pendulum dynamics to achieve efficient bipedal locomotion. Given the intrinsic instability of inverted pendulum systems, which can induce large changes in movement with minimal control input, we hypothesized that this mechanism also contributes to the gait transition. To test this, we developed a neuromusculoskeletal model of the Japanese macaque that integrates a detailed musculoskeletal structure with a physiologically inspired motor control system. Through forward dynamics simulations, we generated a variety of movement patterns by systematically parameterizing motor commands, including failed transitions that are difficult to capture experimentally. We then applied dynamical systems analysis using on an inverted pendulum model to examine the underlying principles of the transition process. Our results demonstrate that successful gait transitions depend on generating an inverted pendulum motion through appropriate control of the forward step length of one hindlimb. These findings provide mechanistic insights into how Japanese macaques coordinate their complex musculoskeletal systems to perform skilled, full-body movements in the gait transition, offering a deeper understanding of both advanced motor control and the evolution of human bipedalism.

title: Anterior hippocampal integration tracks the developmental emergence of flexible navigation through changing environments
abstract: Flexible memory depends on cognitive maps that integrate spatial relationships and guide behavior as environments change. The anterior hippocampus is well positioned to support integration across broad spatiotemporal scales, but its late maturation may constrain development of flexible, map-based navigation. Here, we tested whether hippocampal temporal autocorrelation, an index of neural activity stability over time, tracks the development of spatial integration in humans. In a large resting-state fMRI sample (N = 382; ages 5-34 years; 174 females, 208 males), temporal autocorrelation increased with age in anterior, but not posterior, hippocampus. This anterior-specific pattern was replicated in an independent task-based fMRI sample (N = 83; aged 6-12 years and adults; 41 females, 42 males), wherein we linked hippocampal autocorrelation to dissociable components of spatial behavior. The navigation task separated memory for object locations from the ability to update and generalize knowledge across rotations of the distal reference frame and to new objects. Although all age groups learned object locations, only older participants showed evidence that prior spatial structure supported performance as the environment changed across runs. Critically, hippocampal autocorrelation related to behavior only when spatial knowledge was used across runs, rather than improved through within-run feedback, with the clearest profile emerging in adults. In adults, anterior and posterior autocorrelation jointly predicted precise object-location memory, whereas anterior autocorrelation uniquely predicted efficient navigation trajectories. These findings identify anterior hippocampal temporal autocorrelation as a later-maturing computation that supports the transition from local spatial learning in childhood to flexible navigation through changing environments in adulthood.

title: From labels to latents: revealing state-dependent hippocampal computations and non-spatial replay with Jump Latent Variable Model
abstract: Neural activity is often interpreted by imposing external labels (e.g., position during locomotion) and decoding within that space (e.g. replay). While powerful, such supervision can mask structure in the data that do not correspond to the label. Unsupervised methods, in turn, often assume smooth latent dynamics and miss genuine discontinuities. We introduce a conceptually simple, computationally efficient latent variable model that infers both (i) the latent variables organizing population activity and (ii) whether their dynamics are continuous or fragmented in time. Fitting reduces to an expectation-maximization (EM) procedure that alternates two operations familiar to systems neuroscience - tuning-curve estimation and label decoding - without requiring external labels. Applied to rodent hippocampal recordings, our method identifies a continuity-fragmentation axis that characterizes population activity across sleep-wake brain states, modulated by cholinergic inputs. For a spatial navigation task, the model reveals distinct population patterns at the same physical position that supervised spatial decoding fails to detect. Moreover, the model enables replay analysis beyond spatial trajectories, and finds prevalent pre-play events associated with immobile and off-maze behaviors and post-task replay of locomotion. By not relying on externally imposed spatial labels, our approach exposes structure that supervised approaches obscure and provides a powerful tool for datasets lacking behavioral tracking.

title: Multi-timescale dynamics organize descending pain modulation
abstract: Descending pain-modulatory circuits must coordinate rapid nociceptive responses with slower changes in physiological state, yet how their activity is organized across time remains poorly understood. We investigated this question in physiologically identified pain-modulating neurons of the rostral ventromedial medulla (RVM). The RVM contains ON- and OFF-cells that exert descending control over spinal nociceptive transmission, regulating pain sensitivity and behaviors. By integrating neuronal recordings with probabilistic modeling, we show that unstimulated and stimulus-driven conditions give rise to distinct timescales of ON- and OFF-cell dynamics. During noxious stimulation, we find that population responses undergo rapid activation (<1 s) followed by superimposed slow (~ 100 s) and fast (<10 s) recovery dynamics. In the absence of stimulation, the same neurons exhibit slow quasi-periodic fluctuations in firing activity with a characteristic timescale of approximately five minutes. Gaussian-process models show that these slow dynamics are statistically predictable from past activity, indicating structured temporal organization beyond stimulus-evoked responses. Taken together, these results indicate that descending pain-control circuits exhibit structured dynamics encompassing rapid pain-related signaling and slower fluctuations consistent with ongoing physiological state.

title: Cortico-Hippocampal phase-amplitude coupling is a signature of learned audiovisual associations in humans
abstract: Phase-amplitude coupling (PAC) has been proposed as a neural mechanism for representing sequential information in memory, binding memories, coordinating activity across distributed brain regions, and parsing complex sensory inputs. Importantly, the frequencies contributing to PAC can vary flexibly across brain regions and cognitive states. Here, we asked whether the pattern of coupling across these dynamically varying frequencies can carry information about learned representations. To address this question, we used human intracranial recordings acquired before, during, and after an audiovisual associative learning task. We first identified the emergence of task-related theta- and gamma-band activity within cortico-hippocampal networks during learning and showed that theta-gamma PAC strength within these networks increased following learning. Importantly, PAC comodulograms contained association-specific information: learned associations could be decoded across hippocampal, temporal, and frontal networks during and after learning, with significantly greater decoding accuracy than that obtained from cue-only PAC before learning and from models trained on theta and gamma magnitude alone. This dissociation suggests that the associative information encoded in PAC comodulograms was not reducible to cue-evoked activity or to either of its constituent frequency bands taken independently. Finally, decoding accuracy of models trained on PAC post-learning was positively correlated with behavioral performance. Together, these findings suggest that PAC contains content-specific information in the human brain and identify it as an endogenous neural signature of audiovisual associative learning.

title: Confidence-modulated shared control for reliable intracortical BCI navigation in dynamic environments
abstract: Brain-computer interfaces enable people with paralysis to control neuroprosthetic devices, but reliable operation in dynamic environments remains limited by noise in decoded neural commands. We developed a confidence-modulated probabilistic shared-control framework that adaptively integrates the decoded neural commands with a probabilistic temporal prior to stabilize execution while preserving the directional structure of the decoded command. In two male macaques performing closed-loop tasks in complex environments, shared control nearly eliminated execution-level failures, while maintaining the directional structure of neural commands. Abrupt target changes revealed a limitation: temporal-history dependence transiently slowed responsiveness when recent movement history became inconsistent with the updated command, although this delay was not obligatory. Resetting the temporal prior removed the residual shared-control delay and restored performance, demonstrating a specific contribution of temporal history to the impairment. Here, we show that shared control improves the reliability of continuous intracortical brain-computer interfaces while revealing a trade-off between stabilization and responsiveness.
author_corresponding_institution: Laboratory for Neuro- and Psychophysiology, Department of Neurosciences, KU Leuven and the Leuven Brain Institute, Leuven, Belgium.

title: A multiverse analysis of stomach-brain coupling in humans
abstract: The gastric-brain axis is a burgeoning field of neuroscience; however, inferences from neuroimaging research are often constrained by the high dimensionality of methodological choices potentially leading to disparate outcomes. This study addresses such concerns by performing a multiverse analysis of gastric-brain coupling in humans. We systematically evaluated 5,184 unique analytic pipelines using electroencephalography (EEG) and electrogastrography (EGG) data to survey the methodological sensitivity of gastric-brain coupling. Our results reveal that whilst analytic decisions influence the magnitude of observed coupling, at the group level the phenomenon remains relatively consistent across the parameter space. High inter-individual variance can, however, be observed. Coupling was observed in the alpha, theta, and beta bands, with the latter two bands showing coupling at the largest number of electrodes. Coupling across frequency bands was primarily seen in medial electrodes, with some left lateral coupling also observed. Overall, these findings suggest that EEG-EGG based measurement of gastric-brain coupling is likely to be consistent across a significant range of plausible analytic pipelines at the group-level in healthy participants, providing useful context for future studies.

title: Emergence of long- and short-range functional connectivity parallels the development of neonatal brain gradients
abstract: The emergence of macroscale brain organisation during the perinatal period represents a critical but poorly understood process. Using resting-state fMRI in 325 term-born neonates within the first month of postnatal life, we characterised the early emergence of macroscale brain organisation with functional gradients. Neonatal functional gradients showed a distinct pattern compared with the canonical adult gradients: the principal gradient in neonates, separating the primary sensorimotor and visual networks, broadly corresponded to the secondary gradient in adults (sensorimotor-visual axis), whereas the secondary gradient in neonates, spanning from primary visual to association networks, aligned with the principal gradient in adults (sensorimotor-association axis). We found that the perinatal emergence of distance-dependent functional connectivity paralleled the development of neonatal functional gradients, potentially underlying the protracted development of the sensorimotor-association hierarchy in neonates. Regions with a higher proportion of short-range functional connectivity were more strongly associated with the sensorimotor-visual gradient in neonates, while regions with a greater proportion of middle- to long-range functional connectivity were more strongly associated with the sensorimotor-association hierarchy. Together, these findings highlight the critical role of short- and long-range functional connectivity, which showed a close correspondence with neonatal macroscale functional hierarchy. Disruptions to this process during the perinatal period may alter macroscale brain organisation and contribute to the early origins of neurodevelopmental conditions.

title: Bandpass corticospinal transmission during repetitive TMS revealed by motor unit recordings
abstract: We employed a noninvasive high-density surface electromyography (HDsEMG) framework to track spinal motor neuron responses during repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) and characterize the transmission of rhythmic corticospinal inputs to the alpha motor neuron pool. Eleven healthy individuals performed isometric thumb flexion while rTMS was delivered over the motor cortex at five frequencies (5, 10, 20, 30, and 50 Hz) and three subthreshold intensities (50%, 60%, and 70% of resting motor threshold). Motor units were decomposed from HDsEMG before stimulation and tracked during rTMS, allowing input-output coupling between the stimulation train and individual motor unit and cumulative spike train activity to be quantified. rTMS inputs were significantly transmitted at all frequencies except 5 Hz, indicating widespread corticospinal coupling. At the motor neuron population level, corticospinal transmission preserved the spectral components of the rTMS input and exhibited intensity-dependent increases in coupling strength, consistent with approximately linear transmission. The estimated corticospinal transmission exhibited a bandpass-like profile, with transmission between 20 and 50 Hz significantly greater than at lower and higher frequency ranges. Transmitted rTMS inputs induced frequency-specific increases in the common synaptic input to motor neurons, with oscillations at the stimulation frequency significantly enhanced during rTMS compared with before stimulation. Computational simulations reproduced this frequency selectivity only when excitatory and inhibitory postsynaptic inputs were combined. These findings reveal frequency-selective, approximately linear corticospinal transmission during rTMS and establish a noninvasive framework for assessing corticospinal function, with potential application as a tool for tracking changes associated with neurological disease and response to neurorehabilitation.

title: Hippocampus-evoked polysynaptic responses in the medial prefrontal cortex are attenuated in aged rats.
abstract: The hippocampus-medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) circuit is critical for spatial working-memory and decision-making. Age-associated changes to these functions are attributed to alterations in this circuit, although the exact mechanisms remain unclear. These regions are connected via monosynaptic projections from the intermediate (iHC) and ventral (vHC) hippocampus to the mPFC. We examined the functional connection between these regions in young (10-12 months) and aged (23-26 months) male F344 rats. High-density Neuropixels probes were used to record mPFC field excitatory postsynaptic potentials (fEPSPs) and single-unit responses to electrical stimulation of iHC and vHC. We observed that hippocampal stimulation evoked both short-latency (5-35 ms) monosynaptic and long-latency (35-100 ms) polysynaptic responses across the dorsoventral mPFC axis. Monosynaptic fEPSP amplitude increased with mPFC depth for iHC and vHC stimulation sites. Age did not affect hippocampal-prefrontal monosynaptic transmission as measured by fEPSP amplitude and evoked neural firing. In contrast, polysynaptic responses, reflecting local mPFC circuit recruitment, were larger than monosynaptic responses in young but not aged rats. Polysynaptic fEPSPs increased toward ventral mPFC in young but not aged rats, and polysynaptic evoked firing was reduced with age, most prominently at ventral mPFC depths. Our findings demonstrate that aging preserves the functional direct synaptic transmission but impairs polysynaptic recruitment of local mPFC circuits, with ventral mPFC showing particular vulnerability. These circuit-level deficits may contribute to age-related impairments in cognitive flexibility.

title: Instrumental-Motor Transfer: The Relative Value of Competing Movement Goals Modulates Implicit Motor Learning
abstract: Motor learning depends on the integration of several, often competing signals, including reward and punishment (which guide learning the value of actions via reinforcement learning) and sensorimotor errors (which refine the execution of actions via motor adaptation). If and how these signals interact remains controversial. Here we show that the learned value of actions can fundamentally alter how the motor adaptation system learns from errors. Human participants learned the reward values of different movement targets and subsequently underwent implicit motor learning at those targets. Across several experiments, motor learning was robustly attenuated when it brought the limb toward previously punished movement directions. Moreover, learning was globally suppressed when punished targets were themselves the movement goal. Learning was not reciprocally enhanced when it pushed movements toward previously rewarded directions, revealing a valence asymmetry. Using computational modeling, we present a novel mechanism to explain our effects: the motor adaptation system tunes its error sensitivity according to a movement-specific value gradient. Our findings point to a close interaction between reinforcement learning and motor memory -- a kind of "instrumental-motor transfer" -- where learned action values modulate error-based motor adaptation.

title: Increased CA3 burst activity in Doc2α and Syt7 knockout mice
abstract: The hippocampal CA3 subfield is central to associative learning and memory consolidation. CA3 pyramidal neurons execute these functions by generating hypersynchronous bursts that feed forward to the CA1. Extensive recurrent collateral connections within CA3 are crucial for the generation of this burst activity. Double C2 domain-containing protein  (Doc2) and synaptotagmin 7 (Syt7) are high-affinity calcium sensors implicated in asynchronous release (AR) of neurotransmitter and in the exocytosis of dense-core vesicles (DCVs). Additionally, Doc2 is a sensor for miniature neurotransmission, whereas Syt7 is involved in synaptic facilitation and SV replenishment. Both Doc2 and Syt7 are expressed in the hippocampus, but their potential roles in spontaneously bursting networks, like CA3, remain unanswered. Using whole-cell recordings at near physiological conditions (33-34 {degrees}C and 1.2 mM Ca2+) in acute hippocampal slices obtained from juvenile (P15-21) KO mice lacking Doc2, Syt7, or both proteins, we report no changes in spontaneous inhibitory or excitatory postsynaptic current frequency or amplitude in CA1 pyramidal neurons. However, there was a marked increase in burst activity, originating in CA3, in all three KO conditions; this was not due to changes in AR or the intrinsic properties of CA3 pyramidal neurons. We propose that this novel burst phenotype in Doc2- and Syt7-KO mice is unrelated to changes in neurotransmitter release but might be mediated by changes in neuropeptide release from DCVs in the CA3 subfield, or along upstream pathways. Regardless of the underlying mechanisms, this work reveals that both Doc2 and Syt7 act to regulate network activity.

title: Neurexin mediates neuropeptide release from cholinergic motor neurons through dense-core vesicle localization
abstract: Neurexins are critical synaptic cell adhesion molecules that play many roles in modulating neurotransmitter release and synaptic function, and are high-confidence risk genes for neurodevelopmental conditions such as autism. Understanding the function of the neurexin superfamily has been challenging in mammalian systems that have 3 genes (NRXN1-3) that encode 2-3 major isoforms, which undergo extensive alternative splicing and generate thousands of transcripts. In contrast to mammals, C. elegans has a single gene, nrx-1, encoding only long alpha and short gamma isoforms. Neurexins canonically regulate synapse morphology and function in a neuron- and context-specific manner, through mechanisms related to release of chemical neurotransmitters and receptors.
