abstract: Excessive weight gain after kidney transplantation adversely affects patient and graft outcomes. Machine Learning has been increasingly used to improve risk prediction across a range of transplant-related outcomes, yet its application to post-transplant weight trajectories remains unexplored. This study is the first to evaluate the feasibility of using Machine Learning algorithms to identify predictors of weight gain after kidney transplantation. This retrospective cohort study analyzed 374 adult kidney transplant recipients. We developed an Elastic Net regression model with 10-fold cross-validation to predict body weight variation at 12 months post-transplant. The analysis screened a comprehensive set of demographic and clinical variables, including recipient characteristics, donor type, dialysis duration, and pre-transplant hypertension, to identify predictors within the training (75%) and testing (25%) datasets. Mean weight gain was 4.0 ± 7.4 kg. The Elastic Net model retained four predictors in the final model: female sex, deceased donor source, age, and pre-transplant body mass index. However, the model demonstrated limited predictive performance (R2 = 0.10; Mean Absolute Error = 8.7%), indicating that baseline variables explain only a small fraction of the observed variability in weight change. This pioneering study establishes an analytical benchmark and reveals the informational limits of standard clinical datasets for predicting post-transplant weight gain. While Machine Learning application is feasible, current demographic and clinical variables are insufficient for precise individual prediction. Future models must integrate more granular behavioral and pharmacological data to achieve clinically actionable risk stratification.

abstract: Asprosin a glucogenic adipokine associated with insulin resistance, has been found to be elevated in the plasma of women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). Emerging evidence indicates that it can serve as a promising biomarker for the diagnosis of GDM during the second trimester. However, its utility in the first trimester has not yet been investigated. Therefore, the present study aimed to establish first-trimester reference ranges for plasma asprosin and to evaluate its predictive performance for the subsequent development of GDM. In this prospective cohort study, low-risk women with singleton pregnancies at 10-14 weeks of gestation were consecutively enrolled. Participants with pregestational diabetes were excluded. Baseline clinical characteristics were documented, and blood samples were obtained for the measurement of plasma asprosin concentrations. The diagnosis of GDM at 24-28 weeks of gestation was established using the two-step screening approach. Among the 302 participants, 98 (32.5%) developed GDM. Asprosin concentrations did not differ significantly across gestational ages between 10 and 14 weeks. However, asprosin levels increased significantly with maternal BMI (p < 0.001), demonstrating a quadratic relationship. A first-trimester reference range for plasma asprosin was established. Nevertheless, first-trimester asprosin showed poor predictive performance for subsequent GDM (AUC = 0.516), whereas maternal BMI and age showed modest predictive ability. First, a reference range for first-trimester asprosin was established, which may serve as a valuable benchmark for future investigations examining various aspects of diabetes in pregnancy. Second, first-trimester asprosin concentrations did not discriminate between women who subsequently developed GDM and those who did not.

abstract: This study aimed to assess global stakeholder preferences for key attributes of point-of-care (POC) HIV Nucleic Acid Amplification Tests (NAAT), with the aim of informing product development to support progress toward UNAIDS 95-95-95 targets. A web-based conjoint survey was conducted in August through November 2024 among HIV clinicians, laboratory professionals, and researchers. Participants were asked to evaluate hypothetical POC HIV NAAT profiles varying by six attributes: sensitivity / limit of detection (LOD), sample-collection method, turnaround time (TAT), result format, price, and power source. Relative importance and part-worth utilities were calculated to assess trade-offs in decision-making. One hundred three respondents from 33 countries, primarily in Africa (75%), completed the survey. The relative importance placed on the attributes in the conjoint task varied based on the setting. In community and home-based settings, participants prioritized fingerstick sample collection (25.90%) and faster TATs (28.8%), even at the expense of sensitivity (15.70%). By contrast, respondents from hospitals and health centers valued tests with high sensitivity (42.6%, 40.9%) and faster TATs (31.5%, 22.6%). Across all respondents, price (7.0%), result format (3.30%), and power source (7.25%) were less influential. Stakeholders were willing to make trade-offs among desirable attributes, prioritizing rapid turnaround time, strong sensitivity, and fingerstick sampling over affordability, power requirements, and result format in the conjoint task. These preferences vary by level of care and by use case, underscoring the importance of aligning product features with contextual needs. Engaging stakeholders early in the design process is critical to ensure new POC HIV NAAT technologies are both acceptable and scalable in low-resource settings.

abstract: Thermodynamic characterization of biomolecular interactions is essential for understanding the enthalpic and entropic driving forces of molecular recognition, but established label-free techniques are limited either by bulk refractive-index sensitivity or by the lengthy thermal equilibration required to suppress it. Here, we used focal molography to investigate the temperature-dependent binding of the protein kinase A regulatory subunit (PKA-R) to cyclic AMP (cAMP) derivatives and to derive apparent thermodynamic signatures from kinetic measurements. We first validated the diffractometric readout under conditions that challenge refractometric sensors: the coherent mass density channel strongly suppressed temperature-induced bulk refractive-index effects and resolved binding in 50% human serum despite measurable non-specific adsorption, reducing the need for lengthy equilibration and buffer matching. We then combined focal molography with DNA-directed immobilization (DDI), allowing five cAMP derivatives to be presented in parallel on the same multiplexed chip and followed across five temperatures. This format yielded distinct, internally consistent apparent thermodynamic fingerprints for each derivative, separating ligands with similar affinities by their enthalpic and entropic contributions. Together, these results establish focal molography with DDI as a multiplexed workflow for comparative thermodynamic fingerprinting of biomolecular interactions at higher throughput.

abstract: Host-parasite coevolution is expected to generate strong selection for resistance and infectivity that has the potential to erode genetic variation. Despite this, natural populations often retain extensive genetic variation in these traits. Genotype-by-genotype interactions on fitness can generate negative frequency-dependent selection, which helps maintain this variation by preventing any host or pathogen genotype from retaining a permanent advantage. Because these interactions place genetic variance in the interaction term rather than in additive differences among hosts or pathogens, that variance is masked from directional selection and can remain 'cryptic'. Here we combine coevolutionary modelling with large‑scale experimental infection assays to quantify how host-pathogen interactions structure fitness variance in a vertically transmitted virus system, Drosophila melanogaster and sigma virus. Simulations show that coevolution typically erodes additive genetic variance in host and pathogen fitness, concentrating variance in host-virus interaction terms. Consistent with these predictions, experiments spanning 90 host-virus genotype combinations reveal that transmission, viral load, and virulence are overwhelmingly governed by host-virus genetic interactions rather than host or virus main effects. As a result, neither host resistance alleles nor viral genotypes confer consistently higher fitness across genetic backgrounds. Interactions tend to be sex‑specific, further limiting heritable fitness variation. Our results demonstrate that coevolution can substantially mask heritable genetic variation from directional selection by rendering fitness context-dependent. This extensive cryptic genetic variation may be revealed either when ecological or evolutionary conditions shift, or when the process of coevolution itself alters the direction of selection. This demonstrates the need to account for genotype-specific interactions when forecasting evolutionary responses.

abstract: Inflammation underlies numerous pathological conditions, driving the need for safe and effective anti-inflammatory agents. Anti-inflammatory peptides (AIPs) are promising therapeutics due to their specificity, efficacy, and safety. This study evaluated the cationic antimicrobial peptide IL15.3 for anti-inflammatory activity and cytocompatibility in vitro. IL15.3 demonstrated low cytotoxicity in MTT assays using RAW 264.7 macrophages, normal human dermal fibroblasts (NHDF), and HaCaT keratinocytes. In LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 cells, IL15.3 significantly reduced nitric oxide (NO) production and reactive oxygen species (ROS) in a dose-dependent manner without affecting cell viability. qRT-PCR analysis revealed significant suppression of iNOS, COX-2, TNF-α, and IL-6 mRNA expression, alongside downregulation of NF-κB, JNK, STAT1, and STAT3, and a reciprocal shift in Keap1/Nrf2 expression suggestive of possible antioxidant pathway activation. Label-free proteomic profiling identified 5,191 proteins, revealing a multi-modal mechanism of action. IL15.3 treatment exclusively induced 4 anti-inflammatory proteins (ISG15, PEX14, TNIP3, PR) and upregulated negative regulators NRG1, DAB2IP, IL-18BP and SOCS5. Critically, IL15.3 suppressed key pro-inflammatory mediators including IKKβ, JAK1, JAK3, JNK, and IL-1RAcP, demonstrating comprehensive modulation of NF-κB, JAK/STAT, and MAPK pathways. In silico molecular docking further predicted potential interactions of IL15.3 with iNOS and the Keap1 Kelch domain, offering preliminary structural insight consistent with its putative dual anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activity. Together, these findings indicate that IL15.3 exhibits potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activity through multiple mechanisms in LPS-stimulated macrophages at transcriptional and proteomic levels. The coordinated upregulation of negative regulators and suppression of central inflammatory mediators collectively suggest that IL15.3 may represent a promising therapeutic candidate for inflammatory disorders.

abstract: Mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) remains a major public health challenge, particularly in low-income countries. Previous studies conducted in Ethiopia were largely limited to single health facilities and did not adequately assess important predictors, including maternal viral load, paternal enrollment in antiretroviral therapy (ART), and breastfeeding duration. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the incidence and predictors of MTCT of HIV among HIV-exposed infants in public general hospitals of Tigray, Ethiopia. Hospital-based retrospective cohort study on 485 randomly selected HIV exposed infants attending in public General Hospitals was conducted. All HIV exposed infants attending in public general hospitals of Tigray were the source of population. Data were entered into Epidata version 4.6.1 and exported to SPSS version 23 for analysis. Binary logistic regression model was used and variables at p-value < 0.25 in bivariate analysis were entered into a multivariable logistic regression analysis to examine the predictors of mother-to-child transmission of HIV. Level of significance was declared at p-value <0.05. A total of 444(91.5%) records were included in the analysis. At the end of follow up, 17 (3.8%) (95% CI: 2.3%-5.8%) of the HIV exposed infants became HIV positive. Poor infant adherence (AOR: 5.6; 95% CI: 1.02-30.2), father not enrolled to ART (AOR: 4.4; 95% CI: 1.2-16.7), age of infant at enrolment >6 weeks (AOR: 4.4; 95% CI: 1.2-17.0), mothers enrolled to PMTCT during labor and delivery or after (AOR: 7.9; 95% CI: 1.4-44.7) and mothers on advanced WHO clinical stage at base line(AOR: 4.2; 95% CI: 1.02-17.89) were significantly associated with mother-to-child transmission of HIV. In this study MTCT of HIV is still high. Poor adherence of infant for PMTCT, HIV positive father not enrolled to ART, infant age > 6 weeks at enrollment, mothers enrolled to PMTCT during labor and delivery or after and mothers on advanced WHO clinical stage were predictors of mother to child transmission of HIV.

abstract: For ten years, nintedanib and pirfenidone have been the only approved therapies for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), with nintedanib subsequently also approved for progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF). Previous studies demonstrate low antifibrotic (AF) uptake, but differences by site-of-care and AF uptake after seminal trials (IPF: INPULSIS/ASCEND; PPF: INBUILD) are not well characterized. We evaluated temporal trends in IPF and PPF diagnosis and AF use at academic (AC) versus non-academic (NonAC) centers. Using the U.S. TriNetX Collaborative Network, we compared IPF and PPF incidence, prevalence, and AF use by center type using linear regression across post-trial and post-FDA-approval windows (IPF: 2015-2017, 2015-2024; PPF: 2020-2022, 2020-2024). Slope differences (Δslope) were calculated as AC minus NonAC annual slopes; therefore, positive values indicate faster increases at ACs, whereas negative values indicate faster increases at NonACs. Across both periods, IPF prevalence increased more rapidly at NonACs, while AF use was higher at ACs (2024: 33.5% vs 20.1%, p < 0.001). During the post-approval period (2015-2024), AF initiation and overall use rose faster at ACs: (AC-NonAC Δ slope +0.26 percentage points/year, p = 0.002; + 1.25 percentage points/year, p < 0.001). During the post-INPULSIS/ASCEND period (2015-2017), overall AF use rose faster at ACs (Δ slope +1.23 percentage points/year, p = 0.009), while AF initiation slopes did not differ significantly (Δ slope -0.22 percentage points/year, p = 0.155). PPF prevalence was similar across centers, with higher AF use at ACs in 2024 (17.1% vs 9.8%, p < 0.001). During the post-approval period (2020-2024), AF initiation and overall AF use increased faster at ACs (Δslope +1.16 percentage points/year, p < 0.001; + 1.94 percentage points/year, p = 0.009). During the post-INBUILD period (2020-2022), AF initiation rose faster at ACs (Δ slope +1.42 percentage points/year, p = 0.002), while overall AF slope differences were not significant. Outcome patterns for IPF revealed higher mortality and lung transplant in ACs, but lower respiratory failure and oxygen use. PPF showed higher respiratory failure and mortality in ACs, and no significant differences in lung transplant or oxygen use. AF use in IPF and PPF was higher and rose faster at ACs, suggesting faster AC adoption and potential barriers at NonACs. Mixed outcome findings suggest referral and severity bias may partially explain differences, however, are unlikely to fully account for them. More research is needed to account for referral and severity bias. Given the small NonAC PPF cohort (n = 216), PPF findings should be interpreted with caution.

title: Integrated conservation of linear heritage landscapes from a biocultural diversity perspective: A case study of the Huizhou-Hangzhou Ancient Trail, China.

abstract: Linear cultural heritage landscapes embody the long-term coupling relationships between ecological processes and human cultural practices, yet conservation models guided by a single ecological or cultural goal fail to meet their holistic management needs. Based on the perspective of biocultural diversity, this study takes the Huizhou-Hangzhou Ancient Trail (HHAT) as a case study and constructs a comprehensive conservation framework oriented toward spatial planning. Biodiversity and cultural diversity patterns are assessed and their spatial relationships are quantified using the coupling coordination degree model. The biocultural diversity index is further integrated with the Marxan systematic conservation planning model to identify Biocultural Core Protected Areas (BCCPA) and support differentiated spatial conservation strategies. The results indicate that biodiversity and cultural diversity along the HHAT exhibit a pronounced antagonistic coupling relationship: regions with antagonistic coupling account for 98.90% of the total study area, while coordinated regions make up only 0.02%. Based on the natural and cultural context of the study area, this pattern may be jointly influenced by rigid competition for small‑scale spatial resources, the dual effects of traffic corridors, and the cumulative effects of traditional livelihood activities. In response, an integrated conservation spatial pattern of one core area and two corridors is proposed, together with four conservation strategies: Conservation-Minimal Intervention, Conservation-Appropriate Revitalization, Restoration-Minimal Intervention, and Restoration-Appropriate Revitalization-enabling an effective translation from coupling diagnosis to spatial planning responses. This study advances understanding of biocultural interactions in mountainous linear heritage landscapes and provides a transferable methodological pathway for integrated conservation planning.

abstract: As an emerging pollutant derived from tire rubber, 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) has raised public health concerns due to widespread environmental exposure; however, its potential toxicological effects on avascular tissues such as intervertebral discs remain unclear. This study integrated network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation to investigate the potential mechanisms linking 6PPD-Q exposure to intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD). ADMET toxicological predictions indicated high model-predicted probabilities for SR-MMP and SR-ARE activation. Through multidimensional database integration, 59 common targets potentially associated with 6PPD-Q and IVDD were identified. Protein-protein interaction network analysis further identified five hub genes: PTGS2, MMP2, SMAD3, RELA, and GSK3B. Functional enrichment analysis suggested that these targets were mainly involved in AGE-RAGE, PI3K-Akt, MAPK, TNF, and IL-17 signaling pathways, collectively implicating oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis. Molecular docking showed favorable predicted binding between 6PPD-Q and the five hub proteins, with RELA exhibiting the most favorable docking score (-8.82 kcal/mol). A subsequent 100-ns MD simulation of the 6PPD-Q-RELA complex showed relatively stable RMSD, Rg, and SASA profiles and a concentrated low-energy conformational basin, supporting its dynamic stability under the simulated conditions. Collectively, these computational findings suggest potential molecular links between 6PPD-Q exposure and IVDD and provide hypotheses for subsequent experimental validation.

abstract: Photorefractive Keratectomy (PRK) is a widely used laser-assisted refractive surgical technique. In some cases, it leads to temporary subepithelial fibrosis linked to visual haze, but objective and quantitative tools to monitor these symptoms are lacking. We here present a machine learning-based method for the classification of corneal images from spectral domain optical coherence tomography images recorded in vivo on standard clinical devices and use it to extract quantitative fibrosis indicators. Because of the transient nature and relative rarity of significant post-PRK haze, we trained the model on corneas presenting Fuchs' Endothelial Corneal Dystrophy, causing similar, but permanent, fibrotic changes, and applied it to images from patients who have undergone PRK surgery. Our study shows that the model output (probability of pathological classification) combined with OCT-derived quantitative fibrosis descriptors provides an interpretable and explainable indicator of corneal healing for post-operative follow-up.

abstract: Audience experiences can vary both between performances and among spectators, but little is known about how different methods capture this variation across repeated showings of the same production. We therefore examined audience experience across twenty live performances of the same music theatre production. We combined two complementary methods: immediate audience ratings collected through customer feedback kiosks and more detailed post-performance questionnaires. The kiosks recorded 1,887 responses, corresponding to 67% of total attendance, and 458 audience members (16%) completed questionnaires. Overall, the reception was positive, but kiosk ratings varied significantly across performances, indicating that audience-level enjoyment ratings differed from one showing to another. Kiosk and questionnaire responses to the same enjoyment question did not differ significantly at the aggregate level, suggesting that brief kiosk feedback may provide a practical, low-burden measure of audience-level enjoyment. Cluster analysis of questionnaire data identified three descriptive response profiles that differed primarily in overall engagement and ratings of specific artistic elements. These profiles illustrate heterogeneity within the audience of a single production. Qualitative responses from participants whose quantitative ratings were closest to each cluster centroid provided illustrative accounts of the experiences associated with these profiles. These narratives added context to the quantitative findings by showing differences in emotional tone, interpretive emphasis, and personal connection to the performance. Supplementary interviews with the director, artistic director, and an external playwright illustrated both interest in and reservations about incorporating audience data into creative work. Their comments emphasised the potential of empirical findings to support artistic reflection, while also underscoring the importance of how and when feedback is communicated within production teams.

title: More than gaming: Examining executive functions in esports players.

author_details.name: Yalçıner S
author_details.affiliation: Balıkesir University, Faculty of Sports Sciences, Department of Coaching Education, Balıkesir, Türkiye.

author_details.name: Özdayı N
author_details.affiliation: Balıkesir University, Faculty of Sports Sciences, Department of Coaching Education, Balıkesir, Türkiye.

abstract: The main purpose of this study was to determine the differences in executive function performance levels of esports players who play First-Person Shooter (FPS) and Multiplayer Online Battle Arena (MOBA) game types compared to non-video game players (NVGPs). Other purposes of the study are to examine the relationships of executive function components and their relationships with in-game rank and total game play time variables. The study groups consisted of ninety volunteer participants, all of whom were male young adults between the ages of 18 and 34, 30 of whom actively played FPS video games, 30 of whom actively played MOBA video games, and 30 of whom NVGPs. Corsi Block-Tapping Test (CBT), Wisconsin (Berg) Card Sorting Test (WCST), and Stroop Test Çapa Form (ST) were used as data collection tools. According to the findings of the study; FPS players had significantly higher scores than NVGPs (p < 0.001, F = 8.55) in CBT and less error percentage than the NVGPs (p < 0.01, F = 5.58) and MOBA players had significantly less interference time than NVGPs in the ST (p < 0.001, F = 7.66). In addition, there was a significant negative correlation between CBT and ST interference times for all players (p < 0.05; r = -0.28) and a significant negative correlation between in-game skill and ST interference times for FPS players (p < 0.05; r = -0.41). These findings suggest that digital video game experience shapes cognitive profiles based on genre-specific demands; while FPS gameplay primarily enhances visuospatial working memory capacity, MOBA gameplay fosters stronger inhibition control, with higher in-game skill level reflecting superior inhibitory control in FPS gameplay, and relationship of visuospatial working memory and inhibition components demonstrating an underlying interrelated structure.

abstract: Patients with isolated acute-onset continuous dizziness (iAOCD) are commonly seen at the emergency department (ED). Distinguishing peripheral vestibular disorders from central causes remains challenging. Existing diagnostic tools, including bedside examination and neuroimaging, have important limitations. Otolin-1, an inner ear-specific glycoprotein, has been proposed as a biomarker of peripheral vestibular pathology. This study evaluated whether otolin-1 could serve as a diagnostic biomarker for this differentiation. This study analyzed samples from a prospective multicenter cohort of adult patients who were seen at the ED with acute onset, continuous dizziness without focal neurological deficits. Patients were included within 24 hours of symptom onset. Otolin-1 plasma concentrations were measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Final diagnoses (central versus peripheral) were determined by an expert panel based on clinical assessment, diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging and 3-month follow-up. We analyzed 245 patients (179 peripheral, 66 central). Median otolin-1 concentrations did not differ significantly between peripheral and central causes (517.6 [IQR 443.7-592.8] pg/mL vs 487.9 [424.9-644.4] pg/mL; p = 0.349). No significant differences were observed in hyperacute (<4.5 hours after symptom onset) or acute (4.5-24 hours after symptom onset) subgroups. Similarly, otolin-1 concentrations did not differ between central iAOCD and specific peripheral diagnoses. Substantial overlap in concentration ranges was observed across all comparisons. Receiver operating characteristic analysis similarly showed no useful discrimination (AUC 0.539, 95% CI 0.455-0.623). Otolin-1 does not differentiate between central and peripheral causes of iAOCD in the ED setting. Although biologically linked to inner ear pathology, otolin-1 lacks sufficient discriminatory value as a stand-alone diagnostic biomarker.

abstract: Syphilis has resurged across North America, including syphilis in pregnancy. Congenital syphilis can be prevented by timely treatment of syphilis in pregnancy, but conventional syphilis screening is problematic for people facing barriers to care. Syphilis point-of-care tests (POCT) have improved prenatal syphilis management in low- and middle-income countries. There is minimal literature regarding POCT feasibility and effectiveness for prenatal syphilis screening in high-income countries, where barriers and challenges may differ. Academic and community partners co-designed a prospective single-arm feasibility trial to evaluate syphilis POCT implementation at a low-barrier prenatal clinic in Hamilton, Canada. The INSTI HIV/syphilis POCT was integrated into routine clinical care for pregnant people with ≥1 risk factor for syphilis (unstable housing in the past year; substance use or accessing addictions services in the past year; > 1 sexual partner in the past year; history of sexually transmitted or blood-borne infection; presentation to care >20 weeks gestation). Sexual partners of newly diagnosed pregnant people are also offered POCT. Individuals offered POCT are invited to enroll in the study. The primary feasibility outcome is the proportion of pregnant participants who accept POCT at first offer. Secondary feasibility outcomes include valid POCT results on clinician's first attempt and accurate POCT interpretation by clinicians. Secondary clinical outcomes include time to treatment initiation and completion of treatment among syphilis-positive participants. To promote inclusion of groups facing structural barriers to research, individuals declining study participation are enrolled for limited prospective chart review (primary feasibility outcome only). Target enrollment is N = 62 pregnant participants over 18 months. Baseline participant characteristics and outcomes will be descriptively analyzed. Community-based knowledge mobilization is ongoing. This pilot study will generate novel feasibility data regarding prenatal syphilis screening with POCT in high-income countries and inform design of a multicenter implementation trial. title: Patient experience in National digital health platforms: Evidence from patient-generated feedback in Saudi Arabia.

author_details.name: Albesher AS
author_details.affiliation: Department of Information Systems, College of Computer Sciences and Information Technology, King Faisal University, Al-Ahsa, Saudi Arabia.

abstract: National digital health platforms are becoming fundamental components of modern healthcare delivery; however, patient experience is commonly assessed using overall ratings or sentiment analysis, providing limited understanding of the specific dimensions that influence digital healthcare quality and service improvement. This study aimed to develop a multidimensional framework for understanding patient experience in a national digital health platform, examine variation across healthcare services, investigate changes over time, and identify evidence-based improvement priorities. A qualitative analysis was conducted using 97,034 Google Play reviews of Sehhaty, the Saudi national digital health platform, posted between 2019 and 2026. Reviews were analyzed using an inductive coding approach to develop a patient experience framework, followed by comparative analyses across healthcare services and longitudinal analyses across successive stages of platform development. Nine patient experience dimensions were identified. Patient experience differed considerably across healthcare services, indicating that improvement priorities were service-specific rather than uniform across the platform. Longitudinal analyses showed a shift from predominantly technical concerns during early deployment toward challenges involving service accessibility, integration, continuity of care, as the platform matured. These findings enabled the identification of service-specific priorities for improving digital healthcare delivery. Patient experience in national digital health platforms is multidimensional, service-dependent, and evolves alongside platform maturity. The proposed framework extends approaches based primarily on ratings or sentiment by transforming large-scale patient-generated feedback into actionable evidence for healthcare quality improvement and continuous evaluation of patient-centered digital health services.

abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by persistent hyperglycemia arising from insulin resistance or impaired insulin secretion. Conventional and commercially available effective antidiabetic drugs are often associated with adverse effects and reduced efficacy over prolonged use, highlighting the need for safer and plant-based alternatives. Persea americana seed extract (PSE) has antidiabetic potential but suffers from non-specific distribution and poor bioavailability, thus limiting its clinical application. This study developed and evaluated the poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles encapsulating Persea americana seed extract (PSENP) to enhance therapeutic efficacy and delivery. Nanoparticles were characterized for zeta size, zeta potential, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), stability and their phytochemical composition, with HPLC confirming the presence of bioactive compounds including quercetin, syringic acid, and gallic acid. In-vivo, forty wistar rats were allocated into five groups: normal control, diabetic control, metformin-treated, PSE-treated, and PSENP-treated. Biochemical parameters were evaluated including fasting blood glucose, insulin (serum level), lipid profile, oxidative stress biomarkers (superoxide dismutase, catalase), and inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α). Histopathological examination of pancreatic tissue and safety evaluations for kidney and liver were performed. Moreover, In-silico study demonstrated the strong binding affinity between quercetin and α-glucosidase, thus supporting the glucose-lowering role of quercetin. The PSENP administration resulted in statistically significant glycemic control, enhanced antioxidant activity of enzymes, improved lipid profile, reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines, and preservation of architecture of pancreas, with no renal and hepatic toxicity. The findings of the study indicated that PLGA-based nanoformulation of P. americana seed extract provides a promising therapeutic strategy for diabetes management and its oxidative and inflammatory complications.

title: Predicting under-five child mortality in Zambia: Machine learning versus parametric survival models.

author_details.name: Arge KG
author_details.affiliation: Department of Statistics, College of Natural and Computational Sciences, Samara University, Samara, Ethiopia.

abstract: In sub-Saharan Africa, child mortality remains a critical public health challenge, with Zambia exhibiting some of the highest rates in the region. While survival analysis has identified key risk factors, these methods often fail to capture complex non-linear interactions and the dynamic, time-varying nature of longitudinal markers like birth intervals. This study aimed to develop and compare predictive survival models to improve risk stratification for under-five mortality using the 2024 Zambia Demographic and Health Survey (ZDHS). A cohort of 35,610 live births was initially identified, with a final analytic sample of 9,362 singleton births and 1,236 mortality events (13.2%) after applying exclusion criteria for maternal age and data completeness. We compared four modeling frameworks for predictive comparison: Cox Proportional Hazards (Cox PH), Lasso Cox regression, Random Survival Forests (RSF), and Gradient Boosting Machines (GBM), alongside a Bayesian Joint Model for inference on the birth interval and mortality association. The proportional hazards assumption was assessed using Schoenfeld residuals, and stratified Cox models were employed to address time-varying effects. Model performance was evaluated using nested cross-validation with mother-level outer folds and time-dependent Concordance Indices (C-index) and Area Under the Curve (AUC) metrics across a 48-month follow-up period. Under nested cross-validation, the four survival models demonstrated comparable predictive performance, with C-indices ranging from 0.745 (Cox PH) to 0.750 (Gradient Boosting Machine) and Integrated Brier Scores ranging from 0.095 to 0.096; pairwise comparisons across models were not statistically significant (DeLong's test: all p > 0.05). The Bayesian Joint Model revealed a significant association between the longitudinal birth interval process and the hazard of death ([Formula: see text], 95% CI: 0.023-0.048, p < 0.001), supporting the maternal depletion hypothesis. Variable importance analysis identified birth interval and maternal age as the most influential predictors of child survival, followed by previous child deaths. Stratified analysis of the Cox model revealed significant effects for maternal education (Secondary: HR = 0.426, 95% CI: 0.318-0.570) and previous child deaths (HR = 1.648, 95% CI: 1.529-1.777). Advanced survival modeling using joint modeling techniques provides deeper biological insights into child mortality dynamics, and machine learning and traditional survival models offered equivalent predictive discrimination and calibration in this analysis. These findings support targeted public health interventions focusing on birth spacing, maternal age, and enhanced monitoring for high-risk families as critical strategies for reducing under-five mortality in Zambia.

abstract: The tobacco epidemic is a global public health threat, with addiction often starting in the early adulthood stage of life. The Middle East Region is slow in adopting smoke-free campus policies, and few studies have examined smoking attitudes and behaviors among university students and their perspective on such policies. The objective of this study was to determine the perceptions, knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors toward smoking (used to denote using any tobacco products) and smoke-free campus policies among university students aged between 17 and 30 years old at a large multicampus academic institution in Lebanon. The study utilized a comprehensive cross-sectional study design. The questionnaire used in this study included validated tools for assessing smoking behaviors, such as the Global Adult Tobacco Survey (GATS); the Youth Tobacco Survey (YTS); and the Smoking Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices (KAP) survey, as well as sections for investigating attitudes toward smoking and the smoke-free campus policy. This study reports an alarming prevalence of smoking on campuses (32.2%), with more than half of the surveyed smokers reporting attempts to quit smoking in the past 12 months (53.4%). The factors significantly associated with smoking included having family (OR 7.08, 95% C.I (2.83-17.69) or friends (OR 12.20, 95% C.I (5.48-19.76)) who smoke, as well as experiencing social, emotional, or mental distress (OR 4.09, 95% C.I (1.74-9.63)). Further analysis revealed that agreement with a smoke-free university policy was a significant factor associated with reduced odds of smoking (OR 0.58 95% C.I (0.45-0.78)), whereas the perceived unfairness of smoking bans on campuses was associated with increased odds of smoking (OR 1.87, 95% C.I (1.34-2.61)). The results highlight a promising window of opportunity to implement evidence-based interventions to support students in quitting smoking. Interventions include educational programs to raise awareness of the dangers of tobacco use and programs to break the association between exposure to stress and smoking. Such programs could include a combination of awareness programs and organizing stress-reducing services, workshops, and consultations. Because the design is cross-sectional, these findings describe associations rather than causal effects; they nonetheless support the further evaluation of smoke-free campus policies as one component of a broader strategy to lower students' smoking rates, mitigate peer influence and foster healthier campus environments.

abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a complex and common condition with significant health, social, and economic burdens, especially due to frequent hospitalizations and comorbidities. International research shows current care for COPD is limited by delayed diagnosis, poor coordination among providers, and inconsistent adherence to treatment guidelines, which negatively impacts patient outcomes. Clinical pathways offer a promising solution by improving care coordination, aligning treatment with evidence-based guidelines, and enhancing both patient experiences and system efficiency; however, questions remain about how, for whom, and in which contexts they are most effective. Using a realist evaluation approach, our study will evaluate how, for whom, and in which circumstances an integrated clinical pathway for COPD works in Saskatchewan, Canada. First, we will develop initial program theories based on literature and stakeholder input. Second, we will test these theories using administrative data and realist interviews with healthcare staff, managers, providers, COPD patients, and caregivers. Third, we will refine our theories based on data collected. Fourth, we will translate our findings to enhance future implementation. These phases will be repeated over a three-year span to continuously improve pathway implementation processes and monitor improvements in patient outcomes. Findings will be shared through integrated knowledge translation with system decision-makers and patients. Findings will also be disseminated to the broader research community through conference presentations and peer-reviewed publications.

abstract: Adults with congenital heart disease (CHD) may experience substantial psychological distress. This study evaluated whether a documented history of anxiety disorders is associated with a distinct psychosocial profile in adults with CHD. In this cross-sectional study, 45 adults with CHD were included: 21 with a documented history of anxiety disorders and 24 without. Psychosocial assessment included the EuroQol-5D-3L (EQ-5D-3L), Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (RSES), State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI), and Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II). Associations between psychosocial measures and documented anxiety history were assessed using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for sex, NYHA functional class, and CHD complexity. Moderate depression was additionally assessed using univariable logistic regression. Mean age was 35 ± 9 years in participants with a documented history of anxiety disorders and 31 ± 11 years in those without (P = 0.230); males accounted for 33% and 62%, respectively (P = 0.052). NYHA functional class II-IV was more frequent among participants with a documented history of anxiety disorders (67% vs. 25%; P = 0.018). Compared with those without a documented anxiety history, participants with anxiety history reported greater limitations in usual activities (P = 0.021), higher anxiety/depression scores on the EQ-5D-3L (P = 0.023), poorer self-rated health (P = 0.038), higher trait anxiety (31.2 ± 5.8 vs. 26.5 ± 5.2; P = 0.008), and greater depressive symptom severity (BDI-II median 19 vs. 3; P = 0.001). Self-esteem was also higher (RSES median 27 vs. 25; P = 0.006). After adjustment, BDI-II scores were positively associated with a documented history of anxiety disorders (OR 1.14, 95% CI 1.05-1.28; P = 0.011), while EQ-5D VAS scores were inversely associated (OR 0.64, 95% CI 0.38-0.97; P = 0.048). STAI-State, STAI-Trait, and RSES scores were not significantly associated with anxiety history. None of the variables assessed in the univariable analysis was significantly associated with moderate depression. In adults with CHD, a documented history of anxiety disorders was associated with greater depressive symptom severity and poorer self-rated health after adjustment for relevant clinical factors.

title: TCLNet: A Thermal Contrast-Aware Lightweight Network for infrared object detection.

author_details.name: Zhu X
author_details.affiliation: Xijing University, Xi'an, Shaanxi, China.

author_details.affiliation: Xijing University, Xi'an, Shaanxi, China.

author_details.name: Jin X
author_details.affiliation: Xijing University, Xi'an, Shaanxi, China.

abstract: Infrared object detection plays an important role in low-light and complex-environment perception. However, infrared images often exhibit low signal-to-noise ratio, weak target-background contrast, and limited texture information, which can degrade detection performance in small-target and cluttered-background scenarios while making it difficult to balance detection accuracy and model complexity. To address these challenges, this paper proposes TCLNet, a Thermal Contrast-Aware Lightweight Network for infrared object detection. TCLNet introduces a Thermal Contrast Encoder (TCE) to enhance local contrast-sensitive target representations and a Thermal-Guided Cross-Feature Attention (TGCA) mechanism to promote interactions between contrast-enhanced and semantic features, thereby improving target discrimination and suppressing background interference.Experiments were conducted independently on the M3FD, FLIR ADAS v2 (denoted as FLIR_2), and NUDT-SIRST1 datasets. TCLNet achieves mAP50 values of 60.5%, 45.4%, and 91.4%, respectively, corresponding to improvements of 12.8, 11.3, and 7.5 percentage points over the YOLO12n baseline. Meanwhile, the model maintains a compact size of approximately 2M parameters. These results demonstrate that TCLNet improves infrared target detection, particularly in low-SNR and small-target conditions, while achieving a favorable balance between detection accuracy and model complexity.

title: Teaching and learning strategies for the derivative in engineering education: A scoping review protocol.

author_details.name: Galindo Illanes MK
author_details.affiliation: Universidad San Sebastián, Chile.

author_details.affiliation: Universidad Católica de la Santísima Concepción, Chile.

author_details.affiliation: Universidad San Sebastián, Chile.

abstract: The derivative is a fundamental concept in engineering education, as it enables students to model and interpret phenomena related to rates of change, optimization, and the analysis of physical processes. However, its teaching in higher education often emphasizes decontextualized algebraic procedures, with limited integration of authentic engineering problems and interactive digital technologies. This protocol outlines a scoping review aimed at mapping the available evidence on teaching and learning strategies for the derivative in undergraduate engineering education that incorporate authentic engineering problems, with or without the support of digital technologies. The review will follow the methodological framework proposed by the JBI Manual for Evidence Synthesis and the reporting guidelines of PRISMA-ScR. The review is guided by the PCC framework: (P) undergraduate engineering students; (C) didactic strategies for teaching and learning the derivative grounded in authentic engineering problems, with or without the support of digital technologies; and (C) higher education engineering programs. Searches will be conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, and SciELO for peer-reviewed publications published between 2000 and 2026 in English, Spanish, and Portuguese. Two reviewers will independently screen and select studies using Rayyan, and disagreements will be resolved by consensus. Data will be extracted using a pilot-tested data extraction form and synthesized through descriptive statistics, thematic categorization, and narrative synthesis. The review will provide a comprehensive mapping of didactic strategies, types of authentic problems, and reported learning difficulties related to the derivative in engineering education. The findings are expected to inform instructional design and support the development of evidence-based teaching practices in calculus courses for engineering students.

title: The evolutionary accessibility of cultural fitness landscapes.

author_details.name: Fogarty L
author_details.affiliation: Department of Human Behavior, Ecology, and Culture, Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology, Leipzig, Germany.

author_details.name: Hoyle RB
author_details.affiliation: School of Mathematical Sciences, University of Southampton, Southampton, United Kingdom.

abstract: Many human cultural and technological traits have a complex and peculiar structure. They are often characterized by multiple closely interacting parts that can form modules, and change as a result of innovation, collaboration, and social learning. A full understanding of the ways in which such cultural traits evolve requires a model that accounts for the close epistatic interaction of the constituent parts, and for the uniquely cultural processes that act on them. Here, we generalize the concept of 'adaptive landscapes', where populations search a landscape for optimal combinations of components. This generalization accounts for epistatic interactions, and includes processes such as modularization, communication, and collaboration, that are not features of genetic systems but may be quite common features of cultural systems. We show that modularization in combination with collaborative communication of search results is more successful, but sometimes more costly, than searching a full adaptive landscape. However, in many of the circumstances under which technology evolves, a full search of many thousands of possible modules may not be feasible since time, financial, energetic, and environmental constraints are likely to be strong. Under these conditions, our models suggest that there is a critical value for the number of modules to search below which the global optimum is more likely to be reached by searching the full landscape. The value of this threshold depends on the complexity of the technology. Overall, we suggest that analysis of cultural fitness landscapes is likely to be a fruitful avenue for research into technological change especially when combined with elements of human learning and interaction known to be important features of cultural evolution.

title: The impact of perceived social support on college athletes' academic burnout: The moderating role of cognitive reappraisal within a serial mediation model.

author_details.name: Xu G
author_details.affiliation: College of Physical Education, Yangzhou University, Yangzhou, China.

abstract: College athletes face substantial challenges from the combined demands of academic study and athletic training, placing them at elevated risk for academic burnout (AB). This study examined how perceived social support (PSS) is associated with AB by testing the mediating roles of mental toughness (MT) and athlete burnout (ATHB) and the moderating effect of cognitive reappraisal (CR). Using a cross-sectional design, 1,918 college athletes from over 20 Chinese universities completed standardized questionnaires assessing PSS, MT, ATHB, CR, and AB. Serial and moderated serial mediation were analyzed with the PROCESS macro (Models 6 and 89) while controlling for demographic and sport-related variables. PSS was directly and negatively associated with AB (β = -0.122, p < 0.001), with significant indirect associations separately through MT and ATHB and sequentially through MT and ATHB. CR showed path-specific moderation: at higher levels of CR, the negative PSS-AB association was stronger, but so was the positive ATHB-AB association, whereas the MT-AB association did not differ significantly across CR levels. Thus, CR should not be interpreted as having a uniformly buffering role. These findings may inform future multicomponent support approaches aimed at strengthening PSS and MT and identifying and addressing ATHB, while applying CR-related training cautiously and with attention to the specific pathway involved. The effectiveness and boundary conditions of such approaches require longitudinal or experimental testing.

abstract: Economic diversification is commonly modeled using co-occurrence-based measures of relatedness that quantify pairwise overlap among activities in a capability network. Although such measures are derived from network structure, they operate at the level of first-order neighborhood relations and summarize proximity through local co-occurrence. They do not explicitly encode higher-order structural context, such as indirect connectivity patterns or global positional similarity, into a continuous representation of entities and activities. We develop an embedding-based framework that learns such representations from network topology, enabling the construction of interpretable geometric features, including capability alignment, displacement, and portfolio entropy, that extend standard measures used in economic complexity. We apply this framework to two systems: international trade (1998-2023) and public procurement firms (2009-2024). The resulting representations reveal different structural organization across scales: firms exhibit modular clustering patterns, whereas countries occupy broader, nested capability configurations. In predictive tasks for product and activity specialization, embedding-derived features provide additional explanatory power beyond relatedness in several settings, particularly when forecasting variation in the magnitude of comparative advantage. For country-level entry events, however, persistence remains the strongest predictor. Our results show that relatedness remains the dominant predictor of entry events. In contrast, embedding-derived features become more informative in specific settings, particularly for modeling variation in specialization magnitude and in low-relatedness regimes. More broadly, the findings indicate that diversification depends on structural signals that are both prediction-target-dependent and scale-dependent, with relatedness and embedding-derived features capturing different aspects of the capability space (local overlap vs. structural position).

abstract: White feces syndrome (WFS) is a major health problem affecting intensive shrimp aquaculture, but its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Increasing evidence suggests that WFS may involve complex interactions among host physiological status, intestinal microbial dysbiosis, and environmental microbial communities. However, the relationships among these factors within commercial shrimp culture systems remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the associations among intestinal antioxidant capacity, intestinal microbiota, sediment microbial communities, and water quality parameters in Litopenaeus vannamei affected by WFS under small-pond culture conditions. Healthy and WFS-affected shrimp were collected from a commercial shrimp farm in Zhanjiang, Guangdong Province, China. Intestinal antioxidant parameters, including total antioxidant capacity (T-AOC), superoxide dismutase (SOD), glutathione peroxidase (GSH-Px), and malondialdehyde (MDA), were determined. Intestinal and sediment microbial communities were analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Water quality parameters and microbial community composition were compared between healthy and WFS groups. Compared with healthy shrimp, WFS-affected shrimp exhibited significantly increased intestinal MDA levels and decreased activities of T-AOC, SOD, and GSH-Px, indicating an imbalance in antioxidant status. Significant differences in intestinal microbial community composition were observed between groups, as confirmed by beta-diversity analysis (PERMANOVA, R2 = 0.407, P = 0.022). WFS-associated microbial alterations included changes in dominant bacterial taxa and predicted microbial functional potential related to metabolism. The dominant taxa, referring to the most abundant microbial groups based on relative abundance, differed between healthy and WFS-affected shrimp. Sediment microbial communities also showed substantial compositional shifts, suggesting alterations in the surrounding microbial environment. In addition, nitrate and total nitrogen concentrations were significantly reduced in the WFS group. These findings indicate that WFS occurrence is associated with coordinated alterations in shrimp antioxidant status, intestinal microbial structure, sediment microbial communities, and environmental conditions. This study provides new insights into WFS from a host-microbiota-environment interaction perspective and highlights potential indicators for monitoring shrimp health in aquaculture systems.

abstract: Detecting small faces remains challenging due to scale variation and limited discriminative cues at low resolutions. We address this with a two-pronged approach. First, we modify YOLOv5 by adding extra convolutional layers and small-object-focused detection heads that operate on larger, higher-resolution backbone feature maps, improving sensitivity to tiny targets. Second, we introduce a dynamic, image adaptive patching strategy for scale selection. We compute Cr channel color probability maps and measure the number and density of pixel clusters; a Fuzzy Inference System (FIS) uses these cues to select the most suitable patch size for near and far faces. On the WIDER FACE benchmark, our method attains 93.07% mAP@50 (Easy), 91.25% mAP@50 (Medium), and 84.45% mAP@50 (Hard). On our proposed local dataset, the proposed model achieves 49.36% mAP@50 for different size faces. Beyond faces, the approach generalizes to small object detection on VisDrone-DET2019, reaching 46.76 mAP@50. These results demonstrate that coupling small-object-aware architecture design with color-guided, fuzzy patch selection yields competitive mAP@50 for small and distant targets.

title: Blinks are strategically coupled with head movements in unconstrained natural gaze behavior.

author_details.name: Goettker A
author_details.affiliation: Department of Psychology, Justus Liebig University Giessen, Giessen 35396, Germany.; Department of Psychology, Centre for Mind, Brain and Behaviour, Universities of Marburg, Giessen and Darmstadt, Germany.

author_details.name: Hayhoe M
author_details.affiliation: Center for Perceptual Systems, University of Texas at Austin, Austin, TX 78712.

abstract: Blinks are a ubiquitous yet largely unnoticed aspect of human vision, despite causing frequent interruptions of visual input that can amount to up to 10% of waking time. By leveraging a large dataset of unconstrained gaze behavior during two natural tasks, we found a behavioral strategy to limit the impact of blinks: blinks were strategically coupled with head movements, which minimizes information loss due to unreliable visual input during head movements. Specifically, blink probability increased with higher head velocities and showed strong temporal modulation relative to head movement onset: Blink probability was reduced before head movement initiation and then peaked during the head movement. The strength of this coupling was tailored to the individual needs of participants, with participants with higher baseline blink rates showing stronger synchronization. This indicates that blinks are a part of an individually coordinated strategy when orchestrating eye and head movements during unconstrained natural behavior.

abstract: Huntingtin-associated protein 40 (HAP40) forms a stable protein complex with huntingtin (HTT). Its cellular function and how HAP40 loss influences mutant HTT (mHTT) abundance and pathobiology are currently unclear. Here, using diverse cellular models and omics methods, we demonstrate that HAP40 is an obligate interaction partner of HTT and through its binding controls HTT interactions and the abundance of HTT-associated proteins, indicating that it functions as a HTT interaction regulatory unit. Also, loss of HAP40 in mHTT-expressing striatal cells impairs autophagic protein degradation and triggers transcriptional activation of the CLEAR network, demonstrating that it functions as a proteostasis regulator that acts on quality control pathways. Finally, mHTT-expressing cells lacking HAP40 showed increased secretion of a ~205 kDa mHTT fragment through an endoplasmic reticulum (ER)/Golgi-associated route, indicating that striatal cells reduce intracellular mHTT-induced proteotoxicity through activation of secretory pathways. Together, these results establish HAP40 as a critical proteostasis regulator that through controlling HTT interactions maintains cellular homeostasis.

abstract: Photocorrosion remains a major challenge that hinders the development of photoelectrochemical (PEC) solar fuel production. Although Cu2O is a promising photocathode material due to its suitable band structure and visible light absorption, both oxidative and reductive photocorrosion pathways have been reported, with no consensus established in the research community in the PEC system. In this work, we fabricate three Cu2O photocathodes with distinct charge transport properties to investigate the correlation between charge accumulation and photocorrosion behavior. Both oxidative and reductive photocorrosion were observed depending on the type and location of charge accumulation. Notably, we propose a refined oxidative photocorrosion mechanism in which photogenerated holes induce surface Cu2O dissolution to Cu2+, followed by coordination with adsorbed *OH to form Cu(OH)2/CuO under illumination, which is contrary to the widely assumed direct oxidation from Cu2O to CuO. This work not only provides a unified understanding of the dual photocorrosion pathways in Cu2O, but also offers a generalizable framework for understanding photo-induced degradation in metal oxide photocathodes and for guiding the design of more robust PEC systems through charge transport engineering.

abstract: Protein complexes are pivotal to all major cellular processes. Translation-coupled complex assembly is ubiquitous in eukaryotes, but its molecular basis and prevalence in bacteria remain poorly understood. Here, we combine ribosome profiling and single-molecule optical tweezers to establish principles governing cotranslational assembly of four structurally diverse complexes in Escherichia coli. We reveal how heterotetramers form cotranslationally via hierarchical assembly pathways, with initial heterodimer formation priming the assembly of higher-order oligomers through a topology-dependent organization of homomeric and heteromeric interfaces. Co-post assembly, defined as interaction between nascent and fully synthesized subunits, initiates when dimerization domains are completely exposed at the ribosome. The assembly order is predominantly unidirectional and matches the operon gene order, with upstream-encoded subunits being synthesized first, and then engaging downstream nascent partner subunits. The co-post assembly efficiency depends both on the native operon structure and the ribosome-associated chaperone trigger factor, which binds emerging oligomerization domains and whose dissociation marks the onset of partner subunit engagement. The handover from chaperone engagement to cotranslational assembly is mediated by nascent chain folding. Finally, we show that co-post assembly provides a fitness advantage. Together, these findings reveal how genome organization and chaperone-assisted folding coordinate cotranslational assembly to promote efficient complex biogenesis and cellular fitness in bacteria.

abstract: A few studies have shown that brain catecholamines are implicated in language comprehension. However, the specific cognitive processes they modulate remain underexplored. We hypothesized that catecholamines enhance the unification of syntactic roles and word meanings into coherent multiword structures. This study combined electroencephalography and psychopharmacology to examine the effects of a catecholaminergic stimulant (methylphenidate) on processing sentences containing local syntactic ambiguities. Methylphenidate amplified the P600 event-related potential effect, which has been linked to the recruitment of cognitive resources for processing sentences with increased syntactic load. The drug's impact on semantic processing was subtler, showing a suggestive attenuation of the N400 effect to ambiguous sentences. Furthermore, the increase in the P600 effect under methylphenidate was most pronounced in participants with lower working memory capacity. This study provides evidence for linking catecholamine activity to syntactic unification in healthy individuals. Elevated catecholamine levels appear to increase the cognitive effort invested in syntactic unification, and to support the dynamic prioritization of syntactic information when contextual demands require it.

abstract: Aflatoxins produced by some species of Aspergillus pose a significant threat to global food safety, because they contaminate a variety of crops including maize. In this study, we used host-induced gene silencing (HIGS) to reduce aflatoxin accumulation in maize upon infection with Aspergillus flavus and Aspergillus parasiticus. Two RNAi constructs were designed and introduced into maize, one targeting two essential fungal genes involved in ergosterol biosynthesis (CYP51A and CYP51B) and the other targeting three aflatoxin biosynthesis genes (AflC, AflD, and AflR). The presence of RNAi transgenes was confirmed in 17 and 14 independent lines possessing the CYP51A/CYP51B RNAi construct and the AflC/AflD/AflR RNAi construct, respectively. Most transgenic lines had single-locus integrations and one or two copies of the transgene. Transgene expression varied considerably among the lines. Small RNA sequencing confirmed the production of siRNAs from the HIGS trigger sequences. Levels of CYP51A, AflC, AflD, and AflR transcripts in Aspergillus spp. were successfully decreased upon infection of transgenic maize. However, significant reduction in the level of CYP51B transcripts was not achieved and the CYP51A/CYP51B RNAi transgene had no discernible effect on fungal growth in infected maize. In contrast, we observed significant reductions in aflatoxin accumulation in four AflC/AflD/AflR RNAi transgenic lines infected with A. flavus and in two transgenic lines infected with A. parasiticus. Notably, one AflC/AflD/AflR transgenic line exhibited minimal aflatoxin contamination upon kernel infection with A. parasiticus. These results demonstrate the potential of HIGS to reduce aflatoxin production in mature corn kernels.

abstract: The search for high-performance lubricants is of broad relevance to biomedical applications, including artificial joints, regenerative scaffolds, and osteoarthritis therapies. Here we introduce glycerosomes-phosphatidylcholine (PC)-based vesicles containing glycerol-as a promising boundary lubricant. Using a surface force balance, we show that glycerosomes achieve a friction coefficient as low as 10-5 under a high compression pressure of 15.6 MPa, representing a 20-fold reduction compared to conventional PC liposomes. This level of lubrication surpasses any previously reported boundary lubricant system at such pressures in aqueous media. Mechanistically, glycerosomes exhibit substantially lower adhesion energy than PC liposomes, and theoretical simulations reveal enhanced vesicle stability and flexibility. Our findings establish glycerosomes as a superior hydration lubrication platform, with promising implications for both biomedical implants and industrial applications requiring robust lubricity.

abstract: Division of labor in social insects is enabled by coordinated changes in physiology, neural signaling, and gene regulation, yet it remains unclear to what extent behavioral maturation reflects incremental changes in individual genes and/or a reorganization of transcriptomic regulation at the system level. Here, we analyze the nurse-to-forager transition in worker honeybees (Apis mellifera) from a network perspective, treating the transcriptome as a gene-gene correlation system whose global organization reflects collective regulatory states. Using fat body gene expression data across five developmental time points that span an interval of behavioral transition, we construct signed gene-gene correlation networks and quantify their macro- and mesostate properties. We then descend to the level of the gene and construct microstate gene lists of interacting genes. Behavioral maturation of worker honeybees is accompanied by coordinated, nonmonotonic changes in global network structure rather than simple global shifts in interaction strength across the network. Early stages exhibit broadly positive, globally synchronized correlations, whereas later stages show increased modular segregation and the emergence of antagonistic gene-gene relationships. Despite this differentiation, networks remain fully connected with high global efficiency, consistent with a flexible small-world-like organization. Positive correlations primarily support global integration, while negative correlations act as localized, boundary-enforcing constraints. Negative correlations form a structured pattern of antagonism that is sparse and module-specific, occurring primarily between functional gene modules rather than within them. Network layouts and module analyses reveal two polarized, attractor-like regulatory states, a structure recapitulated in a vitellogenin-centered subnetwork and consistent with prior experimental perturbation studies.

abstract: Close-in planets orbiting core-helium-burning red-clump giants directly challenge tidal-engulfment theory, which predicts that planets within about 1 au of Sun-like stars should be engulfed during red-giant-branch (RGB) expansion. The existence of such survivors would imply missing physical processes in the late stages of stellar and planetary evolution. Yet only one such "forbidden" planet had been identified to date. Here we report three systems-24 Boo b, HD 12648 b, and TYC 4282-605-1 b-whose host stars are confirmed red-clump giants through asteroseismology, showing that each has already undergone dramatic expansion and contraction following helium ignition. Their planets now reside at orbital separations smaller than the maximum stellar radii attained during the RGB phase, implying that they should not have survived. Among them, 24 Boo b orbits at only 0.183 au with a 30-d period, making it the closest planet known around a red-clump giant. These findings demonstrate that this paradox is not an isolated anomaly but signals the emergence of a class of evolved planetary systems. Their survival defies current models of stellar-planetary coevolution and points to unexplored physics shaping planetary architectures around post-RGB stars.

abstract: Pathogen adaptations to new hosts are central to the disease ecology of cross-species transmission and host switching of viruses. The rabies virus is a model for adaptations to different hosts as it induces behavioral changes that facilitate transmission, while being maintained in distinct species-specific cycles of infection. Here, we demonstrate that the rabies virus requires distinct transmission dynamics in two hosts with different ecologies to establish maintenance, using agent-based modeling, analyses of virus glycoprotein-mediated manipulation of neuroreceptor function, and phylogenetic analysis. Epidemiological models suggest that rabies virus variants adapted to arctic foxes, which sustain rabies virus at very low host densities, require a higher probability of transmission than viruses adapted to raccoons. Using in vitro electrophysiology, we demonstrate that the rabies glycoprotein-derived peptides from arctic fox rabies variants are more potent antagonists of alpha7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors. These findings suggest a possible functional basis for the behavioral modifications that drive enzootic rabies transmission in the context of host ecology. In addition, a large proportion of residues that may drive rabies virus adaptation to raccoons and arctic foxes are found within this neurotoxin-like region. Furthermore, a residue in the neurotoxin-like region of the mature rabies virus glycoprotein (residue 183) has been associated with pathogenicity, host switching, and disease ecology in previous studies. We propose the hypothesis that rabies virus transmission dynamics adapt to the ecology and physiology of novel hosts through the selection of glycoproteins that elicit specific degrees of behavioral modification and transmission probability.

abstract: Cells sense infection through dedicated receptors, yet these surveillance pathways are often subverted by pathogen-encoded virulence factors. Guard immunity provides complementary defense by rapidly killing infected cells in response to infection induced stress. However, the symptoms of infection frequently resemble noninfectious stress, raising the question of how they are distinguished. Using quantitative transcriptomics, proteomics, and global translation measurements during viral infections in vitro and in vivo, we show that infection globally suppresses host gene expression and prevents direct antiviral responses. However, the resulting proteostatic stress does not activate guard immunity unless tumor necrosis factor-α (TNFα) is present. We identify the anti-apoptotic protein c-FLIP as a guard for gene expression integrity: its loss sensitizes cells to TNFα, triggering cell death and limiting viral spread. Modeling demonstrates that TNFα and c-FLIP loss function as a biological AND-gate, providing specificity and speed. These findings show how cells integrate internal stress signals with external inflammatory cues to improve the fidelity of death decisions, and how this circuitry may misfire during noninfectious inflammation.

abstract: DNA double strand breaks (DSBs) are repaired through distinct pathways, with homologous recombination (HR) favored when DNA ends undergo extensive resection. Although cytoplasmic N7-methylguanosine (m7G)-modified RNA increases after UV-induced single-strand breaks, its role in DSB repair (including HR) remains unclear. Here, we show that m7G-modified RNA accumulates at DSB sites, where it recruits the m7G reader protein Quaking (QKI)5, to selectively promote HR. Mechanistically, QKI5 directly interacts with MRE11 and enhances its DNA binding affinity, thereby facilitating DNA end resection. Depletion of QKI5 impairs recruitment of the MRE11-RAD50-NBS1 complex to DSBs and reduces HR repair efficiency. Moreover, elevated QKI5 expression is associated with resistance to radiotherapy in both mouse models and clinical cohorts. Together, these findings identify the m7G RNA-QKI5-MRE11 axis as a regulator of HR pathway choice and suggest QKI5 as a promising therapeutic target in cancer treatment.

abstract: The apoptotic regulators BAX and BAK, once activated, form homo-oligomers to trigger mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP), activating the apoptosome and caspases. Activation of BAX-BAK without apoptosome activation triggers sustained efflux of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and caspase-independent cell death. However, the molecular basis of mtDNA efflux remains unclear. We purified a macromolecular complex comprising BAK, BAX, activator BH3-only molecules, voltage-dependent anion channels 1 and 2 (VDAC1 and VDAC2), and prohibitins that released mtDNA from mitoplasts. BAX-BAK activation resulted in VDAC closure, mitochondrial calcium influx, and mtDNA efflux. Loss of VDAC1, VDAC2, or prohibitins prevented BAX-BAK activation-induced mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death without affecting MOMP or mitochondrial inner membrane herniation. These findings support differential regulation of cytochrome c and mtDNA efflux by distinct BAX-BAK complexes.

abstract: The power conversion efficiency (PCE) and stability of flexible perovskite solar modules (PSMs) are less than those of their rigid devices because surface hydroxyls desorption on flexible substrates, which disrupts self-assembled monolayer (SAM) anchoring and perovskite crystallization. We developed a decoupled SAM-perovskite codeposition strategy that accelerates SAM anchoring by reducing the SAM-perovskite interaction and ameliorates perovskite crystallization. The certified PCE with phenethylammonium iodide as the passivation molecule was 20.2% on PSMs with device areas of 750 cm2. With 1,3-diaminopropane dihydroiodide as the passivator, the PCE of 22.0% for a device area of 14.55 cm2 decreased by 8% after 1044 hours under maximum power point tracking at 85°C and 65% relative humidity. The devices pass all sequences of an international commercialization assessment standard for flexible portable PSMs.

abstract: Nanochannels capable of fast and selective mass transport are central to applications in energy, resources, biomedicine, and the environment. However, extreme nanoscale confinement, often coupled with rigid channel environments, imposes substantial frictional and adhesive barriers, causing sluggish transport and constrained selectivity. We identified nanochannel dynamics as a key to addressing these challenges by harnessing the intrinsic mobility (e.g., self-rotation) of confined functionalities to enhance molecular transport. Through a combination of experiments and simulations, we demonstrated that such dynamics reshape transport by promoting kinetic energy transfer and enabling more efficient molecular relays, thereby improving separation performance beyond current benchmarks. Our findings highlight the role of nanochannel dynamics in regulating mass transport under confinement and provide a framework for designing advanced nanochannel systems.

abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) are quantum states that remain localized despite lying within a continuum of extended, delocalized states. Whereas optical BICs have been realized in photonic systems, achieving electronic bound states embedded in a metallic background remains an ongoing challenge. In this study, we used scanning tunneling microscopy to identify two defect-induced electronic states that remain localized within the metallic continuum of Pd5AlI2, a two-dimensional van der Waals metal. Our calculations suggest that electron-hopping interference on the decorated checkerboard lattice of Pd5AlI2 gives rise to a (quasi) flat band built from spatially localized eigenstates that are orthogonal to the dispersive continuum. Atomic defects within this frustrated lattice shift the associated flat-band localized states into the metallic continuum, forming robust, symmetry-protected BICs.

abstract: Two-dimensional moiré materials provide a versatile platform to explore phase transitions in strongly correlated systems. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we imaged the density-driven melting of generalized Wigner crystals (GWCs) and Mott insulators (MIs) in electron-doped, near-60°-twisted molybdenum diselenide bilayers featuring a triangular moiré superlattice. We observed notable electron-hole asymmetry in GWC melting: Hole-doped GWCs yielded interaction-driven disordered states, whereas electron-doped GWCs melted into delocalized liquid-like states. This asymmetry arose from the broken particle-hole symmetry of the moiré superlattice, which produced electron and hole Fermi pockets with different momentum geometries upon GWC condensation. MI states melted without such asymmetry, consistent with the absence of a symmetry-breaking density modulation. This work provides direct visualization of the emergent phases that appear as GWCs undergo quantum melting transitions.

abstract: Immunotherapy with checkpoint inhibitors has revolutionized cancer therapy and enabled considerable therapeutic advances for treating various diseases, including lung cancer. However, the molecular determinants of variable patient outcomes remain unclear. Using long-read RNA sequencing, we mapped the landscape of alternative RNA splicing in human primary lung adenocarcinomas. We identified more than 149,000 full-length messenger RNA (mRNA) isoforms, more than half of which were unannotated and many that occurred in immune-related genes, particularly within the type I interferon response pathway. We functionally characterized retained introns in the STAT2 gene that produced altered protein isoforms that regulated immune signaling and interferon responses and correlated with patient survival after anti-programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunotherapy. These findings position alternative splicing as a regulator of tumor immune responses and reveal intron retention in STAT2 as an interferon regulatory axis that correlates with PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitor response.
