abstract: Bovine anaplasmosis, caused by the tick-borne rickettsial pathogen Anaplasma marginale, is a significant threat to livestock health and productivity. The major surface protein 1a (MSP1a) is a widely used molecular marker for characterizing strain diversity, due to its variable N-terminal tandem repeats. In this study, we analyzed and updated the nomenclature classification of 157 A. marginale MSP1a sequences submitted to NCBI between 2013 and 2023, following the research by Cabezas-Cruz in 2013. We identified and classified 189 unique tandem repeats, reported their tick-transmissibility, predicted their secondary structures and B-cell epitopes, and analyzed amino acid variability. Following this, we conducted a comparative analysis with previously published datasets, which revealed new tandem repeat types, new positions of serine within tandem repeats, and high variation among B-cell epitope variants. We have also classified the unique R1 tandem repeats of the new MSP1a sequences into different ecoregion clusters based on the principal component analysis of NDVI values. This updated classification system enhances the molecular understanding of A. marginale diversity and may contribute to future developments in strain typing, epidemiological investigations, and vaccine research.

title: Non-adaptive evolutionary forces predominantly shape nucleotide composition near human transcription start sites.

author_details.name: Qiu Y
author_details.affiliation: Department of Biochemistry, University of Toronto, Toronto, Ontario, Canada.

author_details.name: Hebraud E
author_details.affiliation: Department of Biochemistry, University of Toronto, Toronto, Ontario, Canada.; Laboratoire Interdisciplinaire des Sciences du Numérique, Université Paris-Saclay, Gif-sur-Yvette, France.; Institut Agro, Rennes Angers, Rennes, France.

author_details.name: Pouyet F
author_details.affiliation: Laboratoire Interdisciplinaire des Sciences du Numérique, Université Paris-Saclay, Gif-sur-Yvette, France.

author_details.name: Palazzo AF
author_details.affiliation: Department of Biochemistry, University of Toronto, Toronto, Ontario, Canada.

abstract: In the human genome, mutation rates vary along genes, yet how their fine-scale structure contributes to gene evolution has remained largely unexplored. Here, we map inherited mutations at single-nucleotide resolution and uncover a striking hypermutation peak at transcription start sites (TSSs) of human protein-coding genes. This pattern is observed both in population polymorphisms and in de novo mutations from parent-offspring trios, and is dependent on transcriptional activity in testes. We also find similar hypermutation peaks at TSSs used to produce long noncoding RNAs and at intergenic RNA Polymerase II pause sites. In addition, we identify distinct mutational signatures at exon-intron boundaries and in introns. By comparing the current nucleotide content to predicted equilibrium levels, inferred from mutation and fixation rates, and by analyzing derived ancestral frequency spectrums, we detect signals that are compatible with a low level of ongoing background GC-biased gene conversion (gBGC) throughout the region and ancestral elevated gBGC activity that is centered right downstream from the TSS. Using a forward-in-time simulation algorithm, we show that the current nucleotide composition surrounding the TSS of protein-coding genes is best explained by local mutation biases coupled to ongoing and ancestral patterns of gene conversions. Our simulations allow us to infer several features of these gBGC events. Overall, these findings indicate that the nucleotide composition around TSSs is largely shaped by non-adaptive forces, particularly mutation bias and gBGC.

title: Nurses' perceptions of an audiovisual material to support patient education on oral health management in diabetes care.

author_details.name: Kudoh R
author_details.affiliation: Institute of Medicine, University of Tsukuba, Tsukuba, Ibaraki, Japan.

author_details.name: Shibayama T
author_details.affiliation: Institute of Medicine, University of Tsukuba, Tsukuba, Ibaraki, Japan.

abstract: Educational support for nurses is essential to promote oral health management education for patients with diabetes. However, few studies have focused on supporting nurses in this context. This study explored the effects of an audiovisual material designed to support nurses' patient education on oral health management in diabetes care. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with eight certified diabetes nurse educators. Data were analyzed using content analysis. Four main themes emerged: (1) enhancement of nurses' individual learning (8/8 participants), including improved knowledge of the connection between oral health and diabetes; (2) promotion of professional development and reflection (5/8); (3) provision of new insights into patient care (7/8), particularly regarding patient motivation strategies; and (4) identification of implementation considerations in diabetes outpatient settings. The findings suggest that the audiovisual material, designed to complement an existing evidence-based educational guide, was perceived as useful and may support nurses' learning and educational practices related to oral health education for patients with diabetes.

title: Occupational health risks from climate-related and infectious-disease stressors: A scoping review of worker safety and resilience.

author_details.name: Odud MA
author_details.affiliation: Department of Industrial and Management Systems Engineering (IMSE), Benjamin M. Statler College of Engineering and Mineral Resources, West Virginia University, Morgantown, West Virginia, United States of America.

author_details.name: Abdul-Aziz OI
author_details.affiliation: Wadsworth Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Benjamin M. Statler College of Engineering and Mineral Resources, West Virginia University, Morgantown, West Virginia, United States of America.

abstract: Objective This scoping review examines how climate-related stressors and infectious-disease conditions, including pandemic-related workplace disruptions, interact to influence worker health, vulnerability, and occupational resilience. The review focuses on shared exposure pathways, vulnerable worker populations, methodological patterns, policy gaps, and strategies for strengthening worker safety under compound hazards. Rather than treating pandemics as isolated events, the review uses pandemic conditions as a lens to understand broader, recurring occupational risks and to inform strategies for building safer and more resilient workplaces under compound hazards. Methods Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, a structured literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for English-language peer-reviewed and formally structured evidence sources published primarily between January 2020 and April 2025, with one pre-2020 policy study retained for foundational context. Out of 612 records initially identified, 10 studies or sources met the inclusion criteria across healthcare, agriculture, construction, emergency response, and other high-exposure sectors after systematic screening and eligibility assessment. Data were charted and synthesized by occupational sector, geographic region, exposure type, worker vulnerability, and methodological approach. Results The evidence indicates that climate-related and infectious-disease stressors frequently converge, amplifying physical, environmental, and psychosocial pressures on workers. Disproportionate risks were observed among migrant workers, informal laborers, low-income populations, older adults, women, and seasonal or cross-border agricultural workers, particularly where access to healthcare, legal protections, or adaptive infrastructure was limited. Most studies relied on descriptive, qualitative, cross-sectional, conceptual, or review-based designs, with limited use of predictive modeling, geospatial analysis, longitudinal evidence, or integrated datasets. Policy responses were often fragmented, with climate adaptation and infection-control measures addressed separately despite overlapping benefits. Conclusions Climate-related and infectious-disease stressors interact to reinforce occupational health inequities and expose persistent gaps in worker protection. The findings highlight the need for integrated, multi-hazard occupational health strategies that align climate adaptation, infection prevention, and psychosocial support. Embedding data-driven early-warning systems, equitable protections for vulnerable workers, and cross-sector coordination into occupational policies may help strengthen workforce resilience during routine operations as well as future climate extremes and public health crises. However, the findings should be interpreted with caution because of the limited number of available studies combining climate-related and infectious-disease occupational risks, heterogeneous study designs, and the emerging nature of the evidence base. Furthermore, since this scoping review maps evidence rather than formally grading evidence strength or testing causal relationships, recommendations should be interpreted as evidence-informed directions for future occupational-health planning and research.

title: Parsing-based approach for entity extraction from natural language software requirements.

author_details.name: Amjad S
author_details.affiliation: Department of Software Engineering, The University of Lahore, Lahore, Pakistan.

author_details.name: Saleem A
author_details.affiliation: Department of Computer Science, Government College University, Lahore, Pakistan.

author_details.name: Khan AS
author_details.affiliation: Department of Software Engineering, The University of Lahore, Lahore, Pakistan.

author_details.name: Anwar MW
author_details.affiliation: Department of Computer Science, Government College University, Lahore, Pakistan.

abstract: Software requirements are written in natural language, so they are inherently ambiguous. This ambiguity results in the misinterpretation of the requirements and leads to an incorrect implementation of the system that does not meet the user's needs. So, it is important for all the stakeholders to comprehend the requirements. The requirement statements revolve around the requirement entities. Identifying requirement entities is essential to understand requirements, and they are used in identifying coreferent entities, creating glossaries, producing summaries of documents, feature extraction, requirements classification, and domain understanding. Manual entity extraction is a labour-intensive task. Recently, transformer-based models have played an important role in improving entity extraction results, but they require extensive pre-training of models for domain-specific tasks. To overcome these challenges, the proposed automated approach is used to extract entities from software requirements without the need for manual efforts and a large dataset for pre-training. In this study, two widely used parsing techniques, constituency parsing and dependency parsing, are applied to extract noun phrase-based entities. In addition, a hybrid approach comprising the combined extractions of both parsers is developed. The dataset comprises the software requirements from the healthcare domain and is manually annotated to establish a gold standard for evaluation. Experimental results indicate that the hybrid approach achieves the best overall extraction performance among the evaluated methods. While the constituency parser achieves the highest precision, it exhibits comparatively lower recall. In contrast, the hybrid approach achieves the highest recall and F1-score while maintaining precision comparable to that of the constituency parser. These results demonstrate that the hybrid method provides a more effective solution for automatically extracting entities from software requirements by leveraging syntactic structures of sentences rather than relying on domain-specific model training.

title: Predicting continuous load-settlement trajectories of bored piles: A GA-optimized weighted ensemble framework with explainable AI.

author_details.name: Giap LV
author_details.affiliation: University of Transport Technology, Hanoi, Vietnam.

author_details.name: Nguyen TL
author_details.affiliation: Le Quy Don Technical University, Hanoi, Vietnam.

author_details.name: Pham TA
author_details.affiliation: University of Transport Technology, Hanoi, Vietnam.

abstract: Accurate prediction of bored pile settlement is a core element in reliable foundation design. While machine learning (ML) models demonstrate superior predictive capabilities compared to traditional analytical methods, their black-box nature and tendency to generate non-physical trajectories significantly hinder their practical application in geotechnical engineering. This study proposes a new computational framework that ensures physical consistency by combining Weighted Ensemble learning with SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) interpretation capabilities. The integrated structure incorporates linear regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, and multilayer neural networks (MLP) to capture the complex interaction between piles and soil through a database of 563 field static load test records. A two-stage hybrid optimization strategy, using Random Search combined with a Genetic Algorithm (GA), was implemented to optimize the global weight set. The results showed that the GA-Ensemble model achieved excellent accuracy on the independent test set (R2 = 0.958, NRMSE = 5.27%, RMSE = 0.380, MAE = 0.2322), successfully neutralizing the ladder errors of the tree model to recreate a smooth, continuous, and mechanically compliant load-settlement (P-S) trajectory. Notably, by converting the SHAP value to a real physical scale (millimeters), the study clarified the algorithm's inference logic. SHAP dependency analysis demonstrated that the model successfully captures the coupling characteristics of elastic compression and geometric nonlinearity by identifying the interaction between external force (P) and free length (Lf). Local diagnostic decompositions precisely extract failure mechanisms, successfully quantifying the "systemic penalty" caused by elastic shortening of structures and foundation puncture even in very stiff soil layers. In short, the proposed method has gone beyond the limits of a purely interpolation tool, establishing a transparent and geomechanically reliable expert system for predicting settlement.

title: Predicting mental health risk in adolescents using interpretable machine learning: Evidence from SHAP analysis.

author_details.name: He J
author_details.affiliation: College of Physical Education, Shanghai Normal University, Shanghai, China.

abstract: Background/objective Adolescent mental health is a critical public health concern; however, the combined contribution of emotional, demographic, and behavioral factors to poor mental health remains incompletely understood. This study applied an interpretable machine learning framework to identify key predictors of elevated mental health risk among adolescents and characterize their relative and non-linear contributions. Methods Data were drawn from the 2021 Youth Risk Behavior Survey (YRBS), comprising 16,946 U.S. high school students. Elevated mental health risk was defined using the YRBS current mental health item (Q85): reporting that mental health was not good most of the time or always during the past 30 days. The distinct 12-month sadness/hopelessness item (Q25) was retained as a predictor in the primary XGBoost model. The operating threshold was selected by maximizing the Youden index using five-fold out-of-fold predictions in the training set and was then locked before evaluation in the held-out test set. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to assess feature importance and directional and non-linear patterns. Results Overall, 28.0% of adolescents were classified as having elevated mental health risk, with higher prevalence among females (39.9% vs. 16.9%) and peak prevalence at ages 16-17. The primary XGBoost model achieved an AUC of 0.806 and PR-AUC of 0.603. At the training-derived threshold of 0.285, accuracy was 0.749, sensitivity 0.754, specificity 0.747, and balanced accuracy 0.750. SHAP analysis identified sadness/hopelessness as the dominant predictor, followed by sex, sleep duration, screen time, and breakfast frequency. In a sensitivity analysis excluding sadness/hopelessness, discrimination decreased (AUC 0.736; PR-AUC 0.510). Conclusion The revised primary model achieved balanced sensitivity and specificity above 0.700 using a threshold selected entirely within the training data. Sadness/hopelessness was the strongest predictor, while demographic and behavioral factors provided additional predictive information. Because sadness/hopelessness is conceptually close to the current mental health outcome and the data are cross-sectional, the model should be interpreted as an auxiliary risk-stratification tool rather than a standalone clinical screening or diagnostic instrument.

title: Predicting visual impairment in type 2 diabetes using key performance indicators identified by the Black Widow and Whale Optimization Algorithms: A case study in Saudi Arabia.

author_details.name: Al-Hussein F
author_details.affiliation: Department of Mathematics and Statistics, College of Sciences, University of Jeddah, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

author_details.name: Tafakori L
author_details.affiliation: School of Science, RMIT University, Melbourne, Victoria, Australia.

author_details.name: Abdollahian M
author_details.affiliation: School of Science, RMIT University, Melbourne, Victoria, Australia.

author_details.name: Al-Shali K
author_details.affiliation: Department of Medicine, King Abdulaziz University Hospital, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

abstract: Visual impairment (VI) is a severe and prevalent complication of type 2 diabetes (T2D), particularly in high-risk populations, underscoring the critical need for early predictive strategies. A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted to develop and validate machine learning (ML) predictive models for VI among patients with T2D in Saudi Arabia. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to employ WOA and BWO as feature selection techniques to identify the most informative predictors of VI among Saudi patients with T2D. Predictive models were subsequently developed and compared using both clinically recommended features and algorithmically selected features derived from WOA and BWO to determine the optimal feature set for predictive performance. Medical records of 1,000 T2D patients (555 VI [55.5%]; 445 non-VI [44.5%]) from King Abdulaziz University Hospital were analyzed. Models were developed using an 80/20 stratified train-test split, with 5-fold cross-validation performed on the training set for internal validation. Patients were divided into two groups: those with HbA1c ≥ 6.5% (full dataset) and a clinically relevant high-risk subgroup with HbA1c > 8% (reduced dataset), which incorporated 19 recommended demographic, lifestyle, and lipid profile features. Models utilizing the reduced dataset consistently achieved superior performance across all algorithms. Among them, the WOA-CatBoost model demonstrated the highest performance (Accuracy = 0.95, AUC = 0.96, 95% CI: 0.94-0.98) using only 9 features, outperforming both the BWO-Random Forest (BWO-RF) model (Accuracy = 0.92, AUC = 0.90, 95% CI: 0.87-0.93) with 10 features and the baseline Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) model (Accuracy = 0.91, AUC = 0.94, 95% CI: 0.91-0.97) with 13 features. Bonferroni-corrected paired t-tests based on five-fold cross-validation accuracies (α = 0.017) confirmed a significant performance advantage of WOA-CatBoost over BWO-RF (t = 10.17, p < 0.001), supporting WOA-CatBoost as the overall best-performing model. Key predictors identified across all three best-performing models included Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), body mass index (BMI), age, occupation, triglycerides (TG), type of food, and smoking. These findings demonstrate that WOA-CatBoost provides a clinically actionable, parsimonious predictive tool for VI risk stratification in T2D patients within the Saudi Arabian healthcare context.

title: Predictors of preeclampsia with severe features: A multi-center analysis of maternal and health system factors in Thai tertiary hospitals.

author_details.name: Boonyaporn T
author_details.affiliation: Doctor of Nursing Science (Candidate), Faculty of Nursing, Mahidol University, Bangkok, Thailand.

author_details.name: Limruangrong P
author_details.affiliation: Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology Nursing, Faculty of Nursing, Mahidol University, Bangkok, Thailand.

author_details.name: Ratinthorn A

author_details.name: Tankumpuan T
author_details.affiliation: Department of Surgical Nursing, Faculty of Nursing, Mahidol University, Bangkok, Thailand.

abstract: Background Preeclampsia (PE) with severe features threatens maternal and neonatal health. This study examined maternal and health-service factors associated with severe features and compared maternal and neonatal outcomes in Thailand. Methods This case-control study enrolled 156 postpartum women with PE (52 with and 104 without severe features) and 111 nurse-midwives in antenatal care, labor, and postpartum units across four Thai tertiary hospitals. Data were collected using postpartum and nurse-midwife questionnaires, and a maternal-neonatal health record form. Group differences were assessed using independent t-test, chi-square or Fisher's exact tests. Multivariable binary logistic regression examined factors associated with severe features, adjusting for antenatal care visits and gravidity. Results Women with severe features more often had a history of PE (32.7% vs. 13.5%, p = 0.006) and differed in BMI distribution (p = 0.007). Three maternal factors were independently associated with severe features: history of PE (aOR = 5.99, 95% CI 2.13-16.83), BMI (aOR = 0.92 per kg/m2, 95% CI 0.86-0.98), and moderate versus low PE knowledge (aOR = 0.13, 95% CI 0.04-0.50). No health-service variable, including nurse training, was independently associated with severe features after adjustment (all p > 0.05). The model explained 29.4% (Nagelkerke R2) of the variance in PE severity and correctly classified 75.8% of cases. Infant birth weight was lower among women with severe features (p < 0.05); delivery mode, hospital stay, birth asphyxia, and NICU admission did not differ significantly. Conclusion A history of PE was associated with higher odds, and moderate (versus low) PE knowledge and higher BMI with lower odds, of severe features. These findings support prioritizing screening for prior PE history and structured antenatal knowledge counseling, together with adequately powered, multilevel studies to clarify the role of health-service factors in PE severity.

title: Prevalence of tobacco use and nicotine dependence among medical interns in Nepal: A cross-sectional study.

author_details.name: Subedi K
author_details.affiliation: Department of Community Dentistry, Gandaki Medical College Teaching Hospital and Research Centre, Pokhara, Nepal.

author_details.name: Gaire G
author_details.affiliation: Department of Community Dentistry, Gandaki Medical College Teaching Hospital and Research Centre, Pokhara, Nepal.

author_details.name: Karki B

author_details.name: Neupane S
author_details.affiliation: Department of Internal Medicine, Institute of Medicine, Kathmandu, Nepal.

abstract: This study was conducted to assess the prevalence of tobacco consumption, nicotine dependence and factors associated with tobacco use among medical interns in Nepal. Data was collected from February to April 2023 using an online questionnaire distributed through multiple platforms, with weekly reminders for five weeks. The questionnaire included demographic characteristics, tobacco use status, type of tobacco, age at initiation, and the six-item Fagerström Test for Nicotine Dependence. A minimum sample of 324 participants was required, and 389 participants were targeted to allow for potential non-response. Of the 798 interns who received the questionnaire, 381 completed it, for a response rate of 47.74%. The majority of participants were male, 54.33% (n = 207) and studying Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery, 64.57%(n = 246). The prevalence of tobacco use was 18.11% (n = 69), including 13.12% smokers (n = 50) and 4.99% smokeless tobacco users (n = 19). Smoking was significantly more common among male and MBBS interns. Exploratory, post-hoc multivariable logistic regression showed that female interns had lower odds of tobacco use than male interns (OR = 0.18; 95% CI: 0.09-0.36). Among the 50 smokers, one participant did not complete the nicotine dependence questionnaire; therefore, 49 smokers were included in the nicotine dependence analysis. Among smokers, nicotine dependence was low in 73.47% (n = 36), moderate in 24.49% (n = 12), and high in 2.04%(n = 1). Among the tobacco users, 44.93%(n = 31) responded that the reason for the initiation of tobacco products was self-interest, followed by peer pressure, 23.19%(n = 16). Tobacco use was less common among medical interns than in the general population, likely reflecting their higher educational attainment. Among those who smoked, most exhibited low levels of nicotine dependence. Self-interest and peer pressure were the primary reasons for tobacco initiation. The exploratory associations should be interpreted cautiously and considered hypothesis-generating.

title: Problematic gaming in occasional, low, intermediate or heavy use gamers - not all screen time is created equal - A reanalysis.

author_details.name: Bediou B
author_details.affiliation: Université de Genève, FPSE, Genève, Switzerland.; neuro @campus biotech, Genève, Switzerland.; Digital Wellness Lab, Boston Children's Hospital, Boston, Massachusetts, United States of America.

author_details.name: Bavelier D
author_details.affiliation: Université de Genève, FPSE, Genève, Switzerland.; neuro @campus biotech, Genève, Switzerland.

abstract: Despite having received increasing attention over the past decade, little is known about the factors that can increase or decrease symptoms of problematic gaming (PG) in individuals with different video gaming (VG) habits (e.g., occasional use gamers vs heavy use gamers). Here, we apply a specification curve analysis to assess the impact of changes in two key risk factors, gaming consumption and impulsivity, as well as one protective factor, family environment, on changes in PG symptoms over 2 years in a large sample of Singaporean adolescents between 2007 and 2009. By considering individual differences in baseline video game habits, we show that changes in VG consumption influenced changes in PG in adolescents who reported not usually playing games at study inception (i.e., occasional use gamers), whereas changes in impulsivity influenced PG in those who reported being the most heavy use gamers at study inception. These findings highlight the importance of designing preventative measures that differ as a function of current video game habits. Possible measures may involve introducing gaming progressively (e.g., through setting age-appropriate limits or structured scaffolding with parents) to improve tolerance and reduce preoccupation in occasional gamers while promoting self-control early in development before gaming can become a problematic habit.

title: Proton transport drives allosteric conformational changes in the MmpL3 transporter.

author_details.name: Yang L
author_details.affiliation: School of Chemistry and Biochemistry, Georgia Institute of Technology, Atlanta, Georgia, United States of America.

author_details.name: North EJ
author_details.affiliation: Department of Pharmacy Sciences, Creighton University, Omaha, Nebraska, United States of America.

author_details.affiliation: Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry, University of Oklahoma, Norman, Oklahoma, United States of America.

author_details.affiliation: Mycobacteria Research Laboratories, Department of Microbiology, Immunology and Pathology, Colorado State University, Fort Collins, Colorado, United States of America.

author_details.name: Gumbart JC
author_details.affiliation: School of Chemistry and Biochemistry, Georgia Institute of Technology, Atlanta, Georgia, United States of America.; School of Physics, Georgia Institute of Technology, Atlanta, Georgia, United States of America.

abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), remains a global health crisis, further complicated by increasing drug resistance. The mycobacterial membrane protein MmpL3, which is essential for transporting cell wall precursors such as trehalose monomycolate (TMM), is a promising therapeutic target. However, the mechanistic link between proton-driven dynamics and substrate transport in MmpL3 is not fully understood. In this study, we use molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how protonation of conserved Asp-Tyr dyads (Asp256-Tyr646 and Asp645-Tyr257) in Mycobacterium smegmatis (Msmg) MmpL3 regulates conformational changes and TMM binding. Protonation at Asp256 induces an open dyad conformation, increases local water accessibility, and is associated with a tendency toward more open configurations of the periplasmic binding pocket. In contrast, protonation at Asp645 stabilizes a closed dyad conformation, reduces water accessibility, and narrows the transmembrane binding pocket. These findings support a proposed sequential protonation model in which protonation-dependent conformational changes are allosterically coupled to substrate translocation.

title: Quality and accuracy of complementary feeding information on Instagram: A cross-sectional content analysis study.

author_details.name: Rafter A
author_details.affiliation: School of Biological Sciences, Technological University Dublin, Grangegorman, Dublin, Ireland.; Trinity College Dublin, The University of Dublin, College Green, Dublin, Ireland.

author_details.name: Proctor ES

author_details.affiliation: School of Biological Sciences, Technological University Dublin, Grangegorman, Dublin, Ireland.

author_details.affiliation: Department of Quantitative Health Sciences, John A. Burns School of Medicine, University of Hawai'i, Honolulu, United States of America.; Nutrition Support Shared Resource, University of Hawai'i Cancer Center, Honolulu, United States of America.

abstract: Instagram is a social media platform commonly used by parents and caregivers to source complementary feeding advice, yet the reliability of the information provided is unknown. This study aimed to evaluate the quality and accuracy of complementary feeding information disseminated on Instagram, a global digital communication platform, and to assess its alignment with World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines. A cross-sectional content analysis study was conducted on Instagram in March 2025. 13 complementary feeding-related hashtags were used to identify relevant posts. Quality was evaluated using a modified version of the Principles for Health Information on Social Media (PRHISM) tool, which applied 11 relevant principles to evaluate the digital health content. Alignment with WHO recommendations for timing of introduction and food groups were used to assess accuracy. 650 Instagram posts were identified. Following screening, 302 posts were evaluated for quality and accuracy. Of the 103 posts that mentioned when to introduce complementary foods, 93.2% recommended introduction at 6 months, in line with WHO recommendations. Among the 268 posts addressing food types, 52.6% promoted consumption of all three WHO-recommended food groups. Overall, information quality was classified as mediocre according to the PRHISM criteria, with most posts (93.0%) scoring between 26 and 50 out of 100. The lowest scoring PRHISM domains were attribution, supplementary information, and the presentation of risks and benefits. Instagram, a widely accessed channel for health advice, provides complementary feeding information that varies in accuracy and is of mediocre quality. While accurate for the timing of complementary food introduction when compared to WHO guidelines, the accuracy of the types of foods recommended, and the quality of information provided, are more variable. These findings underscore the need for digital health policies, content regulation, and professional engagement to improve the quality and accuracy of nutrition-related information on social media and promote equitable, evidence-based caregiving practices.

title: Regenerating forests around Taï National Park sustain biodiversity despite constrained floristic recovery.

author_details.name: Houphouët ADL
author_details.affiliation: Université Jean Lorougnon Guédé, Unité de Formation et de Recherche en Environnement, Daloa, Côte d' Ivoire.

author_details.name: Sangne YC
author_details.affiliation: Université Jean Lorougnon Guédé, Unité de Formation et de Recherche en Environnement, Daloa, Côte d' Ivoire.

author_details.name: Diarrassouba A
author_details.affiliation: Office Ivoirien des Parcs et Réserves, Soubré, Côte d' Ivoire.

author_details.name: Ehouman E
author_details.affiliation: CIRAD, Forêts et Sociétés, Montpellier, France.; Forêts et Sociétés, Univ Montpellier, CIRAD, Montpellier, France.

author_details.name: Hérault B
author_details.affiliation: CIRAD, Forêts et Sociétés, Montpellier, France.; Forêts et Sociétés, Univ Montpellier, CIRAD, Montpellier, France.

abstract: Extensive deforestation and disturbance have reshaped forest landscapes in West Africa, including areas surrounding Taï National Park, the largest remaining block of Upper Guinean rainforest. Although many degraded areas are currently undergoing regeneration, the capacity of these secondary forests to recover their biodiversity attributes remains insufficiently assessed within this park. This study quantifies the multidimensional restoration of biodiversity across 125 secondary forest plots and 15 primary forest plots representing 14,731 inventoried individuals in four sectors of the park. Using a Bayesian modelling framework, we estimate recovery trajectories of Shannon diversity, floristic composition, functional traits (wood density, leaf mass per area, seed mass), and conservation-relevant species. The different biodiversity attributes recovered at contrasting rates. Diversity was restored more rapidly (λ = 0.06) than floristic composition (λ = 0.03), and these recovery rates varied according to environmental variables. Among these, the presence of remnant trees showed the highest median on diversity (0.53 ± 0.61) and floristic composition (0.37 ± 0.17), promoting the rapid recovery of both attributes, followed by prior land use, particularly cocoa farming which also positively influenced the recovery of alpha diversity (λ = 0.03) and floristic composition (λ = 0.02). Regarding functional traits, they displayed contrasting dynamics: leaf mass per area (LMA) and seed mass recovered rapidly along successional gradients, whereas wood density followed a more gradual recovery trajectory. From a conservation perspective, although the proportion of IUCN Red List species remained stable along the successional gradient, old-growth indicator species were significantly more abundant in primary forests. To ensure the long-term conservation of biodiversity, protecting both primary and regenerating forests is essential to preserve the ecological resilience of this park.

abstract: Purpose The abductor hallucis (ABDH) contributes to foot function and mobility, which can influence quality of life, making accurate assessment of muscle volume important. While magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is often considered to be the reference standard of medical imaging, ultrasound (US) provides a cost-effective, rapid and dynamic way of assessing muscle size and function. This study aimed to evaluate the criterion validity and intrarater reliability of US-derived ABDH muscle volume measurements compared with MRI when image analysis was performed by assessors with limited experience. Methods Us And MRI were employed to measure the right and left ABDH muscle volume involving 22 participants (females = 12; males = 10). Following exclusions, 37 feet were available for analysis, with 36 complete MRI-US observations. Muscle volume of the ABDH was calculated across the muscle belly every 0.5 cm both manually by utilizing a truncated cone (TC) formula and with a semi-automated tool in the OsiriX (OX) software. Intrarater reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), standard error of measurement (SEm), and minimal detectable change (MDC). Criterion validity was evaluated using Pearson correlations, Bland-Altman analyses, and two one-sided tests (TOST) with a determined ±10% equivalence margin. Results Side-specific intrarater reliability was high across methods (ICC(3,1) = 0.932-0.997), with SEm values of 0.251-0.709 cm³ and relative MDC values of 4.48%-12.95%. Very strong associations were observed among methods (r = 0.906-0.995). Bland-Altman limits-of-agreement half-widths were 6.52%-9.84% for MRI-MRI and 17.86%-27.35% for MRI-US comparisons. All three method comparisons met the ± 10% equivalence criterion. Conclusion US-derived ABDH volume measurements demonstrated high intrarater reliability and statistical equivalence to MRI within the ± 10% margin. Although MRI-US comparisons showed greater individual-level variability than MRI-MRI comparisons, US may provide a practical alternative for assessing ABDH muscle volume when MRI is impractical.

abstract: Background Research-creation is a methodological orientation that integrates creative and artistic processes with scholarly inquiry, positioning creative practice as a primary mode of knowledge generation. Originating largely within the arts and humanities in Canada, research-creation has increasingly appeared in health sciences contexts, including rehabilitation, mental health, health professions education, and community health research. However, no review has systematically mapped how research-creation is defined, conceptualized, or applied within health sciences scholarship, and significant ambiguity persists regarding the forms of data it generates, how those data are analyzed, and how creative outputs function within empirical research processes. Objectives This scoping review aims to map how research-creation is defined and conceptualized in health sciences literature; identify the purposes for which it is used and the health-related contexts in which it appears; describe the theories, methodological approaches, and creative methods employed; and examine what forms of health-related data are generated, how they are analyzed, and how knowledge is mobilized. Eligibility criteria Sources were included if they explicitly used the term "research-creation" (or its hyphenated and slash variants) to describe their method, approach, or project; focused on health, illness, care, healthcare systems, rehabilitation, mental health, public or community health, or health-related training; and generated empirical or experiential material analyzed or discussed in relation to health. No language limits were applied. Sources of evidence A systematic search of 22 article databases was conducted from inception to Aug 2026. Grey literature searches included EBSCO Open Dissertations, and ProQuest Dissertations and Theses. Reference lists of included studies will be hand-searched. Charting methods Data will be extracted independently by two reviewers using four structured charting tables capturing study characteristics, population, concept, and context. An expanded extraction framework was developed to accommodate the distinctive methodological features of research-creation, including creative processes, citational lineages, creative outputs, and forms of health-related data generated. Data will be analyzed using inductive qualitative content analysis. Extraction tools will be piloted on a subset of five included studies. Results The search identified 842 sources, with 577 remaining after duplicate removal. Title and abstract screening, full-text screening, and data extraction are currently underway. Conclusions This scoping review will provide the first systematic mapping of research-creation within health sciences research and training. Findings may strengthen interdisciplinary dialogue between arts, social sciences, and health disciplines; support methodological transparency for researchers employing creative inquiry; and serve as a resource for researchers, trainees, practitioners, and supervisors seeking to understand how research-creation contributes to health-related knowledge production.

abstract: Background Perioperative electronic health record (EHR) datasets are increasingly used to study postoperative morbidity, although database-recorded adverse-event indicators may not correspond to standardized complication endpoints. We characterized these indicators after adult abdominal surgery in MOVER EPIC and examined associations with routinely available perioperative variables. Methods This retrospective cohort study identified adult abdominal surgical encounters from 2017-2022 through procedure-name screening and case-level deduplication. The primary outcome was a broad composite of EHR-captured postoperative adverse-event indicators recorded within the indexed perioperative encounter. The secondary outcome was a narrower composite of severe EHR-captured adverse-event indicators. Multivariable logistic regression was performed in the primary complete-case cohort, adjusting for age, sex group, ASA physical status, procedure group, and operating-room duration. Sensitivity analyses included ASA-excluded models, alternative duration specifications, first-encounter restriction, penalized regression, patient-level cluster-robust inference, and inverse probability weighting (IPW). Results Among 5,679 encounters, the broad composite occurred in 166 (2.92%), the narrow severe composite in 95 (1.67%), and death in 23 (0.40%). In the primary complete-case cohort (n = 5,349; 147 broad events), ASA IV + was strongly associated with the broad composite compared with ASA III (adjusted OR 4.66, 95% CI 2.92-7.45; p < 0.001). Laparotomy/adhesiolysis was also associated with higher odds (OR 1.79, 95% CI 1.02-3.13; p = 0.041), whereas spline analyses suggested modest nonlinearity in the age association; operating-room duration was not independently associated. IPW estimates were materially similar, although the estimate for ASA I-II was less precise. Conclusions Clinician-assigned ASA physical status was the most consistent correlate of EHR-captured postoperative adverse-event indicators. ASA may reflect comorbidity burden and perceived perioperative vulnerability rather than directly measuring physiological reserve. These findings should not be interpreted as standardized 30-day postoperative complication risks.

abstract: Motivation Predicting drug sensitivity across diverse cancer samples is a fundamental challenge in personalized therapy and drug discovery. This task requires comprehensive characterization of both drug and cancer cell line features. Current approaches often fail to fully capture the complex structural characteristics and interactions of drug compounds and struggle to integrate multi-omics features derived from the same sample, limiting their feature representation capacity. Consequently, there is a need for modeling frameworks that can jointly model molecular structural features and multi-modal cellular contexts in a unified manner. Results We present SADRP, a structurally aware multi-modal framework for drug response prediction, designed to model complex molecular structures and multi-omics data. For drug representation, SADRP incorporates Shortest Distance Path (SDP) encoding and edge encoding to capture both topological relationships and bond-type chemical semantics. For cell line profiling, a multi-view interactive encoder integrates gene expression and DNA methylation, capturing cross-omics synergistic complementarity. SADRP consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, while also identifying potential therapeutic candidates and biomarkers, providing mechanistic insights and supporting applications in drug discovery and personalized medicine.

abstract: "Schrödinger's Cat" is a quantum mechanics thought experiment in which a cat in a sealed box is considered both alive and dead until the box is opened and its true state observed. In species threat assessments, the reverse paradox can apply. We present the case of the Erect-crested penguin (Eudyptes sclateri), one of four extant penguin species currently listed as "Endangered" on the IUCN Red List - a classification based largely on limited and inconsistent observations from the 1970s. Between 2022 and 2024, we surveyed the entire global population of Erect-crested penguins, a species confined to two subantarctic island groups in the New Zealand region: the Bounty Islands and the Antipodes Islands. Population estimates were derived from drone surveys of the entire global range, conducted primarily during the incubation stage, complemented with ground counts to establish nest-to-bird ratios and estimate breeding population size. On the small Bounty Islands (~50 ha), we found approximately 27,800 breeding pairs - nearly as many as on the Antipodes Islands (~29,800 pairs), which are roughly 40 times larger and historically considered the species' stronghold. Although data since the mid-1990s are sparse, available evidence suggests divergent population trajectories: the Bounty Islands population appears stable over at least the past 25 years, whereas the Antipodes Islands population has declined by more than 40% since the mid-1990s, a trajectory that approaches - and under precautionary assessment likely warrants - "Endangered" classification. These contrasting trajectories likely reflect fundamental differences between the two sites: on the Bounty Islands, birds have access to potentially more productive subtropical waters during the non-breeding season, while on the Antipodes Islands, Subantarctic skua predation on fragmenting colonies generates a self-reinforcing Allee effect and penguins face potentially less favourable oceanic conditions. Thus, like Schrödinger's cat, the Erect-crested penguin population occurs in two states - stable and moving towards extinction - which only became clear once the proverbial box was opened. This situation highlights the challenges of assessing extinction risk when a species comprises spatially segregated populations on distinct demographic trajectories. While the Antipodes population clearly warrants concern, the stability of the Bounty Islands population would likely reduce the species' global conservation status to "Vulnerable" under IUCN criteria. This creates both a communicative and conservation conundrum: the binary population trajectories - one stable, one declining - combine to improve the global threat category while effectively obscuring a severe and genuine population-level crisis, and may even weaken the fisheries protections critical to safeguarding what may be the species' last stable stronghold, the Bounty Islands.

abstract: Reliable early warning of infectious disease outbreaks remains a major challenge for surveillance systems, particularly for vector-borne pathogens whose transmission depends on interactions among hosts, vectors, and climate-sensitive environmental conditions. Data-driven forecasting offers a promising approach for predicting outbreak risk using surveillance and environmental data. This study develops a logit-weighted ensemble (LWE), a machine-learning framework that predicts outbreak occurrence 1-6 months ahead at the administrative unit-month scale using routinely available outbreak notifications and gridded climate data. Bluetongue virus (BTV), an arbovirus of ruminants transmitted by Culicoides biting midges, provides a well-characterised system in which transmission is strongly shaped by climate, making it a useful system for applying and testing this approach. The framework is evaluated using surveillance data collected between 2005 and 2024 from France, Greece, and Italy, selected for their long-running and high-quality outbreak surveillance records. Across all three countries, the LWE achieved the strongest and most stable predictive performance under a recall-focused evaluation that prioritises correctly identifying outbreak months. It outperformed or matched 14 benchmark models, with differences becoming more pronounced at longer lead times (month +3 onward), when predictions are more uncertain and outbreaks are relatively rare. Predictability varied across countries, with the highest performance in Greece, strong performance in France, and lower, more variable performance in Italy, reflecting differences in how consistently outbreaks occur and spread across regions. Overall, the results demonstrate that horizon-aware, climate-informed forecasting can reliably identify months and locations at elevated risk of outbreak occurrence up to six months in advance, supporting surveillance planning and preparedness across heterogeneous European settings. The ensemble framework provides a robust and portable strategy for outbreak prediction using routinely collected surveillance and environmental data.

abstract: Previous work demonstrated that ectodermal cells exhibit greater susceptibility to SARS-CoV-2 than endodermal and mesodermal cells, raising concerns about potential vulnerability of the developing nervous system. We hypothesized that neural stem cells (NSCs) derived from human ectoderm are susceptible to SARS-CoV-2. Using pseudotyped viral particles representing both wild-type and Omicron spike variants, we confirmed efficient transduction in NSCs, with Omicron variants preferentially utilizing endocytosis-mediated entry. Inhibition of endocytosis with filipin and OcTMAB significantly reduced viral entry across all spike variants. Low glycosylation levels on NSCs facilitated viral entry, and enzymatic removal of glycosylation increased their susceptibility. Ectodermal infection by SARS-CoV-2 raises serious concern for potential teratogenic effects on the nervous system, possibly causing latent or subclinical anomalies not immediately evident at birth. Therefore, future clinical studies and long-term surveillance of infants and children exposed in utero are necessary to investigate and identify potential neurodevelopmental deficits.

abstract: Background Each year, thousands of patients are diagnosed with gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding. Many of these patients undergo colonoscopy and are subsequently diagnosed with benign or malignant colorectal neoplasms. The aim of this study is to evaluate whether patients with cardiovascular comorbidities, many of whom are on anti-platelet or anticoagulation therapy, are more likely to be diagnosed with new benign or malignant colorectal neoplasms than patients without cardiovascular comorbidities. Methods From the 2007-2011 NIS, 802,080 primary lower GI bleed admissions (ICD-9) were identified; 283,925 had cardiovascular comorbidities. We compared patients with vs without these comorbidities for the primary outcome of new benign or malignant colorectal neoplasms. Weighted analyses accounting for the complex survey design were performed in SAS 9.4, with trends assessed using Cochran-Armitage tests and linear regression and associations with colorectal cancer stage evaluated by multinomial logistic regression (p ≤ 0.05). Results Between 2007-2011, the odds of malignant colorectal neoplasms increased between 49.9% and 65.3% for patients without cardiovascular comorbidities when presenting with a lower GI bleed, compared to those with cardiovascular comorbidities. Between 2007 and 2011, the most notable and statistically significant difference was observed in 2010, when patients with cardiovascular comorbidities had 10.5% higher odds of being diagnosed with benign colorectal neoplasms than those without cardiovascular comorbidities. Conclusion Patients presenting with a lower gastrointestinal bleed without cardiovascular comorbidities were significantly more likely to be diagnosed with malignant colorectal neoplasms than those with cardiovascular comorbidities.

abstract: The evolutionary origins of complex communication remain contentious, with social, ecological, and environmental factors proposed as selective drivers. The Social Complexity Hypothesis for Communicative Complexity (SCHCC) predicts that the cognitive demands of navigating socially intricate groups favour the evolution of complex communication. Although several studies provide support for the SCHCC, its empirical basis remains limited and inconsistent, as evidence is drawn predominantly from a small number of well-studied taxa (primarily primates), often neglects species' complete vocal repertoires, and employs inconsistent approaches for assessing social and vocal complexity. This narrow focus limits its generalisability across animals, underscoring the need to characterise the full communicative complexity of additional model species to expand its evolutionary relevance. Vultures, with their varied social structures, provide a unique system to test this hypothesis, yet foundational work on communication in this guild is limited. Here, we present the first quantitative analysis of the vocal repertoire of the critically endangered, highly social Rüppell's vulture, based on 2,500 calls recorded from two captive populations (35 individuals) across diverse social contexts. Using a fuzzy clustering approach, we reveal a repertoire far more complex than previously assumed, comprising multiple discrete and graded call types, with gradations likely conveying additional information. Calls serve diverse functions, including mediating parent-offspring interactions, manipulating conspecifics, and resolving conflicts. The Rüppell's vulture repertoire exceeds the average call repertoire size observed across birds and is likely an adaptation to this species' social life. Our results further establish vultures as a promising model for studying the vocal evolution and provide a framework for comparative analyses that can illuminate the selective pressures shaping complex communication.

abstract: Background High fasting plasma glucose (HFPG) is an established risk factor for breast cancer (BC). However, accurate and up-to-date estimates of the global burden of breast cancer attributable to high fasting plasma glucose (BC-HFPG) are scarce. This study aims to provide a comprehensive analysis of the burden of BC-HFPG using data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) database from 1990 to2023. Methods We performed a comprehensive descriptive analysis of the burden of female BC-HFPG based on the GBD 2023 database. The core metrics analyzed were the absolute number of death and disability-adjusted life years (DALY). To ensure comparability across populations with differing age structures, we also analyzed the age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR) and the age-standardized DALY rate (ASDR). The average annual percent change (AAPC) was used to further comprehensively describe the burden of disease and its changing trends. In addition to the retrospective analysis from 1990 to 2023, we used the Bayesian age-period-cohort (BAPC) model to generate predicted data on the burden of female BC-HFPG from 2024 to 2050. Results Female BC-HFPG accounted for 48,307 deaths and 1,406,186 DALYs globally in 2023. From 1990 to 2023, the global ASMR and ASDR of female BC-HFPG showed overall upward trends, with an average annual percentage change (AAPC) of 0.28% (95% CI: 0.18% to 0.38%) for ASMR and 0.44% (95% CI: 0.37% to 0.51%) for ASDR; the two rates increased from 0.92 and 26.22 per 100,000 in 1990 to 1.00 and 30.17 per 100,000 in 2023, respectively. The burden varied substantially across the 21 GBD regions and 204 countries and territories in 2023. In 2023, SDI was only weakly correlated with ASMR (Spearman ρ = 0.20, P = 0.004) and not significantly correlated with ASDR, and the burden peaked in low-middle SDI quintile countries. The BAPC model projected that the ASMR and ASDR of female BC-HFPG would continue to rise from 2024 to 2050. Conclusion The global burden of female BC-HFPG increased from 1990 to 2023 and is projected to continue rising through 2050, disproportionately affecting low- and low-middle SDI regions. These findings suggest that glycemic management and metabolic risk-factor control warrant consideration within comprehensive breast cancer prevention frameworks. However, because this is an ecological, population-level analysis, whether glucose lowering interventions can reduce breast cancer incidence remains to be established in prospective interventional studies. Our results may help prioritize regions and populations for future etiological and intervention research.

abstract: Basalt fiber, a natural and eco-friendly reinforcement, has demonstrated superior properties compared with conventional synthetic fibers. This study investigates the effect of ageing on the mechanical and vibrational properties of Basalt/Epoxy, Glass/Epoxy, and Basalt-Glass/Epoxy hybrid composites. Laminates were fabricated using vacuum bagging, ensuring uniform fiber-matrix volume fractions, and then exposed to ageing in seawater, tap water, and distilled water for a duration of 80 days. The moisture absorption pattern followed Fickian diffusion, with seawater exhibiting the highest diffusion coefficients owing to matrix breakdown and osmotic influences. Tensile tests demonstrated a decrease in failure stress and modulus for all materials after ageing, with Glass/Epoxy composites experiencing the most notable degradation despite absorbing less moisture, indicating a weakening of the fiber-matrix interfacial bond. The hybrid laminates exhibited moderate tensile and vibrational characteristics and maintained mechanical performance better in harsh environments. Free vibration tests showed that the natural frequency diminished as mass increased due to moisture absorption, while damping factors rose after ageing. Overall, the combination of basalt and glass fibers enhanced environmental resilience, indicating their suitability for structural applications under challenging conditions.

abstract: Background Sleep disturbances and oral health problems are both prevalent public health concerns with substantial impacts on quality of life and systemic health. However, population-based evidence examining the independent associations between multiple dimensions of oral health and multiple sleep outcomes remains limited. This study investigated the associations between oral health indicators and sleep disturbances among Canadian adults using nationally representative survey data. Methods We utilized data from adults aged 18 years and older who completed the 2017-2018 Canadian Community Health Survey (CCHS). Four oral health indicators were assessed: self-reported oral health, oral pain, bleeding gums, and dry mouth. Four sleep outcomes were examined: short sleep duration, insomnia symptoms, unrefreshing sleep, and difficulty staying awake. Multivariable logistic regression models were used, with progressive adjustment for sociodemographic factors, health status, and health behaviors. Results All four oral health indicators were significantly associated with most sleep outcomes in the full adjusted model. For short sleep duration, the strongest association was observed for poor oral health (AOR: 1.623). For insomnia symptoms, dry mouth (AOR: 1.904) and oral pain (AOR: 1.826) exhibited the strongest associations. For unrefreshing sleep, oral pain (AOR: 1.937) and dry mouth (AOR: 1.808) were associated with higher odds of reporting unrefreshing sleep. For difficulty staying awake, dry mouth (AOR: 1.720) and oral pain (AOR: 1.701) showed the strongest associations. Conclusion Oral health problems are associated with multiple dimensions of sleep disturbance. These findings highlight the need for integrated care and complementary screening between dental and sleep medicine.

abstract: The successor representation (SR) is a reinforcement learning strategy which has been suggested to underlie nuanced forms of habitual behavior, rendering it a candidate mechanism for mental health conditions thought to involve habitual control, such as addiction. However, paradigms used to assess habits in humans cannot detect SR use. Together with the fact that they are usually conducted in disorder-irrelevant contexts, this may explain why the evidence for a hypothesized shift from goal-directed to habitual behavior in addiction is inconsistent. Here, we tested whether individuals with high-risk (n = 260) compared to low-risk drinking behavior (n = 260) rely more on SR or a rigid goal-based dimension-reduced SR variant, particularly in alcohol-related contexts. An online multi-stage decision-making task performed in either a virtual bar or apartment context allowed us to dissociate (red)SR from model-based and model-free learning strategies by testing how well participants adapted their choices to different types of distal changes in the environment. Findings suggest that a particular type of SR, namely a (reduced) random-policy SR-like strategy, contributes to human behavior, but that high-risk drinkers do not differ from low-risk drinkers in their use of this strategy. Instead, both groups seem to rely less on what is likely a (reduced) random-policy SR strategy in alcohol-related contexts - and instead more on model-free control. Results suggest that the use of an adaptive, resource-efficient decision-making strategy is selectively downregulated in substance-related contexts. This study highlights the importance of considering contextual modulation and nuanced decision strategies in understanding habitual and goal-directed behavior in mental health conditions such as addiction.

abstract: Postpartum anemia affects approximately 75% of women in India. We conducted this implementation research (IR) related to the use of ferric carboxymaltose (FCM) intravenous (IV) iron as part of a trial in anemic postpartum women. The aim of the IR study was to understand potential facilitators and barriers to implementation of single-dose FCM IV iron. This is a mixed-methods study in three secondary-level healthcare facilities in Belagavi, India, designed to explore selected Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research constructs and Proctor's framework elements. Quantitative data were gathered via surveys of postpartum women who received IV FCM (n = 308) and from healthcare workers and administrators (n = 16). Qualitative data included in-depth interviews with 15 women who received IV FCM, 15 family members of women, and 15 healthcare workers and administrators. Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively, and interview transcripts underwent directed content analysis to augment survey findings. Nearly all women believed IV iron made anemia symptoms better, 76% felt the single infusion process was very easy, 58% completely agreed to receive treatment again, and 69% were very likely to recommend treatment to family or friends. Family members were supportive of women receiving FCM. Health workers felt that single dose FCM had comparative advantages over oral iron; however, 4/10 health workers said giving FCM IV iron is harder than oral iron because of the patient monitoring involved and 8/16 health workers and administrators felt there were not enough trained staff to provide the service. Fewer than half of health workers and administrators (7/16) believed their hospital had enough resources to implement IV FCM infusions, and 9/16 said getting the necessary supplies would be a moderate or major barrier. In conclusion, the intervention was well accepted by women and their families and feasible for government health staff within the context of a trial. Future scale up of FCM IV iron would require out-of-pocket costs to be covered by public funding, staff training on the intervention, and strategies, such as dedicated staff or task shifting, to allow for monitoring during and after the infusion.

abstract: The increasing use of accelerometers as digital health technologies in clinical trials and clinical care is driving the need for data processing to meet medical standards. The aim of this study was to create and test a modular pipeline for the pre-processing of high-resolution accelerometry that assures the quality, transparency and traceability of digital measures from sensor-level data. The objective is for the pipeline to be a foundational layer in the development, implementation and comparison of measures. The study developed the open GENEAcore package to meet the requirements of regulators, verifying the engineering implementation and analytically validating outputs against reference datasets. Early stages included the optimisation of calibration and non-wear detection. Data-driven detection of behavioural transitions was then validated to give direct bout outputs without the need to identify rules for epoch aggregation and interruptions. The utility for measure development was shown by comparing two algorithms for the characterisation of activity intensity in both the epoch and bout paradigms. Non-wear was detected with a balanced accuracy of 92.3% and the commonly used 13mg acceleration standard deviation threshold was empirically validated with a sensitivity analysis for the first time. The detection of transitions proved reliable with 99% detected, on average, within 2 seconds of their occurrence to give a mean expected event duration of 68.6s from a log-normal distribution. The different activity intensity algorithms were more than 99% concordant during movement but their outputs diverged in low movement conditions. Importantly, variable duration bouts created 31% higher daily activity durations compared to 1-second epochs. This evaluation of pre-processing steps has confirmed the attention to detail required to create robust and reproducible results for later clinical validation where small changes in an algorithm or its implementation may have clinically meaningful consequences.

abstract: Synaptic remodeling in emotional circuits contributes to the development of stress-related emotional disorders. However, such remodeling generally exhibits considerable heterogeneity across specific neuronal populations and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identified C1ql2 as a key molecular regulator that governs projection-specific synaptic vulnerability within basolateral amygdala (BLA). Transcriptional profiling revealed that C1ql2 expression is enriched in BLA neurons projecting to ventral hippocampus (BLA →vHPC PNs), but not in those projecting to nucleus accumbens (NAc), and is significantly down-regulated following chronic social defeat stress (CSDS). Gain- and loss-of-function manipulations demonstrated that C1ql2 regulates stress-induced neuronal remodeling in BLA →vHPC PNs, including dendritic hypertrophy, synaptic outgrowth, and enhanced glutamatergic transmission, thereby shaping susceptibility to anxiety-like behavior. We further found that CSDS-induced C1ql2 loss impairs microglial engulfment of BLA →vHPC PNs synapses, leading to aberrant synaptic accumulation. Our findings establish C1ql2-mediated neuron-microglia cross talk that critically regulates circuit-specific synaptic pathophysiology in stress-related disorders.

abstract: A new frontier in condensed matter physics is to stack atomically thin layered materials with different properties and create intriguing phenomena which do not exist in any of the constituent layers. Transition metal dichalcogenide 4Hb-TaS 2, with an alternating stacking of a spin liquid candidate 1T-TaS 2 and a superconductor 1H-TaS 2 , is a natural heterostructure for such a purpose. Recently, rare phenomena were indeed observed, including chiral superconductivity, two-component nematic superconductivity, topological surface superconductivity, and enigmatic magnetic memory. A widely proposed starting point to understand such a mysterious heterostructure requires strong electronic correlation, presumably provided by 1T-TaS 2 layers with a narrow flat band near the Fermi level (E F ). Here, by using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, we reveal the theoretically expected flat band near E F in the energy-momentum space. However, this flat band only exists on the 1T-TaS 2 terminated surface layer with broken translational symmetry, but not on the 1T-TaS 2 subsurface layers buried in the bulk. These results directly challenge the foundation of the current theoretical paradigm. On the 1T-TaS 2 terminated surface layer, we further revealed a pseudogap and an anomalous doping effect. These phenomena and the dichotomy between surface and bulk layers also shed light on the unusual coexistence of distinct electronic orders in this mysterious heterostructure.

abstract: T cell activation relies on the coordinated integration of T cell receptor (TCR) and cosignaling pathways, yet how these signals are physically organized remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that CD28 co-stimulation is driven by a condensation mechanism in which the CD28 intracellular domain (ICD) forms signaling condensates with the Src-family kinase Lck. Ligand engagement promotes CD28 ICD accessibility and triggers rapid CD28/Lck condensation, enhancing CD28 phosphorylation, cytoskeletal polarization, and cytokine production. The downstream effectors of CD28, including PI3K and GRB2, can also be recruited into the CD28-Lck condensates in our reconstituted system. We further identify PD-1 as a graded regulator of this process: Monophosphorylated PD-1 is recruited into CD28/Lck condensates, whereas diphosphorylated PD-1 competitively binds the CD28 ICD and dissolves these assemblies. CD28 and PD-1 ICDs also undergo condensation directly, revealing a dynamic and compositionally heterogeneous signaling system. Guided by this competitive condensation mechanism, we engineer CD28 ICD mutants that preserve Lck condensation while resisting PD-1-mediated disruption. Incorporation of these condensation-selective mutants into Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) constructs confers resistance to inhibitory signaling and enhances antitumor efficacy in vivo. These findings establish condensation as a central organizing principle of CD28 costimulation and provide a biophysical framework for engineering more resilient therapeutic T cells.

abstract: The cell surface is a critical nexus in cellular communication and a rich landscape yielding the majority of current therapeutic targets, yet only a small fraction of cell surface proteins have been targeted therapeutically. The cell surface proteome (surfaceome) comprises only ~1% of the human proteome by mass, motivating enrichment strategies to detect surfaceome alterations in disease for drug target discovery. Developments in photocatalytic technology have revolutionized the study of protein neighborhoods around specific targets of interest, but photocatalysis has been underutilized for global surfaceome analysis. Here, we describe five distinct photocatalytic surfaceomics strategies, all without the need for cellular engineering, that apply the photocatalyst Eosin Y attached to different cell surface structures: direct glycan ligation, glycan attachment via two different lectins, membrane insertion, and free in extracellular space. We systematically compare these photocatalytic surfaceomics methods to each other as well as to three established chemical and enzymatic surfaceomics methods. We demonstrate that the different photocatalytic surfaceomics techniques achieve broadly similar canonical cell surface protein enrichment but show some important differences reflective of cell surface attachment mechanism. These mechanistically orthogonal surfaceomics techniques consistently identified numerous nonglycosylated proteins with high concordance, many of which represent an underappreciated class of noncanonical cell surface proteins lacking traditional cell surface protein features that may represent potential drug targets. This study substantially expands options for surfaceomics methods using photocatalytic proximity labeling.

abstract: Understanding how warming affects life-critical physiological processes is increasingly important as ocean temperatures rise at unprecedented rates. We study the stomatogastric system of the crab Cancer borealis . Movement depends on multiple temperature-sensitive processes, from motor pattern generation to neuromuscular transmission and contraction. Previous studies examined these levels separately and showed that warming increased pyloric rhythm frequency until the rhythm crashed at extreme temperatures. Here, we examined how the neuromuscular transform responds to this increase in motor neuron activity. We simultaneously recorded motor neuron activity, muscle fiber membrane potential, and contraction force. As temperature increased, the pyloric rhythm frequency increased, the excitatory junctional potential amplitudes remained constant, and muscle contraction diminished and failed. When muscles were stimulated at a fixed low frequency mimicking neuronal activity at cold temperatures, contraction decreased with acute warming. Increasing motor nerve stimulation frequency to mimic neuronal activity at warm temperatures partially rescued contraction. This shows that the temperature-dependent increase in neuronal firing provides partial compensation but is insufficient to prevent the loss of contraction at high temperatures. Because warming hyperpolarized muscle fibers, it moved the membrane potential further from the contraction threshold, and decreased synaptic integration, thus protecting against overexcitability. However, high-potassium-induced contractures revealed that the contractile machinery remained functional at high temperature, but the nerve-evoked depolarizations were apparently not large enough to cross the threshold for muscle contraction. Thus, a variety of temperature-dependent compensatory mechanisms overlap to extend the temperature range over which the neuromuscular system remains functional over a broad temperature range.

abstract: With more than one third of the human proteome being structurally disordered, intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) are key contributors to complex cellular functions, despite their highly dynamic conformational ensembles remaining elusive to conventional techniques in structural biology. Coarse-grained (CG) simulation methods thus serve as a gold standard to refine IDP ensembles. These methods, when relying on elastic network models or rigid body to sample secondary structure, are however inherently limited in their capability to model and sample transient secondary structure at a residue-level resolution as informed by experimental data. This fundamental limitation persists despite experimental evidence suggesting that transient structural propensities are a fundamental hallmark of IDP function. Through an artificial neural network capable of predicting backbone chemical shifts from C α -only protein conformations, we present a generalized framework which does not rely on dihedral parameterization to equip one bead-per-aminoacid CG force fields with the ability to sample functional elements of secondary structure. When applied on a large set of IDPs in isolation or condensates, our approach correctly recapitulates both local and global arrangements, yielding experimentally informed ensembles that can inform structure-mediated function and resolve force field limitations. This can yield a fruitful exploration of ensemble-to-function relationships in IDPs, allowing to explore phenomena such as secondary structure propensity and nucleation in condensates, conformationally selected binding motifs across disordered ensembles or conformational preferences of sequence-specific short-linear motifs.

abstract: Despite the long-held view of Mycobacterium tuberculosis ( Mtb ) as a genetically conserved pathogen, many genomic regions remain poorly resolved due to high sequence homology and repetitive content. Using complete genome assemblies generated from long-read sequencing of 151 globally representative clinical isolates, we comprehensively analyzed genome-wide patterns of genetic diversity and evolution across the Mtb genome. Our analysis uncovers pronounced diversity hotspots within paralogous regions (PRs) generated by recurrent gene conversion between homologous genes. In many cases, these hotspots exhibit more than an order of magnitude greater genetic diversity than the rest of the Mtb genome, which is otherwise characterized by remarkably low variation. Mutations within these regions display clustered substitution patterns, excess paralog-matching variants, and distinct mutational spectra consistent with ongoing gene conversion. Our analysis identifies over 300 individual gene conversion events (GCEs) distributed throughout the Mtb phylogeny. These GCEs occur predominantly within gene families associated with virulence and host-pathogen interactions, including the PE, PPE, and ESX families. Several of the most pronounced diversity hotspots occur in antigens encoded within PRs. Among these, the vaccine candidate PPE18 harbors mutations in validated epitope sequences and predicted alterations in HLA-II binding. Together, these findings demonstrate that gene conversion actively shapes antigenic and virulence-associated diversity in Mtb .

abstract: Harry Leonard Swinney passed away peacefully at his home in Austin, Texas, on July 13, 2026, at the age of 87. Harry was an exceptional experimental physicist, well-known for elegant studies of instabilities, nonlinear dynamics, chaos and pattern formation in a wide variety of fluid, chemical, and granular systems, work whose influence propagated into numerous scientific and engineering disciplines well beyond the particular problems that prompted it. The late Russell Donnelly of the University of Oregon used to say, "Harry is a prince"; Russ meant it, in the spirit of the tenth-century Persian poet Ferdowsi, as a compliment affirming the nobility, dignity, integrity, and grace with which Harry pursued his science and treated everyone he worked alongside.

abstract: Ticks, like Ixodes scapularis , can parasitize a diverse array of vertebrates, favoring natural hosts but feeding opportunistically on others. Natural hosts, as well as permissive hosts such as laboratory mice, tolerate repeated infestations, while many incidental hosts may acquire anti-tick immunity, as first described in guinea pigs. We show that tick-immune guinea pigs display altered dermal cytology and a distinct transcriptome, predominantly upregulating the IL36γ cytokine. Interference with IL36γ signaling, via gene knockdown, chemical inhibition, or its natural antagonist IL36RN, reversed anti-tick immunity in guinea pigs. Conversely, genome engineering to silence IL36RN in C3H mice, representing a permissive host, disrupted tick engorgement, interfering with the transmission of Lyme disease pathogens. These findings firmly establish IL36γ as a central mediator of protective anti-tick immunity involving I. scapularis in mammalian hosts and support future strategies to interfere with tick-transmitted infections.
